paper.title: SIGMA observations of the low mass X-ray binaries of the Galactic Bulge
paper.abstract: The soft gamma-ray telescope (35--1300 keV) SIGMA aboard the high energy GRANAT space observatory has been monitoring the Galactic Bulge region for more than 2000 h of effective time since March 1990. In the resulting average 35--75 keV image we detected ten sources at a level of > 5 standard deviations, 6 of which can be identified with low mass X-ray binaries (LMXB). Among them, one is the 1993 X-ray nova in Ophiuchus (GRS 1726-249), one is an X-ray pulsar (GX 1+4), two are associated with X-ray bursters (GX 354-0 and A 1742-294) and two with bursting X-ray binaries in the globular clusters Terzan 2 and Terzan 1. Their spectral and long term variability behavior as measured by SIGMA are presented and discussed.

paper.title: EXCESS workshop: Descriptions of rising low-energy spectra
authors: Vázquez de Sola Fernández, Francisco Andrés
paper.abstract: Many low-threshold experiments observe sharply rising event rates of yet unknown origins below a few hundred eV, and larger than expected from known backgrounds. Due to the significant impact of this excess on the dark matter or neutrino sensitivity of these experiments, a collective effort has been started to share the knowledge about the individual observations. For this, the EXCESS Workshop was initiated. In its first iteration in June 2021, ten rare event search collaborations contributed to this initiative via talks and discussions. The contributing collaborations were CONNIE, CRESST, DAMIC, EDELWEISS, MINER, NEWS-G, NUCLEUS, RICOCHET, SENSEI and SuperCDMS. They presented data about their observed energy spectra and known backgrounds together with details about the respective measurements. In this paper, we summarize the presented information and give a comprehensive overview of the similarities and differences between the distinct measurements. The provided data is furthermore publicly available on the workshop's data repository together with a plotting tool for visualization.
categories: Astrophysics - Instrumentation and Methods for Astrophysics

paper.title: The KM3NeT infrastructure: Status and first results
paper.abstract: KM3NeT is a research infrastructure in construction under the Mediterranean Sea. It hosts two large volume neutrino Cherenkov telescopes: ARCA at a depth of 3500 m, located offshore Sicily, and ORCA, 2500 m under the sea level, offshore the southern French coast. The two detectors share the same detection principle and technology and the same data acquisition design, the only difference being the geometrical arrangement of the optical sensors. This allows to span a wide range of neutrino energy and cover a large scientific program: The study of neutrino properties, first of all neutrino mass ordering, the identification and study of high energy neutrino astrophysical sources, indirect dark matter searches and core collapse supernovae detection.

paper.title: EUSO-SPB2: A sub-orbital cosmic ray and neutrino multi-messenger pathfinder observatory
paper.abstract: The next generation of ultra-high energy cosmic ray (UHECR) and very-high energy neutrino observatories will address the challenge of the extremely low fluxes of these particles at the highest energies. EUSO-SPB2 (Extreme Universe Space Observatory on a Super Pressure Balloon 2) is designed to prepare space missions to address this challenge. EUSO-SPB2 is equipped with 2 telescopes: the Fluorescence Telescope, which will point downwards and measure fluorescence emission from UHECR air showers with an energy above 2 EeV, and the Cherenkov Telescope (CT), which will point towards the Earth's limb and measure direct Cherenkov emission from cosmic rays with energies above 1 PeV verifying the technique. Pointed below the limb, the CT will search for Cherenkov emission produced by neutrino-sourced tau-lepton decays above 10 PeV energies and study backgrounds for such events. The EUSO-SPB2 mission will provide pioneering observations and technical milestones on the path towards a space-based multi-messenger observatory.
categories: Astrophysics - Instrumentation and Methods for Astrophysics

paper.title: Transport of Nitric Oxide in the Winter Mesosphere and Lower Thermosphere
paper.abstract: Nitric oxide (NO) plays key roles both in thermospheric energetics and upper-lower atmosphere coupling. However, mesospheric NO in the polar night region has often been underestimated in whole atmosphere models, and the exact causes are not well understood. Recent high-resolution (HR) WACCM-X simulations show significant increase in NO in the polar night, and our analysis reveals distinct differences in the vertical transport between the HR and coarse resolution (CR) simulations: The residual mean vertical wind in the mesosphere and lower thermosphere (MLT) region displays mesoscale flow channels that are strong and alternate between upward and downward directions in the former, with large net downward transport over the polar region. In the latter it is much weaker and even upward over large latitude ranges. Moreover, the resolved waves in the HR simulations induce downward eddy transport of NO in the MLT much stronger than the parameterized diffusion in CR simulations.

paper.title: Measuring the cosmic dipole with golden dark sirens in the era of next-generation ground-based gravitational wave detectors
paper.abstract: The tensions between cosmological parameter measurements from the early-universe and the late-universe datasets offer an exciting opportunity to explore new physics, if not accounted for unknown systematics. Apart from the well-known Hubble tension, a tension up to ~4.9σ in the cosmic dipole has also been reported. While the cosmic dipole is mainly induced by the observer's kinetic motion, an intrinsic dipole arising from the anisotropy of the universe could also play an import role. Such an intrinsic anisotropy can be a dark energy mimicker that causes the observed accelerating expansion of the universe. As a new and powerful tool, gravitational waves can serve as an independent probe to the cosmic dipole. A useful type of events to achieve this is the ``golden dark sirens'', which are near-by well-localized compact binary coalescences whose host galaxies can be identified directly due to precise localization. By forecasting golden dark sirens obtained from 10-year observations using different possible detector networks in the future, we find that the standard LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA detectors are not able to detect a meaningful amount of golden dark sirens, and hence next-generation ground-based detectors are essential to obtain a strong constraint on the cosmic dipole. In particular, we find that a three-detector network consisting of more than one next-generation detectors can yield a constraint on the cosmic dipole at an order of 10<SUP>-3</SUP> when jointly measured with H <SUB>0</SUB>. Moreover, a constraint on the cosmic dipole at an order of 10<SUP>-4</SUP> can be achieved when fixing H <SUB>0</SUB>.

summary.context_outlook: 当地宇宙计数观测给出的宇宙偶极显著超出CMB运动学偶极（类星体计数约4.9σ差异 [[Secrest+ 2021]]，超新星数据亦有约3.3σ迹象 [[Singal 2022]]）时，引力波被视为独立的各向同性检验探针。引力波宇宙学本身已从GW170817亮标准汽笛 [[Abbott+ 2017]] 发展到无需电磁对应体的暗汽笛群体统计测量 [[Abbott+ 2023]]，并有工作预测用ET/CE的并合事件计数 [[Mastrogiovanni+ 2023]] 或模拟亮汽笛网络 [[Cousins+ 2024]] 来测量宇宙偶极。本文指出这类分析隐含地把CMB静止系光度距离当成已知量，转而采用邻近、定位极佳且在局域区内只有一颗最亮星系的「金暗汽笛」——其宿主星系可由 [[Singer+ 2016]] 式的后续观测证认，此前已被用于预测H0精度 [[Gupta 2023]] ——首次把宇宙偶极与H0放在同一似然中联合拟合。展望来看，随着下一代探测器每年探测10^5–10^6个事件，暗汽笛分析中的选择效应、星系表完备性与宿主星系证认概率将取代统计误差成为主导系统项，而把金暗汽笛与CBC计数法、亮汽笛以及脉冲星计时阵列的运动学偶极测量联合，并纳入宿主星系本动速度 [[Nimonkar+ 2023]] 与完整的运动学效应理论框架 [[Cusin+ 2024]]，有望最终判定偶极张力究竟来自新物理还是计数方法的系统误差。

paper.title: The Length Sensing and Control of the Ground-based Laser Interferometric Gravitational Wave Detectors
paper.abstract: During the operation of ground-based laser interferometric gravitational wave detectors, the internal optical systems are subject to various noise disturbances, resulting in uncontrollable displacements. To enhance the sensitivity of the detectors and enable the detection of faint gravitational wave signals, it is imperative to employ a length sensing and control system. This system ensures that multiple optical cavities within the detector remain in resonance, thereby facilitating the design of gravitational wave signal readout schemes. Beginning with the configuration of laser interferometric gravitational wave detectors, this paper outlines the fundamental principles of length feedback control and parameter design criteria. Drawing on specific parameters of the Advanced LIGO, Advanced Virgo, and KAGRA control systems currently in operation, a detailed exposition is provided on the working principles and applications of length sensing and control systems in gravitational wave detectors.

paper.title: Euclid preparation: CXIII. Simulated galaxy catalogues for non-standard cosmological models
paper.abstract: Stage-IV galaxy surveys will provide the opportunity to test cosmological models and the underlying theory of gravity with unparal-leled precision. In this context, it is crucial for the Euclid mission to leverage its spectroscopic and photometric probes to systematically investigate and incorporate non-standard cosmological models, including modified gravity, alternative dark energy scenarios, massive neutrinos, and primordial non-Gaussianity. For this, we produce and release publicly simulated galaxy catalogues from a broad suite of non-standard cosmological simulations, which we processed through a model-independent analytical pipeline, making use of ROCKSTAR for halo identification, and a modified version of the SciPic library for the galaxy-halo connection using the halo occupation distribution framework. One of the goals of this paper is also to test the validity of the template-fitting method for galaxy clustering analyses, even in cases where the template significantly differ from data. For this purpose, we investigate the multipoles of the two-point correlation function in redshift space and VDG<SUB>∞</SUB>, a highly performant, state-of-the-art model for galaxy clustering. Across a wide range of models, the linear growth rate multiplied by the matter density within spheres of radius of 12 Mpc, fσ<SUB>12</SUB>, exhibits a notable robustness to the choice of cosmological template. Compared to previous works, our study extends this result to numerous scenarios with markedly distinct gravitational or dark energy dynamics. We find that the most of the scatter in cosmological parameter inference already appears when using the cosmological model of the simulations as templates. Using a `wrong' template can also introduce an additional scatter, although with smaller amplitude. Often, we find deviations much larger than error bars, meaning that the Gaussian approximation for the covariance might need to be further studied. Looking ahead, future cosmological investigations must broaden their scope to include a diverse array of non-standard theoretical frameworks extending beyond ΛCDM and rudimentary dynamic dark energy models.

paper.title: Searching for outbursts from symbiotic binaries in GOTO and ATLAS data
paper.abstract: Symbiotic binaries contain a white dwarf accreting material from a red giant star typically through a wind. We present the results of a search for outbursts from symbiotic binaries using photometric data obtained using the GOTO all-sky survey taken from 2023 onwards. After identifying ten candidate outbursting systems, we used ATLAS photometry to characterise their photometric behaviour before 2023, leaving five systems whose photometric behaviour was consistent with an outburst. The ATLAS data also provide colour information that gives insight into the nature of the outburst. The outburst from LMC N67 is the first reported Z And-type outburst from a symbiotic binary in the Large Magellanic Cloud. In OGLE SMC-LPV-4044 and HK Sco we found previously unreported outbursts. The ongoing outbursts of QW Sge and V4141 Sgr started in 2024 and have already been reported. By better identifying and characterising Z And-type outbursts from many systems, it will be possible to better understand the physics of these events, which are still not fully understood.

paper.title: Fast partial-sky spherical harmonic transforms
paper.abstract: Context. Our main motivations are the South Pole Observatory program targeting primordial gravitational waves from inflation and cosmic microwave background (CMB) lensing from South Pole Telescope, requiring high-resolution, numerically intensive work on small sky fractions. Aims. We aim to make significant improvements in the efficiency of general-purpose spherical harmonic transforms on limited regions of the sky. Methods. We extended the doubled Fourier sphere (DFS) method, which allowed it to handle more efficiently high numbers of locations on a region of the sphere. Results. We achieved speed-up factors ranging from 3 to 10 on the SPT-3G main field, along with a BICEP3 deep footprint and much more on smaller patches, at the same level of accuracy. Conclusions. Our algorithm allowed us to eliminate the usual disadvantages of arbitrary pixelisations in comparison to isolatitude pixelisations (or flat-sky approximations), making it ideal for ambitious workflows that require repeated spherical harmonic transforms on limited sky regions.

paper.title: A0538-66: A transient ultraluminous X-ray source with a relativistic outflow, 69 ms pulsations, and anomalous optical activity
paper.abstract: A0538--66 is a peculiar Be/X-ray binary in the Large Magellanic Cloud, hosting the fastest spinning neutron star of its class (~69 ms) and showing the brightest optical bursts of any system of this type. We report four XMM-Newton observations obtained near periastron in 2025, together with MAXI and REM monitoring, and a reanalysis of archival RXTE data. On 30 September 2025 the source reached L<SUB>X</SUB> ≈ 1.5 × 10<SUP>39</SUP> erg s<SUP>-1</SUP> (0.2--10 keV), the highest level since 1980, and in February, May, and August 2026, MAXI detected similarly bright outbursts. During the XMM-Newton observation taken on 30 September 2025, we detected the pulsations, measuring P<SUB>spin</SUB> = 69.25878(2) ms and Ṗ<SUB>spin</SUB> = 6.58(9) × 10<SUP>-10</SUP> s s<SUP>-1</SUP>; the pulsed fraction was low (≈3% in 1--10 keV), increased with energy, and the soft and hard pulse profiles were shifted by half a cycle. A new detection in RXTE data of 3 December 1998 gives a faster spin period of P = 68.88813(28) ms. The XMM-Newton/RGS spectra show emission lines from photoionised plasma at rest and blueshifted absorption lines that imply an outflow at ~0.12c. This indicates a highly super-Eddington accretion rate and an intrinsic L<SUB>X</SUB> ≈ 1.5 × 10<SUP>39</SUP> erg s<SUP>-1</SUP>, and it makes A0538--66 a transient ultra-luminous X-ray pulsar, a class of which only a few objects are known so far. Since 2023 the optical bursts observed by REM have become longer and brighter, resembling those of the 1980s, but most of them lack a luminous X-ray counterpart (L<SUB>X</SUB> > 10<SUP>37</SUP> erg s<SUP>-1</SUP>). We interpret these results in terms of a radiation pressure dominated accretion disc whose geometrically thick inner regions intermittently screen the innermost emitting regions.

paper.title: Radiation hydrodynamics of star-disc collisions: From system parameters to outflows and light curves
paper.abstract: Context. Quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) are nuclear transients that produce bright, repeating soft X-ray flares superimposed on quiescent emission. A promising interpretation is that they are powered by star-disc collisions, in which a star crosses an accretion disc around a supermassive black hole, drives shocks, and launches dense outflows from which radiation emerges. Aims. We present a systematic study of star-disc collisions, linking the physical parameters of the collision to the resulting outflows and emerging bolometric luminosities. Methods. We performed three-dimensional local radiation-hydrodynamic simulations, varying the disc surface density and vertical density profiles, stellar velocity and radius, and local collision angle. We focused on the regime in which the star remains unperturbed by the collision. Results. Variations of the stellar velocity and the accretion-disc surface density leave the bow-shock and outflow morphology largely unchanged. However, faster stars produce brighter flares, while denser discs mainly increase the flare duration. Increasing the stellar radius increases the momentum of the forward outflow and produces brighter and longer flares. More centrally concentrated discs yield brighter and shorter flares because radiation escapes more efficiently through the outer low-density layers. More oblique crossings reduce the momentum and luminosity asymmetry of two outflows and lengthen the flares. We provide empirical scalings for the peak luminosity and flare duration with the individual system parameters and apply them to GSN 069. The best candidate solutions favour a star with a radius ~R<SUB>⊙</SUB> on a retrograde orbit that collides with a dense post-stellar tidal disruption event (TDE) disc with a vertically concentrated density profile. Conclusions. Our findings suggest that specific combinations of system parameters can reproduce the characteristic flare amplitudes, durations, duty cycles, and `strong-weak' flare patterns observed in QPE sources.

paper.title: Evidence of suppressed nonthermal broadening in a flare ribbon from stereoscopic observations
paper.abstract: Context. Flare ribbons are footpoints of newly reconnected magnetic loops. They are commonly associated with strong plasma flows and a pronounced nonthermal broadening of transition-region lines resulting from impulsive energy deposition. However, the mechanism governing energy transport into flare ribbons remains uncertain, particularly under different magnetic field configurations. Aims. We aim to understand the energy deposition process at a flare ribbon located close to a sunspot by determining the physical nature of the small-scale downflows hosted by the ribbon. Methods. We studied small-scale downflows in a remote ribbon during the M7.7-class event on 30 September 2024 using coordinated observations from the Solar Dynamics Observatory, the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS), and Solar Orbiter. We used stereoscopic imaging from Solar Orbiter and IRIS to detect plane-of-sky motions on small scales (~200 km). We conducted spectroscopic analysis of IRIS Si IV profiles complemented by C II and Mg II diagnostics. Results. Apparent downflow speeds measured from Solar Orbiter imaging (limb view) are 85--130 km s<SUP>-1</SUP>, while IRIS images (disk view) reveal plane-of-sky speeds of 70--85 km s<SUP>-1</SUP>. In contrast, the IRIS Si IV profiles at the brightest ribbon pixels are well approximated by a single Gaussian, with minimal Doppler shifts and unexpectedly small nonthermal widths (~ 10 km s<SUP>-1</SUP>). Peak Si IV emission also coincides with a deeper Mg II central reversal, while the electron densities are one to two orders of magnitude higher than typical quiet-Sun values. Conclusions. The absence of significant line-of-sight velocity and nonthermal broadening differs from the typical behavior of flare ribbons. Our results are consistent with a scenario in which plasma motions are guided by highly inclined (nearly horizontal) magnetic fields in a chromospheric canopy and are not accompanied by strong turbulence or wave motions. This study suggests that flare ribbons can exhibit a wide diversity of lower-atmospheric responses and emphasizes the critical role of magnetic field geometry.

paper.title: Characterizing NGC 6383: Study of fundamental properties, pre-main sequence stars, mass segregation, and age using Gaia DR3 and 2MASS
paper.abstract: Context. This study is focused on the young open cluster NGC 6383, situated in the Carina-Sagittarius arm within the Sh 2-012 star-formation region. Previous studies have provided estimates of the distance, age, and structural properties of the cluster. The presence of pre-main sequence (PMS) and low-mass stars, combined with Gaia DR3 and 2MASS data, makes NGC 6383 a compelling target for a refined characterization. Aims. We aim to identify cluster members, determine the fundamental parameters, assess the mass segregation, and derive the age and distance of NGC 6383 from Gaia DR3 and 2MASS data. Methods. We employed Bayesian analysis and machine-learning techniques, including Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (HDBSCAN) for member identification, PyMC for the Bayesian modeling, the Sagitta neural network for the identification and age estimation of PMS stars, and ASteCA for the isochrone fitting. Results. We identified 321 likely cluster candidates, with <inline-formula>p̃ > 0.5<mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mover><mml:mi>p</mml:mi><mml:mo>~</mml:mo></mml:mover></mml:mrow><mml:mo>></mml:mo><mml:mn>0.5</mml:mn></mml:math></inline-formula>, and used a reference sample of 254 sources with <inline-formula>p̃ >= 0.6<mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mover><mml:mi>p</mml:mi><mml:mo>~</mml:mo></mml:mover></mml:mrow><mml:mo>>=</mml:mo><mml:mn>0.6</mml:mn></mml:math></inline-formula> to derive the cluster parameters. The mode cluster age is ≃3.5 Myr, with log(age yr<SUP>-1</SUP>) = 6.55<SUB>-0.20</SUB><SUP>+0.40</SUP> (with the uncertainty dominated by PMS model systematics that act toward older ages) and the distance is 1.11 ± 0.06 kpc. The core radius is 1.96<SUB>-0.16</SUB><SUP>+0.19</SUP> arcmin (0.63<SUB>-0.05</SUB><SUP>+0.06</SUP> pc); the King outer radius, measured on the only extraction that reaches a fitted background annulus beyond the cluster (70 arcmin), is 54<SUB>-11</SUB><SUP>+7</SUP> arcmin (17.4<SUB>-3.6</SUB><SUP>+2.3</SUP> pc). This posterior is truncated from above by the adopted prior bound, so we report it as a model-dependent outer scale. Given the cluster's dynamical youth (age ≃0.14 of the half-mass relaxation time), the mass segregation of binary stars, which is conditional on the membership of the outer low-mass candidates, is consistent with a primordial or near-primordial origin. The color-magnitude diagram shows a well-defined main sequence and a population of PMS stars, whose bulk lies between the 1.6 and 6.3 Myr isochrones, consistent with a recent, possibly extended star formation episode. The software used for this investigation has been released with the paper. Conclusions. Combining machine-learning membership with Bayesian parameter estimation, our analysis provides updated parameters for NGC 6383, an apparent age spread consistent with recent, possibly extended star formation, and a segregation pattern. This pattern, which is conditional on the membership of the outer low-mass candidates, is consistent with a primordial origin or with rapid early dynamical segregation (near-primordial).

paper.title: The link between extreme particle acceleration and X-ray binary jets
paper.abstract: Context. The detection of multi-TeV radiation from several black-hole X-ray binaries has positioned the source class as a promising candidate to explain the observed cosmic-ray flux in the PeV energy range. Aims. We aim to determine what distinguishes the systems detected in the gamma-ray range from the rest of the population. Methods. We built on existing catalogues of black-hole X-ray binaries by including information on the radio and gamma-ray emission from these systems. We then compared the > 100 TeV gamma-ray luminosity to different properties of the systems and evaluated the strength of the (rank) correlation (τ<SUB>K</SUB>) between them. Additionally, we compared the distribution of sources in our sample with the positions of unassociated gamma-ray sources in the 1LHAASO and 1HGPS catalogues to determine whether a correlation exists between them. Results. We find no correlation with the mass of the compact object, the companion mass, or the inclination angle. Instead, we find evidence for a strong correlation (τ<SUB>K</SUB> > 0.5) between the gamma-ray luminosity and the radio and hard-state X-ray luminosities in our sample. The limited number of gamma-ray detections means that this correlation cannot yet be claimed as statistically significant. We find indications that a high (≳20%) duty cycle (defined as the fraction of time spent in outburst) might be a requirement for > 100 TeV gamma-ray loudness. We find significant evidence (> 3σ) that black-hole X-ray binaries are located near unassociated gamma-ray sources in the region of the sky not covered by LHAASO. This evidence is only significant when comparing to X-ray binaries detected in the radio band, not for the sample without a reported radio detection. Conclusions. We conclude that radio-bright black-hole X-ray binaries with a high duty cycle are more likely to be detected as gamma-ray sources than sources that are not detected in the radio band or those with low duty cycles. This result suggests that the particles responsible for the gamma-ray emission are associated with the jets, either accelerated within them or via their interaction with their surroundings.

paper.title: Interpretation of fast radio bursts from CHIME/FRB baseband data
paper.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are radio pulses that originate from cosmological distances. Thousands of FRB sources have been discovered, but their origins remain unknown. Analyses of the energy function and redshift evolution of the volumetric event rate could provide crucial insights into FRB progenitors. In this paper, we used the V<SUB>max</SUB> method to analyse the FRB energy functions and volumetric event rate evolution based on CHIME/FRB BaseCat 1 data. The baseband data provide improved fluence and bandwidth measurements compared to Catalogue 1, enabling a more robust analysis of FRB energy and population studies. The V<SUB>max</SUB> method allows us to investigate volumetric event rate evolution as a function of redshift without any prior assumptions. The selection functions for baseband data were derived to re-weight the samples when calculating the number density. We observe Schechter-like shapes for the energy function with a unified slope index of γ ∈ [ - 1.8, -1.6]. Neither the cosmic star formation rate density (SFRD) nor the cosmic stellar-mass density scenario can be ruled out. We further discuss the scenario that FRBs are primarily produced from systems that evolve with a delay relative to SFRD. The rate evolution trend suggests a scenario of a delayed model with a delay time τ ≈ 4.66 Gyr, hinting at delayed core-collapse supernovae or compact binary mergers. Our work highlights the importance of baseband data, and the BaseCat 2 data are required to explore FRB populations and rate evolution.

paper.title: Isochrones in primordial magnetic field evolution
paper.abstract: Context. In the early Universe, a primordial magnetic field undergoes a turbulent decay while its length scale increases due to an inverse cascade. The size of the largest processed eddy scales with the Alfvén speed and grows with time. In a diagram of Alfvén speed versus length scale, all possible solutions must lie on a line through the origin, with a slope proportional to the inverse of the present time. In principle, however, such lines can also be defined for earlier times. Aims. The lines for earlier times form isochrones that might be observationally accessible, for example, through the magnetically driven stochastic gravitational wave background. However, the position and slope of these isochrones is sensitive to the zeropoint of the time. We show that for any initial magnetic field, a proper time can be determined such that the resulting isochrones at early times are nearly parallel to those at late times, that is, they have the same slope. Methods. We used two-dimensional numerical simulations of decaying magnetohydrodynamic turbulence and varied the initial position of the peak in the magnetic energy spectrum. In this case, the evolution is governed by the conservation of anastrophy. Results. A fit to the Alfvén time yielded an accurate estimate of the factor by which the decay time is longer than the Alfvén time, while the offset in the fit provided an estimate of the proper time that needs to be added to the nominal time since the beginning of each simulation. We also found that an initial velocity field with a realistic strength produced a straighter track from the beginning. Conclusions. The magnetic field parameters lie on universal isochrones even for early times. They provide a testable framework for magnetic fields generated at times as early as the end of inflation, starting with the time of reheating.

paper.title: Unveiling the hot interstellar medium in nearby galaxies with eROSITA
paper.abstract: Context. Diffuse X-ray emission in galaxies arises from both stellar-feedback-heated gas and unresolved compact sources. Previous studies mainly focused on the integrated X-ray luminosity, leaving the thermal component, especially in low star formation rate (SFR) galaxies, largely unexplored. Aims. We aim to characterize the diffuse X-ray emission of nearby galaxies over a wide range of SFRs and to test how the X-ray luminosities L<SUB>X</SUB> scale with star formation in a blind volume-limited sample. Methods. We analyzed data of the four eROSITA/Spectrum-Roentgen-Gamma all-sky surveys (eRASS:4) for 140 galaxies within 25 Mpc drawn from the Updated Nearby Galaxy Catalog and cross-matched with HECATEv2. Early-type galaxies were treated separately, while the star-forming galaxies were divided by specific SFR (sSFR) into low-, medium-, and high-sSFR subsamples. We extracted spectra of the integrated emission and modeled them with thermal plasma and power law components. For each subsample, we stacked the spectra and derived total and thermal-component X-ray luminosities. We then fitted relations for the star-forming galaxies. Results. The stacked spectra show a systematic change with sSFR: High-sSFR galaxies exhibit a pronounced soft thermal component, whereas low-sSFR and early-type galaxies are increasingly dominated by the harder nonthermal continuum. For the total 0.5--8 keV luminosity, we find log L<SUB>X</SUB> ~ 39.5 + 0.9 logSFR, with an intrinsic scatter of ~0.9 dex. For the 0.5--2 keV luminosity of the thermal component, we find log L<SUB>X</SUB> ~ 38.7 + 1.1 logSFR, with a smaller intrinsic scatter of ~0.7 dex. Conclusions. The X-ray luminosity of the thermal component remains well correlated with the SFR down to ~10<SUP>-5</SUP> M<SUB>⊙</SUB> yr<SUP>-1</SUP> and is consistent with previous relations for star-forming galaxies, while the total L<SUB>X</SUB> - SFR relation is flatter and more scattered. This result suggests that at low SFR, the total X-ray output is likely dominated by a small number of unresolved X-ray binaries, whereas the thermal X-ray luminosity remains a robust tracer of stellar-feedback-related X-ray emission.

paper.title: Euclid preparation: CXIV. Review of forecast constraints on dark energy and modified gravity
paper.abstract: The Euclid mission has been designed to provide, as one of its main deliverables, information on the nature of the gravitational interaction, which determines the expansion of the Universe and the formation of structures. Thus, Euclid has the potential to test deviations from general relativity that will allow us to shed light on long-lasting problems in the standard cosmological Λ cold dark matter model, ΛCDM. Euclid will mainly do this by using two complementary probes: weak gravitational lensing and galaxy clustering. In this paper we review pre-launch Euclid analyses for dark energy and modified gravity. These include forecast constraints with future Euclid data on cosmological parameters for different cosmological models, such as a time-varying dark energy component, phenomenological modifications of the perturbation sector and specific modified gravity models, with further extensions that include neutrino physics and the coupling to the electromagnetic sector through the fine-structure constant. We review the study of the impact of non-linear clustering methods on beyond-ΛCDM constraints with Euclid. This is of fundamental importance to efficiently predict the large-scale clustering of matter and dark matter haloes, given that we will have access to a wealth of information on scales beyond the linear regime. We inspect the extension of theoretical predictions for observable quantities in alternative cosmologies to ΛCDM at fully non-linear scales by means of N-body simulations. We discuss the impact of relativistic corrections in extended cosmological models. Overall, this review highlights the significant potential of the Euclid mission to tightly constrain parameters of dark energy and modified gravity models, or perhaps to detect possible signatures of a ΛCDM failure.

paper.title: Rotating models of very massive close binary stars at solar metallicity: Evolution and remnant masses
paper.abstract: To investigate the evolution of massive close binary systems at solar metallicity, we utilized the Modules for Experiments in Stellar Astrophysics (MESA) numerical code to compute a grid of 2880 detailed evolutionary models. These models consist of rotating stars with initial masses between 100 and 250 M<SUB>⊙</SUB> and initial orbital periods of three to ten days. We find that, with the exception of a small fraction of systems in contact on the zero-age main sequence (ZAMS), the binaries with standard stellar wind mass-loss rates reach core collapse without undergoing mass transfer. The primary stars remain relatively compact as their radii do not exceed ≈20 R<SUB>⊙</SUB>. The evolution is dominated by extreme stellar wind mass loss, enhanced by rapid rotation driven by tidal synchronization. As surface hydrogen is heavily depleted during the main sequence, the stars transition into the optically thick Wolf--Rayet wind regime, ultimately shedding 90% to 95% of their initial mass. Consequently, increasing the initial stellar mass does not yield more massive remnants; all resulting black holes (BHs) fall within a narrow range of 7--14 M<SUB>⊙</SUB>. This severe mass loss causes significant orbital widening, ensuring that the resulting double BH systems will not merge within a Hubble time. We conclude that presented evolutionary models with standard stellar wind mass-loss rates result in BHs less massive than ≈15 M<SUB>⊙</SUB> in very wide configurations. We also show that if mass-loss rates are scaled down by a factor of two or more, the same initial binary configurations can form (sometimes via mass transfer) significantly closer double BHs with masses exceeding 50 M<SUB>⊙</SUB> -- this matches the upper range of LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) observations. Corresponding maximum stellar radii were restricted to ≈25 R<SUB>⊙</SUB> and ≈65 R<SUB>⊙</SUB> for wind mass-loss reductions of 50% and 10%, respectively. Although excluded from our standard wind models, secondary-to-BH mass transfer or a common envelope phase becomes viable when assuming reduced mass-loss rates. These binary interactions would substantially tighten the orbit, potentially producing double BH binaries close enough to merge within a Hubble time.

paper.title: Two successive solar energetic electron events on 24 December 2022
paper.abstract: Aims. We investigated two successive solar energetic electron (SEE) events observed by Solar Orbiter, associated with the same active region and separated by ~25 minutes, on December 24, 2022. Methods. We performed the forward fitting to in situ temporal profiles to derive the solar injection profiles of SEEs, and utilized the extended pan-spectrum (EPS) fitting method to self-consistently determine the shape of SEE energy spectra. Then we examined the temporal relationship between SEE solar injections and candidate solar flares and/or coronal jets. Results. After considering the effects of interplanetary propagation and instrumental response, we found that the SEE #1 (#2) event can be formed by three (two) solar injections that dominate, respectively, at ≲22 keV, 22--290 keV, and 290--746 keV (at ≲26 keV and 26--185 keV). In both events, the low-energy SEE injection starts earlier, peaks earlier and lasts longer as the electron energy decreases, producing a very hard power-law energy spectrum. The high-energy injection is roughly independent of energy in its timing, with a short duration of ~3--6 minutes and a soft energy spectrum, which coincides with a B-C class flare, HXR burst, and coronal jet. The #1 event shows another, middle-energy injection with the start-time (duration) getting earlier (longer) but the peak-time growing earlier and then later as the electron energy decreases, and with a hard energy spectrum. Conclusions. In both SEE events, the low-energy injection likely comes from a progressive acceleration process occurring high in the corona, while the high-energy injection can arise from an instantaneous acceleration of the lower-energy electrons, accompanied by an HXR burst and/or coronal jet. In the #1 event, the middle-energy injection can result from an additional process, leading to a much more efficient acceleration at ≳25 keV. Thus, successive SEE events may form through very dynamic and complex processes.

paper.title: Synchronized disturbances detected by COSMIC satellites, GNSS and geomagnetic observatories in the band of Pc5: a case study of the 2022 Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai eruption
paper.abstract: The cataclysmic submarine eruption of Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai (HTHH) on 15 January 2022 launched a global cascade of atmospheric acoustic-gravity waves, driving a profound electrodynamic coupling across the lithosphere-atmosphere--ionosphere (LAI) system. To characterize the vertical structure of energy transfer from the HTHH eruption, electron-density profiles from the COSMIC-2 radio occultation constellation were analyzed in combination with regional GNSS-TEC measurements and ground-based magnetometer records. Following the HTHH eruption, intense ultra-low-frequency (ULF) Pc5 geomagnetic pulsation emerged with a dominant spectral signature characteristic of fundamental atmospheric acoustic resonance. Notably, our multi-instrument analysis demonstrates that these ground-based magnetic oscillations are synchronized with ionospheric disturbances in the same range of Pc5, captured simultaneously across near-field GNSS-TEC measurements and COSMIC-2 topside electron-density profiles. Such temporal synchronization provides evidence for a rapid, vertical atmospheric-ionospheric resonance established immediately following the eruption. Furthermore, applying a Short-Time Average/Long-Time Average (STA/LTA) algorithm, the detected horizontal wave propagation velocities (311--322 m/s) are shown to match the fundamental atmospheric Lamb wave mode. Crucially, spatiotemporal cross-validation shows that COSMIC-2 and epicentral GNSS observations captured an instantaneous, localized topside plasma response (04:15--04:45 UT) that strictly preceded the horizontal Lamb wave advection. These findings confirm that the immediate geospace response was driven by a vertical troposphere-thermosphere acoustic resonance cavity generating localized E×B plasma drifts, establishing COSMIC-2 as a critical diagnostic tool for space weather monitoring over expansive, instrument-sparse oceanic domains.

paper.title: Evolution-aware temporal modelling of magnetic complexity for multi-horizon M/X-class solar flare prediction
paper.abstract: Solar flare prediction is a rare-event forecasting problem governed by nonlinear, time-dependent magnetic evolution in solar active regions. This study presents an evolution-aware framework for multi-horizon prediction of M- and X-class flares using Space-weather HMI Active Region Patch magnetic parameters, engineered temporal differences, and GOES-derived flare-history features. Active regions are represented as chronological sequences and evaluated using long short-term memory, bidirectional long short-term memory, decomposition-based recurrent networks, Transformer models, a physics-regularised decomposition model, and probability ensembles. Forecast horizons of 3, 24, and 72 h are assessed using chronological training, validation, and test splits. Probability thresholds are selected from validation data only. To address methodological robustness, the revised evaluation includes static LR/MLP/SVM baselines, feature-group ablations, moving-average kernel sensitivity, learning-curve inspection, dropout sensitivity, bootstrap confidence intervals, blocked temporal cross-validation, and McNemar tests. The validation-selected 3 h family meta-average ensemble achieved a test true skill statistic of 0.753. The tuned bidirectional recurrent model achieved 0.481 at 24 h, while the simple probability-average ensemble achieved 0.594 at 72 h. Static baselines showed that final pre-prediction states are highly competitive, especially at 24 h, but temporal/evolution-aware models improved TSS at 3 h and 72 h. Feature ablations further showed that the dominant predictive signal is horizon-dependent: recent GOES flare-history memory is strongest at short horizons, while SHARP magnetic-state variables remain central at 72 h. The results provide a cautious, leakage-conscious evaluation framework for operational space-weather applications and identify where temporal modelling adds value beyond static active-region classification.

paper.title: GWTC-4.0: Searches for Gravitational-wave Lensing Signatures
authors: van den Brand, J. F. J.
paper.abstract: Gravitational waves can be gravitationally lensed by massive objects along their path. Depending on the lens mass and the lens--source geometry, this can lead to the observation of a single distorted signal, multiple repeated events, or a mixture of both. We present the results for gravitational-wave lensing searches on the data from the first part of the fourth LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA observing run (O4a). We search for strongly lensed events in the newly acquired data by (1) searching for an overall phase shift present in an image formed at a saddle point of the lens potential, (2) looking for pairs of detected candidates with consistent frequency evolution, and (3) identifying subthreshold counterpart candidates to the detected signals. Beyond strong lensing, we also look for lensing-induced distortions in all detected signals using an isolated point-mass model. We do not find evidence for strongly lensed gravitational-wave signals and use this result to constrain the rate of detectable strongly lensed events and the merger rate density of binary black holes at high redshift. In the search for single distorted lensed signals, we find one outlier: GW231123_135430, for which we report more detailed investigations. While this event is interesting, the associated waveform uncertainties make its interpretation complicated, and future observations of the populations of binary black holes and of gravitational lenses will help determine the probability that this event could be lensed.

paper.title: Multispacecraft Constrained Modeling of Solar Energetic Particle Transport across Different Heliocentric Radii and Heliolongitudes
paper.abstract: Multispacecraft observations of solar energetic particles (SEPs) across diverse heliocentric radii and longitudes enable us to disentangle radial and longitudinal SEP transport effects from variable interplanetary magnetic connectivity. We analyze four SEP events jointly detected by different combinations of Parker Solar Probe (PSP), Solar Orbiter, STEREO-A, and the Solar and Heliospheric Observatory, covering heliocentric distances of 0.42--1 au and distinct longitudinal positions. We compare observed 13--23 MeV proton flux time series with 18 MeV predictions from a fully three-dimensional focused transport model with an ideal Parker spiral magnetic field, which self-consistently simulates SEP propagation at the exact radial and longitudinal spacecraft sampling locations. The model incorporates key physical processes governing SEP transport: field-aligned streaming, pitch-angle scattering, cross-field diffusion, solar wind advection, magnetic focusing, and adiabatic cooling. We adopt event-specific transport parameters, with parallel mean free paths of 0.2--0.7 au and perpendicular-to-parallel diffusion ratios of 2%--10%. Observations show that SEP onset timing, rise duration, and peak flux are jointly modulated by heliocentric distance, longitudinal separation, and magnetic connectivity. Our simulations well reproduce the overall temporal evolution and reservoir-like decay signatures across all multispacecraft events, though noticeable discrepancies remain in the early rise and near-peak phases. These results provide empirical constraints on critical SEP transport parameters, advancing our understanding of SEP acceleration, propagation, and diffusion mechanisms, and offer valuable insights for practical space weather forecasting.

paper.title: Constraints on the r-process Delay Time from Dwarf Spheroidal Galaxies
authors: de los Reyes, Mithi A. C.
paper.abstract: The ancient stellar populations and simple structure of the local dwarf spheroidal galaxies (dSphs) make them excellent laboratories for studying the chemical evolution of the early Universe. In this paper, we fit one-zone galactic chemical evolution models to C, Mg, Si, Ca, Fe, Sr, Y, Ba, and Eu abundances in the dSphs Sculptor and Draco. By including the s- and r-processes in our model, we are able to place constraints on the timescale of r-process enrichment in these dSphs. We find that neutron star mergers cannot be the only source of the r-process in Sculptor and Draco, and that a prompt r-process source is required to explain the observed stellar abundances. When neutron star mergers are the only source of the r-process in our models, their minimum delay time must be just 14--16 Myr. The neutron-capture abundances in Sculptor and Draco can also be fit by models with a longer neutron star merger minimum delay time combined with a prompt r-process source that operates on the same timescale as massive star evolution, such as magnetorotational supernovae. Additionally, the Sr and Y abundances in the dSphs set limits on the Sr and Y yields per r-process event. We find that theoretical r-process yields overestimate Sr and Y production by a factor of up to 100.

paper.title: Exploring Magnetic Reconnection in a Sub-A-class Microflare Using Data-constrained Numerical Simulation and Multi-instrument Observations
paper.abstract: Solar flares are intermittent events that convert free magnetic energy into heat and kinetic energy of charged particles, along with a rearrangement of magnetic field lines (MFLs) through magnetic reconnection. This work investigates an active-region sub-A-class microflare detected by the Solar X-ray Monitor on board Chandrayaan-2. The MFL topology, its evolution, and the associated magnetic reconnection in the flaring region are investigated. The coronal magnetic field is constructed using the nonlinear force-free field (NLFFF) extrapolation model, indicating the presence of a magnetic flux rope (MFR) at the flaring location. Notably, this MFR exhibits regions of high magnetic field gradient and a nonuniform distribution of twist along its axis. Furthermore, the dynamics of the MFR is explored using a three-dimensional data-constrained magnetohydrodynamics simulation performed using the EULAG-MHD code. The simulation shows overall untangling of the MFLs that constitute the MFR, along with changes in their connectivity, which suggests underlying magnetic reconnection. Further, a few representative MFLs belonging to the MFR over a given time span are advected with the plasma flow to maintain their identity. These field lines show a change in connectivity, and such reconnections can contribute to the unfurling of the MFR. The overall scenario is generally consistent with the concept of braiding reconnection in an MFR.

summary.highlight: 把 Chandrayaan-2 XSM 探测到的亚A级微耀斑与 NLFFF 外推和三维数据约束 MHD 模拟结合起来，直接追踪磁流绳内磁力线的解缠与连接性改变，为磁流绳内部的编织重联（braiding reconnection）提供了微观证据；同时揭示该磁流绳沿轴扭转不均匀、并存在高磁场梯度区。
summary.authors_en: Simrat Kaur, Ramit Bhattacharyya, Satyam Agarwal et al.
summary.context_outlook: 太阳耀斑释放自由磁能的过程长期被归因于磁重联，而小尺度微耀斑因能量低、时标短，其磁流绳结构与重联几何以往多靠成像观测间接推断，难以对三维磁场演化施加直接约束。本文沿用了“先用非线性无力场外推重建耀斑前磁拓扑、再用数据约束 MHD 模拟追踪其演化”的技术路线，但把研究对象下探到亚 A 级微耀斑，并以 Chandrayaan-2 太阳X射线监测器的能谱信息作为约束条件。模拟结果显示磁流绳的磁力线整体解缠、连接性发生改变，支持了磁流绳内部编织重联的图像，也提示沿轴扭转不均匀与强磁场梯度区可能是重联优先发生的部位。随着多视角、高分辨率 X 射线与极紫外观测的积累，这类数据约束模拟有望把微耀斑的统计研究与单个事件的精细拓扑诊断衔接起来，并进一步检验编织重联在纳耀斑加热中的作用。

decision.reason: 对单一亚A级微耀斑应用已有NLFFF外推与MHD模拟方法，获得磁流绳编织重联的常规个案证据，属增量性工作，未达到显著改变科学认识的门槛。

paper.title: Eight New Ultramassive Black Hole Masses Confirm Best Correlation with Galaxy Core Sizes
paper.abstract: We analyze black hole (BH) scaling relations at the high-mass end, focusing in particular on the regime of ultramassive black holes, M<SUB>BH</SUB> > 10<SUP>10</SUP> M<SUB>⊙</SUB> (UMBHs). Building on the new dynamical BH mass measurements presented in our companion paper for a sample of 16 brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs), including eight newly identified UMBHs based on triaxial Schwarzschild models, we investigate the implications of these measurements for BH scaling relations. This first sample of triaxial BH mass determinations increases the number of known UMBHs by a factor of 2 and dramatically increases the constraints for BH mass scaling relations at the high-mass end. We find that BCGs are outliers in the canonical M<SUB>BH</SUB> ∝ σ<SUP>4-5</SUP> relation, while the size of their depleted cores---the central light-deficient region---offers a tighter correlation with M<SUB>BH</SUB> with a scatter of 0.22 dex in this mass regime, confirming and extending earlier findings that core size provides a robust proxy at the high-mass end. Our measurements smoothly join the trend already established in previous studies. This also holds for tight correlations between core size and sphere-of-influence radius and core size and core density, which, along with the correlation between M<SUB>BH</SUB> and core size, strongly support the BH binary model for the formation of the centers of the most massive galaxies, as the observed core sizes are inconsistent with gravitational-wave recoil predictions and the galaxies display central tangential orbital anisotropy expected from scouring.

paper.title: When the Shadow Meets Its Measure: Assessing the Feasibility of Submillimeter Black Hole Shadow Imaging in Megamaser-disk Active Galactic Nuclei
paper.abstract: Well-modeled water megamaser disks offer a path to black hole shadow (BHS) tests of strong-field gravity beyond Sgr A* and M87*: their very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) angular dynamics precisely constrains M<SUB>∙</SUB>/D, the maser-disk orientation, and the dynamical center within the maser reference frame, thereby predicting the fiducial Schwarzschild BHS angular size without an externally adopted distance. We assess 21 megamaser galaxies as BHS targets using published maser measurements to calculate BHS angular sizes and baseline requirements. We combine new Submillimeter Array (SMA) continuum observations with archival Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) and Very Large Array (VLA) measurements to estimate arcsecond-scale 230 GHz flux densities and identify the strongest nuclear-region sources for higher-resolution follow-up. We also estimate the maximum dust and extended-jet contributions, examine limited variability measurements, and, for the leading candidate NGC 4258, evaluate the astrometry required to detect a spin-dependent offset between the BHS center and the maser dynamical center. Only NGC 4258 has an adopted BHS angular size resolvable with an Earth--L2 baseline; the other adopted sizes require longer baselines, while an Earth--L4/L5 separation would be sufficient for all. Five sources reach S<SUB>230</SUB> ≳ 10 mJy. However, whether the observed 230 GHz emission arises on BHS scales and is sufficiently optically thin to reveal a BHS remains unknown throughout the sample. NGC 4258's submillimeter excess is consistent with a thin disk transitioning to an advection-dominated flow; its spin-offset test remains infeasible with present maser astrometry.

paper.title: Different Origins for the Line-emitting and Photospheric Components in Tidal Disruption Events: A Case for ASASSN-14ae
paper.abstract: Tidal disruption events (TDEs) are believed to launch outflows that play a crucial role in producing optical emission lines. In this study, we investigate emission properties expected within the wind-driven outflow framework, in which an outflow is continuously injected from the central engine. We perform radiative transfer calculations to compute synthetic line properties and apply the model to the optical TDE ASASSN-14ae. We find that a two-component structure with a high density contrast, consisting of an optically thick inner layer and an optically thin outer layer, is required to simultaneously reproduce the observed photospheric and Hα properties. The optically thin component exhibits a power-law temporal evolution in the mass-outflow rate and kinetic power, with the total ejected mass of ~0.25 M<SUB>⊙</SUB>, indicating that it might originate in a super-Eddington accretion-disk-driven outflow. The optically thick component is responsible for the photospheric emission, and we argue that this component is more plausibly interpreted as a quasi-hydrostatic envelope rather than an outflow. Interestingly, the kinetic power of the optically thin component and the bolometric luminosity originating from the optically thick component are comparable, and they share the same temporal evolution. This finding indicates that these two components are energetically linked through an equipartition process---pointing to a scenario in which the accretion energy is first converted to the kinetic energy of the outflow, and then this energy is dissipated to the envelope through the outflow--envelope interaction before it emerges from the surface of the envelope.

summary.title_zh: 潮汐瓦解事件中线发射成分与光球成分的不同起源：以ASASSN-14ae为例
summary.tldr: 用辐射转移计算模拟连续注入的星风外流并应用于光学TDE ASASSN-14ae，发现必须引入“光学厚内层+光学薄外层”的高密度对比双成分结构，才能同时再现光球连续谱与Hα谱线。
summary.highlight: 把TDE的“外流”拆成起源不同的两个物理组分：光学薄外流以幂律演化、总抛射质量约0.25 M⊙，符合超Eddington吸积盘驱动；光学厚成分更像准静态包层。更关键的是二者动能功率与辐射光度相当且同步演化，暗示吸积能量先转为外流动能、再经外流-包层相互作用耗散为辐射的能量均分图景。
summary.authors_en: Takifuji, Hare, Keiichi Maeda
summary.context_outlook: TDE的光学发射线长期被归因于中心引擎持续注入的外流/星风，这一图像可追溯到 [[Rees 1988]] 提出的吸积-外流基本框架；而 ASASSN-14ae 作为近邻、谱线明亮的典型事件，其光球辐射与宽Hα一直是检验外流模型的试金石 [[Holoien+ 2014]]。以往工作多倾向用单一外流成分同时拟合连续谱与谱线，本文的辐射转移计算表明这并不足够，只有引入高密度对比的双成分结构才能自洽解释观测。由此，“TDE外流”被拆分为物理起源不同的两部分：光学薄部分的质量损失率与动能功率呈幂律演化、总质量约0.25 M⊙，指向超Eddington吸积盘驱动外流；光学厚部分则更可能是准静态包层而非外流。展望未来，这种“外流+包层”的双成分图像有望推广到更多TDE样本，并推动把能量均分与外流-包层相互作用纳入自洽的流体+辐射转移模拟，与紫外、偏振及长期多波段监测结合，厘清吸积能量在动能与辐射之间的分配机制。

paper.title: The Deep Newtonian Regime in Late-time Blast Waves: Inevitable Transition and Distinct Flux Signatures
paper.abstract: In many astrophysical transients, outflows drive shocks into the ambient medium, accelerating electrons to nonthermal energy distributions that produce broadband synchrotron emission. At late times, even initially collimated relativistic jets evolve into quasi-spherical Newtonian blast waves. As the shock decelerates, the post-shock internal energy per particle decreases; below a critical velocity <inline-formula> <mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>β</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>DN</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>≈</mml:mo><mml:mn>0.2</mml:mn></mml:math> </inline-formula>, only a fraction ξ<SUB>e</SUB> < 1 of electrons are accelerated to relativistic energies, defining the deep Newtonian (DN) regime. We develop a unified analytic framework for synchrotron emission in this phase, applicable to both single-velocity and stratified ejecta. For gamma-ray burst afterglows in a uniform medium, the DN transition occurs at <inline-formula> <mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>t</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>DN</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>≈</mml:mo><mml:mn>3.7</mml:mn><mml:mspace></mml:mspace><mml:msubsup><mml:mrow><mml:mi>E</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>51</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn><mml:mo>/</mml:mo><mml:mn>3</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msubsup><mml:msubsup><mml:mrow><mml:mi>n</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>0</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn><mml:mo>/</mml:mo><mml:mn>3</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msubsup></mml:math> </inline-formula> yr, yielding a shallower decay by δα = 6(p - 2)/5 relative to standard Newtonian predictions. For kilonova remnants (E<SUB>0</SUB> = 10<SUP>50.5</SUP> erg, M<SUB>ej</SUB> = 0.1 M<SUB>⊙</SUB>), the DN phase begins prior to deceleration; neglecting it underestimates radio flux by factors of ~3--5 during coasting and even more thereafter. Magnetar-boosted remnants (E ~ 10<SUP>52</SUP> erg) should reach ~ 10 -- 100 μJy at 3 GHz at ~ 40Mpc, though limits on GW170817 already disfavor a long-lived millisecond magnetar. In core-collapse supernovae in a wind medium (ρ ∝ r<SUP>-k</SUP>), the peak luminosity remains constant during coasting, while ν<SUB>pk</SUB> ∝ t<SUP>-1</SUP>; for SN 2023ixf, we find k = 1.29 ± 0.14. The DN spectral energy distribution typically satisfies ν<SUB>m</SUB> < ν<SUB>sa</SUB> < ν<SUB>c</SUB>, peaking at sub-GHz frequencies where LOFAR and SKA-low are most sensitive. Even nondetections place robust constraints on ambient density and outflow energetics.

summary.context_outlook: 长期以来，晚期爆炸波常被直接外推为标准牛顿绝热球状爆炸波，深牛顿区（β<0.2、只有比例 ξ_e 的电子被加速到相对论能量）要么被忽略，要么只作零散处理，因而晚期低频光变的推断一直带有系统性偏差。本文把这一转变纳入统一的解析框架，同时覆盖单一速度与分层抛射物，明确给出均匀介质下 GRB 余辉的转折时标、千新星遗迹在减速前就进入深牛顿区的事实（忽略它将低估射电通量 3–5 倍以上），以及风介质超新星在滑行阶段峰值光度不变而 ν_pk∝t^(−1) 的行为，并用 SN 2023ixf 反演出 k≈1.29。对 GW170817 的限制也顺势强化了对长寿毫秒磁星的排除，同时说明磁星增能遗迹在 ~40 Mpc 处仍可给出 10–100 μJy 量级信号。展望未来，随着 LOFAR 与 SKA-low 在亚 GHz 打开窗口，深牛顿区将从“晚期细节”变成由低频段反演外流能量与环境密度的主要工具，而非探测同样能给出有力约束。

paper.title: Tentative Excess Dispersion Measures toward DESI Galaxy Groups from Localized Fast Radio Bursts
paper.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) provide sensitive probes of ionized baryons through their dispersion measures (DMs). In this work, we test whether localized FRB sight lines intersecting foreground galaxy groups exhibit a measurable excess in cosmic DM relative to clean nonintersecting sight lines. We crossmatch 117 localized FRBs with measured DMs and host redshifts against a foreground group catalog from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. Within the catalog footprint and at z<SUB>host</SUB> < 0.5, we identify 23 sight lines intersecting foreground groups and 18 clean nonintersecting sight lines for the main comparison. A joint fit to this sample gives a positive offset of <inline-formula> <mml:math><mml:mn>143</mml:mn><mml:mo>.</mml:mo><mml:msubsup><mml:mrow><mml:mn>3</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mn>53.0</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>+</mml:mo><mml:mn>53.2</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msubsup><mml:mspace></mml:mspace><mml:mi>pc</mml:mi><mml:mspace></mml:mspace><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi>cm</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mn>3</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup></mml:math> </inline-formula> in the inferred cosmic DM, DM<SUB>cosmic</SUB>, for the group-intersecting sight lines relative to the nonintersecting control sample. A template fit for the foreground halos gives <inline-formula> <mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>A</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>halo</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mn>0.3</mml:mn><mml:msubsup><mml:mrow><mml:mn>4</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mn>0.50</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>+</mml:mo><mml:mn>0.51</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msubsup></mml:math> </inline-formula>, with a positive posterior median but a weakly constrained detailed halo contribution. A mock forecast within the DESI footprint indicates that larger samples of localized FRBs would improve the foreground halo-template constraint.

paper.title: Coronal Green-line Emission during a Solar Prominence Eruption: Spectroscopic Evidence of Its Correspondence with the Extreme-Ultraviolet Late Phase
paper.abstract: We report spectroscopic observations during a prominence eruption on 2025 October 9 from the Sun's west limb, associated with an M2.0 flare that commenced at 12:11 UT. The event was captured in sit-and-stare mode by the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) on board Aditya-L1, providing continuous observations of the Fe XIV 5303 Å coronal green line. The spatially averaged green-line emission exhibits a clear correspondence with the EUV late-phase (ELP) emission observed in multiple Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO)/Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) channels. In particular, an enhanced 5303 Å emission peak at 15:24 UT coincides with secondary peaks in the AIA 211, 171, 193, and 335 Å passbands, occurring ~173 minutes after the X-ray peak. The 5303 Å line-width information provides important constraints on the mechanism responsible for the ELP. The line-width decreases progressively by about 28% toward the ELP peak, broadly consistent with the cooling of postflare coronal loops. This behavior suggests that the ELP is predominantly associated with plasma cooling, with relatively weak additional energy input from magnetic reconnection, which does not produce a significant enhancement in line widths. The estimated nonthermal velocity decreases from ~36 km s<SUP>-1</SUP> during the impulsive phase to ~21 km s<SUP>-1</SUP> during the gradual phase, indicating a reduction in turbulent plasma motions. And Doppler velocities evolve from predominantly positive values during the eruptive rise phase to negative values during the later gradual phase, implying upward and subsequent downward plasma motions. To our knowledge, this study provides the first space-based spectroscopic evidence linking coronal green-line emission with the ELP and its origin during a solar flare.

paper.title: Probing the High-energy Emission of the Very-high-energy-emitting Changing-look Blazar B2 1420+32
paper.abstract: We present a multiwavelength temporal and spectral study of the changing-look blazar B2 1420+32 using Fermi Large Area Telescope, Swift X-Ray Telescope, and Swift UV Optical Telescope data from MJD 58818--60721. The source reached a peak 0.1--300 GeV photon flux of (4.62 ± 0.29) × 10<SUP>-6</SUP> ph cm<SUP>-2</SUP> s<SUP>-1</SUP> around MJD 60488, about 60 times the 4FGL-DR4 average, during which the photon index hardened to 2.19 ± 0.14; the flux--index evolution shows only weak evidence for global harder-when-brighter behaviour. The fractional variability is strongly energy dependent, largest in gamma rays, substantial in the optical/UV, and low in X-rays. Strong gamma ray--optical/UV correlations and a moderate gamma ray--X-ray correlation are observed. We identified five activity states for broadband spectral energy distribution (SED) modelling. Their X-ray spectra are described by a log-parabola, with significant negative curvature in four of the five states. The high-energy (X-ray and gamma-ray) components of their SED are modeled using synchrotron self-Compton (SSC), external Compton (EC), and SSC+EC scenarios. The SSC-only and EC-only models either require physically disfavoured parameters or fail to reproduce the very-high-energy (VHE) emission, whereas SSC+EC provides the most self-consistent description, with a seed-photon temperature of ~10<SUP>3</SUP> K favouring an infrared torus origin. The brighter states require larger bulk Lorentz factors and higher jet powers, while the magnetic field is comparable across most states but drops sharply in the VHE state. The break energy also changes significantly between outbursts, indicating that the spectral shape evolves between activity episodes. These results suggest that Doppler boosting and jet energetics set the activity level, and the break energy governs the spectral shape between outbursts.

paper.title: Radio and X-Ray Observations of the Transitional Supernova 2019yvr: Insights into the Progenitor Mass-loss History
paper.abstract: The final life stages of the massive star progenitors of stripped-envelope supernovae (SESNe) remain an open question, especially when it comes to the timing and magnitude of the progenitor stripping. Observing SESNe across the electromagnetic spectrum allows for the most direct constraints on mass loss in the final stages of progenitor evolution. In this work, we present radio (GMRT+VLA) and X-ray (Swift+Chandra) observations of SN 2019yvr obtained from 18 to 1784 days postexplosion. SN 2019yvr was a Type Ib supernova (SN Ib, with strong helium but little or no hydrogen ) that transitioned into a Type IIn supernova (SN IIn, with shock-driven hydrogen features from interaction with circumstellar material, CSM) at ~100 days postexplosion. The radio evolution is best fit by a synchrotron self-absorbed model with a ρ ∝ r<SUP>-1.54±0.31</SUP> CSM density profile, suggesting a decreasing mass-loss rate from the progenitor in the years leading up to the explosion. The radio-derived shock speed is high, more than 30,000 km s<SUP>-1</SUP> at early times, suggesting a compact progenitor star. The combined radio and X-ray data probe CSM that extends from 1.7 × 10<SUP>16</SUP> cm up to ~20 × 10<SUP>16</SUP> cm and was created by mass loss from ~(1-3) × 10<SUP>-5</SUP> M<SUB>⊙</SUB> yr<SUP>-1</SUP> (assuming a CSM speed of 100 km s<SUP>-1</SUP>). The combined dataset rules out any dramatic jump in CSM density (which was seen in the optical analog SN 2014C) associated with the emergence of optical hydrogen emission lines. We place SN 2019yvr in context with similar transitional SNe and discuss implications for the progenitor.

paper.title: EP J062132.0+623837: A Multiwavelength Study of a Changing-look Active Galactic Nucleus Discovered by Einstein Probe
paper.abstract: EP J062132.0+623837 is a new X-ray source identified in 14 day binned survey data from the Wide-field X-ray Telescope on board the Einstein Probe (EP). Subsequent X-ray observations with the Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT) on board EP localized the source to the central region of the galaxy 2MASX J06213207+6238390 at z = 0.084. Here, we present a comprehensive analysis of the multiwavelength data for this object. During the FXT and Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory/X-Ray Telescope follow-up, the source remained X-ray active, with observed luminosities of (3--9) × 10<SUP>43</SUP> erg s<SUP>-1</SUP>, and its X-ray spectra were well described by power-law models with photon indices of Γ ~ 1.5. The optical spectrum of the host galaxy clearly reveals a broad-line active galactic nucleus (AGN) exhibiting significantly enhanced broad Balmer emission lines compared to an archival spectrum obtained 4 yr earlier, thereby marking a changing-look transition from Type 1.8 to Type 1.5. Furthermore, long-term optical and mid-IR light curves indicate that the nucleus underwent dramatic brightening around 2010 and has since shown substantial variability. Given the spatial coincidence and multiwavelength behavior, we identify EP J062132.0+623837 as a changing-look AGN, initially detected by EP and subsequently confirmed to exhibit large-amplitude variability across multiple bands. This case study demonstrates the great potential of wide-field time-domain X-ray surveys for discovering changing-look AGNs, paving a new avenue for their systematic identification as a powerful complement to ongoing optical surveys.

paper.title: A Generalized Template Matching Algorithm for Correcting Jitter Noise in Pulsar Timing
paper.abstract: Pulsar timing is a valuable source of high-precision astrophysical measurements that can be used to probe gravitational physics, including by detecting gravitational waves. An important factor limiting the precision of these measurements is pulse jitter; i.e., intrinsic, short-timescale variation in the amplitude and shape of pulses from a given pulsar. Because conventional pulse time-of-arrival (TOA) measurement relies on template matching, which assumes the average pulse shape is stable, such variation gives rise to jitter noise in TOA measurements. Here, we introduce a generalization of the template matching technique, making use of principal component analysis, which can account for variations in pulse shape. We compare this technique to other proposals for mitigating jitter noise in pulsar timing, paying particular attention to the possibility of corrections absorbing other astrophysical signals of interest, and we demonstrate its effectiveness using simulated data.

paper.title: Unveiling Multimessenger Emission from Hidden Cores of Microquasars
paper.abstract: Microquasars are radio-emitting X-ray binaries with relativistic jets and are established sources of ~100 TeV gamma rays, making them promising candidates for cosmic-ray acceleration. Motivated by recent detections of ~100 TeV photons from Cygnus X-1 and multi-PeV photons from Cygnus X-3, we employ the Astrophysical Multimessenger Emission Simulator (AMES) to model their multimessenger emission from radio to ultrahigh-energy gamma rays. Our modeling suggests that particle acceleration is extremely efficient in the jet region. The observed ≳0.1 PeV gamma rays can originate from either pγ or pp interactions, depending on the location and physical conditions of the emission region, while also reproducing the lower-energy spectra. These configurations yield observationally testable predictions. In the poorly constrained 0.1--10 TeV band, the models predict either a deep valley, a mild suppression, or a power-law spectrum. Additionally, models involving compact emission regions comparable to the orbital separation predict strong variability, while those invoking more extended and static external zones show more stable behavior. We also provide a possible qualitative explanation for the energy-dependent modulation patterns, relying primarily on changes in the Doppler factor and external γγ absorption. In particular, explaining the PeV emission from Cygnus X-3 favors a compact emission region, for which a magnetic field strength of order 10<SUP>2</SUP> G is required. Finally, after accounting for pion and muon cooling, the predicted neutrino flux is suppressed, implying that detection is more challenging than previously thought.

paper.title: FEADME: Fast Elliptical Accretion Disk Modeling Engine
paper.abstract: We present FEADME (Fast Elliptical Accretion Disk Modeling Engine), a GPU-accelerated Python framework for modeling broad Balmer-line emission with a relativistic elliptical accretion-disk formalism. Using JAX and NumPyro for differentiable forward modeling and Bayesian inference, FEADME enables reproducible analyses of large samples of disk-dominated emission-line profiles. We apply the framework to 237 double-peaked emitters (DPEs) and five tidal disruption events (TDEs) with disk-like Hα emission, fitting three model families per spectrum and selecting the preferred model using the widely applicable information criterion (WAIC). After posterior-quality filtering, the disk-bearing active galactic nuclei (AGNs) sample contains 165 sources, and the TDE sample contains 27 usable epochs. Within the common elliptical-disk model, AGNs occupy a broad, continuous distribution of disk geometries and kinematics summarized by five phenomenological Gaussian-mixture morphology bins, while TDE and AGN parameters overlap in radial scale, local broadening, and emissivity slope. The TDE epochs tend toward lower fitted eccentricities and broader nondisk Gaussian components. Comparison with published circular-disk plus spiral-arm fits to the same AGN spectra produces substantially different distributions of inclination, radii, emissivity slope, and local broadening, demonstrating that these inferred parameters depend strongly on the treatment of profile asymmetry. Most AGNs and TDEs favor models containing a disk and an additional broad-line component, suggesting that disk emission commonly coexists with more isotropic or wind-driven gas. These results demonstrate FEADME's utility for population studies and the importance of a consistent asymmetry prescription when comparing disk structures across accretion environments.

paper.title: Radio Follow-up of a Subthreshold Gamma-Ray Burst in the Sky Localization Area of GW241125
paper.abstract: Since the Fermi satellite's identification of a candidate γ-ray burst (GRB) temporally coincident with GW150914, several tentative, and often debated, associations between electromagnetic (EM) transients and gravitational-wave (GW) signals from binary black hole (BBH) mergers have been reported. One such event, GW241125, was identified during the fourth observing run (O4) of Advanced LIGO and found to be spatially (within the large GW localization uncertainty) and temporally coincident with a subthreshold GRB detected by the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory (Swift) Burst Alert Telescope (BAT) Gamma-Ray Urgent Archiver for Novel Opportunities (GUANO). Here, we present results from a radio follow-up campaign targeting the BAT-GUANO localization region, carried out with the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA). We also reanalyze Swift/X-Ray Telescope observations of the field, and combine these results with optical upper limits. Our analysis constrains the isotropic kinetic energy of a putative relativistic jet launched in the BBH merger to ≲3 × 10<SUP>50</SUP> erg for n<SUB>ISM</SUB> = 1.0 cm<SUP>-3</SUP>. We also discuss both the challenges and diagnostic power of radio follow-up in assessing candidate BBH--GRB associations, and present projections for analogous studies in the LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA observing run 5 (O5), and in the era of next-generation ground-based instrumentation. The enhanced sensitivity and localization capabilities of detector networks such as Cosmic Explorer and the Einstein Telescope, paired with the enhanced sensitivity of next-generation radio interferometers such as the next-generation VLA and the Square Kilometre Array, will significantly strengthen coordinated multimessenger follow-up of BBHs. These next-generation facilities are likely to probe whether BBHs host relativistic ejecta.

paper.title: Fast X-Ray Transients from Dense Circumstellar Material Shock Breakout and Cooling Emission
paper.abstract: In this Letter, we explore the soft X-ray shock breakout (SBO) and cooling emission of supernovae interacting with preexplosion dense circumstellar material (CSM) shells as a subclass of extragalactic fast X-ray transients. For geometrically thin CSM shells, we find that the SBO luminosities span a range of a few × 10<SUP>43</SUP>--10<SUP>45</SUP> erg s<SUP>-1</SUP>, with peak times typically ≲10<SUP>4</SUP> s, both of which are primarily determined by the light-travel effect. When the shell's outer radius is located at ~100--500 R<SUB>⊙</SUB>, the SBO temperatures fall into the energy band covered by the current soft X-ray facilities. We derive analytic lightcurves for SBOs in dense CSM shells and explore how different physical parameters affect the observed lightcurves and the temperature evolution. Despite the multitemperature nature of the emission caused by the light-travel effect leading to nonthermal-like spectra, we find that the time-resolved spectra within the limited soft X-ray band can still be well described by a blackbody model. This provides a natural explanation for the observed blackbody-like time-resolved spectra of soft X-ray SBO events. Our model can reproduce the observed X-ray lightcurves and temperature evolutions of the three known X-ray SBO events, EP260321a, XRF 060218, and XRO 080109, revealing a diversity in the properties of the dense CSM shells ejected by stripped-envelope progenitors before the explosion. Future discoveries of more soft X-ray SBO events by facilities such as Einstein Probe will provide opportunities for probing the episodic mass-loss history of massive stars in the final stages before core collapse.

paper.title: A Grid of Fast-rotating, Chemically Homogeneous, Supernova and/or Long Gamma-ray Burst Progenitors
paper.abstract: The understanding of the mechanism(s) by which massive stars collapse and possibly explode is rapidly maturing. Uncertainties in the structure of the stellar core at the onset of collapse are often dominant in numerical simulations, and a limited number of progenitor grids are available. This is especially true for explosions where rotation and magnetic fields play a significant or primary role. We present a grid of 113 single-star models with initial masses M<SUB>ZAMS</SUB> = 30--90 M<SUB>⊙</SUB> and initial rigid rotation ω<SUB>ZAMS</SUB> = 0.5--0.99 ω<SUB>crit</SUB> computed at Z = 0.001 with the open-source stellar evolution code MESA. We adopt a 128-isotope nuclear reaction network capable of following the weak reactions deleptonizing the core during and after silicon core burning. By construction, these models experience rotationally induced chemically homogeneous evolution, and reach the onset of collapse (v<SUB>infall</SUB> ≲ -300 km s<SUP>-1</SUP>) with large and structured amounts of angular momentum, possibly sufficient to form accretion disks on a protocompact object. Therefore, these progenitor structures provide a homogeneous set of models with updated input physics and improved algorithmic accuracy to understand stellar explosions of (some types of) stripped-envelope supernovae, possibly jetted and/or broad-lined, collapsars or magnetar-powered, and/or long gamma-ray bursts.

paper.title: Mock Catalogs of Strongly Lensed Gravitational Waves via a Halo Model Approach with Spaceborne Detectors
paper.abstract: Future spaceborne gravitational-wave (GW) detectors, such as LISA and DECIGO, are expected to detect a large number of GW events, a fraction of which may be strongly lensed by intervening galaxies or galaxy clusters. In this work, we develop a comprehensive framework to simulate strongly lensed GWs in the context of spaceborne detectors. Based on realistic astrophysical models for both the source population and the lens distribution, we construct mock catalogs of lensed GW events, referred to as GW--LMC--space. Our results show that, for a 4 yr LISA observation, the expected number of lensed events ranges from 0 to 131, depending on the adopted formation model of massive black hole binaries (MBHBs). The corresponding lensing probability for MBHBs can reach up to ~0.3%. For DECIGO, we find that the number of lensed events in a 1 yr observation is expected to lie in the range of 0--44, with a lensing probability of ~0.15% for stellar-mass binary black holes (BBHs), binary neutron stars (BNSs), and neutron star--black hole binaries (NSBHs). We further show that the overlap of lensed signals is a common feature in spaceborne detectors, which can significantly affect both the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) estimation and event identification. These results highlight the importance of accounting for signal overlap in the analysis of strongly lensed GW events in future spaceborne GW observations.

paper.abstract: Solar flares are violent energy-release events in the solar atmosphere, accompanied by intense electromagnetic radiation and energetic particles that threaten satellites, radio communications, and power infrastructure, making accurate flare prediction essential for space weather early warning.
