The two components jointly predict flare occurrence probability, with the True Skill Statistic (TSS) as the primary metric. Under active-region-isolated five-fold cross-validation, the model achieves TSS values of <inline-formula> <mml:math> <mml:mrow> <mml:mn>0.861</mml:mn> <mml:mo>±</mml:mo> <mml:mn>0.021</mml:mn> </mml:mrow> </mml:math> </inline-formula> and <inline-formula> <mml:math> <mml:mrow> <mml:mn>0.844</mml:mn> <mml:mo>±</mml:mo> <mml:mn>0.041</mml:mn> </mml:mrow> </mml:math> </inline-formula> for the <inline-formula> <mml:math> <mml:mrow> <mml:mo>>=</mml:mo> </mml:mrow> </mml:math> </inline-formula>C-class and <inline-formula> <mml:math> <mml:mrow> <mml:mo>>=</mml:mo> </mml:mrow> </mml:math> </inline-formula>M-class tasks, respectively, and performs at least as well as the strongest baselines retrained on the same data and the same folds. paper.title: Iceberg-Generated Waves From SWOT: Disintegration of Iceberg A-76A in the Southern Ocean
paper.abstract: Amid rising global temperatures, icebergs are calving more often and drifting into open waters. Their disintegration processes can trigger energetic surface gravity waves that propagate away from the iceberg remain poorly documented. paper.title: Whispers of supergravity in gravitational wave backgrounds: Determining the gravitino mass from cosmic thermal history

paper.title: Dark energy perturbations and the robustness of cosmological neutrino-mass measurements
paper.abstract: Cosmological observations are placing increasingly stringent bounds on the sum of neutrino masses, approaching the lower limits implied by neutrino oscillation experiments. Recent studies have suggested that dynamical dark energy may alleviate this apparent tension. Different combinations of neutrino mass and dark-energy clustering can provide similarly good fits to current data while yielding significantly different neutrino-mass constraints. Our results show that cosmological neutrino-mass measurements are inherently model dependent and that reliable neutrino-mass inference requires a consistent treatment of dark-energy perturbations.

paper.title: Mathematical Methods of Analytical Description of Wave Disturbances in the Stratified Atmosphere
paper.abstract: Wave disturbances are an important component of the dynamics of the Earth's atmosphere. They propagate throughout the entire atmosphere: from the lower surface layers, where they can be generated by ground and tropospheric sources, such as earthquakes, volcanoes, tsunamis, anthropogenic sources, etc., and up to the rarefied upper layers (~500 km), where their sources are solar wind disturbances, magnetic storms, and charged particle showers. The paper considers two main methods for analytically solving the system of differential equations describing linear wave processes in a model of a stratified non-isothermal atmosphere. It is noted that the equations for linear disturbances describe the following types of waves: acoustic and internal gravity waves freely propagating at an angle to the horizon, as well as horizontal (evanescent) waves. It is shown that acoustic and gravitational waves are described within the framework of the standard method, which consists in reducing the system of linear equations to a single second-order differential equation for one of the components of the perturbed velocity. The solution of this equation allows us to determine other perturbed quantities. Analysis of this method showed that it allows us to satisfactorily describe waves in the isothermal part of the Earth's atmosphere (thermosphere). The limitation of the specified method for considering evanescent waves is due to the fact that in this case we do not obtain a solution for all values of the horizontal wave vector. Another method, developed by us in previous works, is more acceptable for describing evanescent waves for arbitrary values of the horizontal component of the wave vector. The essence of this method is to use additional relations between the velocity components. This allows us to obtain easily integrated differential equations and find their solutions for each of the components, that is, to actually fully consider the problem of evanescent wave propagation. However, a limitation of this method is that it does not allow finding solutions in a non-isothermal atmosphere, except for the fundamental f-mode.

paper.title: Natal kicks of compact binaries - I. Population synthesis framework and illustrative examples
paper.abstract: The natal kicks imparted to neutron stars and black holes at birth are critical for understanding massive-star evolution, compact-object formation, and compact binary merger rates. However, constraining these kicks is challenging, since they cannot be directly observed. Here, we outline a framework for inferring natal kick probability distributions for compact binaries. Our method embeds the rapid binary-population code COSMIC in a Monte Carlo workflow that evolves ensembles of simulated binaries. From those which host compact objects, we can select subsets that match the observational characteristics of any given system (e.g. component masses, orbital period, mass-transfer status, systemic velocity). As a proof-of-concept, we apply this framework to six compact binaries spanning a wide range of companion masses and compact-object types. For each system, we identify the evolutionary channel(s) that could have led to the current observational characteristics, and isolate regions of allowed natal kicks and progenitor parameter space. We reconfirm that at least one black hole system, XTE J1118+480, must have received a natal kick <inline-formula><tex-math>$\upsilon _{\rm NK}\gt 100$</tex-math></inline-formula> km s<inline-formula><tex-math>$^{-1}$</tex-math></inline-formula>. The neutron-star system, GX 301--2, is also inferred to have received an impulsive kick exceeding 280 km s<inline-formula><tex-math>$^{-1}$</tex-math></inline-formula>. We discuss the strengths and limitations associated with population-synthesis-based inference methods and explore the effects of adopting different prescriptions for critical binary evolution phases. We provide a detailed demonstration of the non-linear relationship between <inline-formula><tex-math>$\upsilon _{\rm NK}$</tex-math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula><tex-math>$\upsilon _{\rm sys}$</tex-math></inline-formula>, highlighting the shortcomings of relying on observations alone to measure natal kicks. The inferred kick velocity distributions across our benchmark sample are generally consistent with previous constraints.

paper.title: Prospects of resolving and localising individual supermassive black hole binaries with pulsar timing arrays: the host ranking challenge
paper.abstract: Pulsar Timing Arrays (PTAs) are soon expected to detect individually resolved supermassive black hole (SMBH) binaries, opening the possibility for multi-messenger discoveries. The biggest challenge will be to pinpoint the host galaxy in a large localisation area. We simulate realistic binary populations consistent with the gravitational wave (GW) background, projecting the PTA sensitivity for the next 0-10 years. We inject the loudest binary on top of the background and use a standard detection pipelines to constrain its properties. We cross-match the GW sky map with comprehensive all-sky galaxy catalogues and estimate the number of candidate hosts in the localisation area assessing, for the first time, the number of missing galaxies due to incomplete coverage. We develop a ranking system that excludes galaxies with properties inconsistent with the GW posteriors, and prioritizes the remaining galaxies for follow-up observations. We find a ≍21, ≍38 and ≍51 percent probability of resolving a binary in the next 0, 5 and 10 years, respectively, reduced to 0.3, 3.8 and 14.1 percent if we consider only sources potentially localisable within 2,000 deg<SUP>2</SUP>. The localisation areas span hundreds of square degrees, but shrink significantly with the addition of more data. They contain on average ≍190,000 early type galaxies and ≍40,000 active galactic nuclei, with ≍33,500 missing candidate hosts. Our ranking method can exclude about 37 percent of the potential hosts and efficiently rank those remaining when the galaxy catalogue provides SMBH masses and redshifts, but becomes more inefficient when it relies on apparent magnitudes.

paper.title: Set them free: extending RAMCOAL to model massive black hole triplets in hydrodynamical simulations of galaxies
paper.abstract: Massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) and the higher-order multiples produced by repeated galaxy mergers evolve through regimes that cosmological simulations cannot resolve. These regimes determine merger delays, spins, recoils, and host galaxies at coalescence. We extend the RAMCOAL subgrid model to follow massive black hole triplets within hydrodynamical galaxy simulations. In the original three-stage binary model, black holes evolve as sink particles, undergo dynamical friction, and form bound binaries that harden through stellar scattering, gas torques, circumbinary-disc coupling, and gravitational-wave emission. When a hierarchical triplet becomes chaotic, RAMCOAL samples a library of outcomes from direct N-body experiments and follows the resulting mergers, exchanges, and ejections alongside the accretion and spin evolution of each black hole. Isolated-galaxy tests with different triplet geometries show that orbital configuration alone can change which pair merges and its coalescence time. For the first time, we follow an MBH triplet to coalescence within a hydrodynamical simulation of gas-rich galaxies, coupling triplet-driven mergers to host-galaxy evolution. Subgrid integration costs ≲ 1 ms of single-core time per MBH system and time step, independently of particle resolution. The resulting coalescence properties reflect the environment encountered during subgrid evolution. RAMCOAL thus provides a step towards merger catalogues linking gravitational-wave signatures to the galaxies in which the black holes evolve.

paper.title: A Log-Uniform Initial Magnetic Field Distribution Explains Pulsar and Magnetar Populations through Magnetic Inclination Alignment
paper.abstract: The origin of the gap in the observed magnetic field distribution between pulsars and magnetars raises a challenge to understanding these populations within a unified framework. We analytically show that the gap can be naturally explained by the alignment of the magnetic inclination angle between the magnetic and spin axes. Based on coupled evolution of spin-down and magnetic inclination angle in the plasma-filled magnetosphere, the alignment timescale follows τ<SUB>α</SUB>∝B<SUP>-2</SUP>. Thus, strongly magnetized neutron stars including high-B pulsars and magnetars align more rapidly than pulsars with 10<SUP>12</SUP> G, reducing their beaming fraction and thereby suppressing their observed numbers. However, magnetars are primarily identified through X-ray activity and are therefore relatively less affected by beaming. Taking into account both beaming fraction and luminosity corrections, we reconstruct the initial magnetic field distribution from the observed distribution. We show that pulsars and magnetars do not dictate intrinsically distinct initial distributions, but can instead be understood within a single continuous initial magnetic field distribution, such as a log-uniform distribution.

paper.title: Time-Delay Recovery in AGN Reverberation Mapping via Mutual Information
paper.abstract: Active galactic nuclei exhibit complex, nonlinear multiwavelength variability that standard cross-correlation techniques, sensitive only to linear covariance, may fail to capture fully. We apply time-lagged Mutual Information (MI) lag estimation, via the Kraskov-Stoegbauer-Grassberger k-nearest-neighbour estimator (k = 5) with a 150-iteration Random Subset Selection bootstrap, to the light curves of four Seyfert galaxies (Mrk 509, NGC 5548, NGC 4151, and NGC 4593) monitored across eight energy bands by Swift. In the UV/optical regime the MI estimator successfully reproduces the inter-band disc reprocessing lags established by the interpolated cross-correlation function, with performance degrading toward the optical where low variability amplitude produces poorly defined MI peaks. In the X-ray bands, where the physical X-ray, UV coupling is known to be weak the estimator fails to recover consistent lags across the sample, with the notable exception of NGC 4593. Contextualising these outcomes within the multifractal characterisation of our previous work, we discuss how MI performance relates to the multifractal spectral width ∆α of each band, and we propose ∆α as a candidate diagnostic for anticipating where MI-based reverberation mapping is likely to succeed or fail in multiband datasets of active galactic nuclei.

Overall, our results support a scenario in which a weakly magnetized neutron star accretes efficiently through a disk extending close to the stellar surface, demonstrating the power of broadband reflection spectroscopy in constraining neutron star accretion geometry.

paper.title: Stellar structure and rates of stellar precession
paper.abstract: We investigate the detectability and behaviour of spin--axis precession, applying classical formulae to twelve close binary systems (α CrB, AR Cas, FT Ori, QX Car, AI Hya, AG Per, V526 Sgr, V346 Cen, YZ Cas, MY Cyg, β Aur, RZ Cha), for which recent data have been published (Berkowitz, 2024). Using EZ-Web ZAMS models together with an extended version of the RADAU code, we computed internal structure parameters k₂, gyration radii β, and mechanical ellipticities ∊ₘ from which corresponding theoretical precession ratios (P/U) can be derived. Comparison with long-term photometric inclination changes |∆i| reveals a clear physical trend: systems with high precessional rates and relatively large masses (e.g., QX Car, AR Cas, AI Hya) exhibit the largest inclination variations, whereas older and more evolved systems (such as FT Ori and α CrB) show significantly weaker signatures. In all cases, the observed |∆i| values lie systematically below the corresponding ZAMS predictions, consistent with increasing central concentration, reduced mechanical ellipticity, and progressive tidal damping as the stars evolve. Overall, the results show that spin--axis precession is not only detectable in young massive binaries, but its amplitude directly traces their internal structure, underscoring precession's potential as a powerful diagnostic for probing stellar interiors and guiding future evolutionary modelling.

paper.title: Analysis of solar flare and sunspots on 4th Jan 2025 and their effects on space weather
paper.abstract: Solar flares and coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are among the most energetic phenomena in the solar system, often impacting space weather and terrestrial technologies. In this study, we utilize SunPy, an open-source Python library for solar physics, to analyze solar active regions and their correlation with flare and CME events observed on 4th January 2025. Data from GOES, SDO (AIA and HMI), Solar Oribter (STIX), e-CALLISTO, Aditya L1 (SUIT), and SOHO are processed to track flare intensity, active region evolution, shock wave and CME dynamics. The analyzed flare is identified as an X1.8-class event, and our study highlights key magnetic precursors that led to it. This work enhances understanding of solar eruption precursors and supports future predictive models for space weather forecasting.

paper.title: Timing and spectral variability of the accreting X-ray pulsar GX 301-2
paper.abstract: This work presents timing and spectral analyses of the accreting HMXB pulsar GX 301-2 using February 2025 NuSTAR data. We detected 670.12 ± 0.05s coherent pulsations at MJD 60708 in 3--45keV energy range. During this observation, the hardness ratio evolved from soft to hard state. This transition coincided with an increase in the absorption column density and substantial changes in the pulse profile. During the softer state, the pulse profile was primarily sinusoidal in shape with numerous complex sub-structures at lower energies. Beyond <mml:math><mml:mo>~</mml:mo></mml:math>10keV, signs of a double-peaked structure emerged, albeit weakly. The pulse profiles were dual-peaked during the harder state, and the broad main peak was narrower at higher energies. The pulsed fraction showed a steady increase with energy and was persistently greater during the harder state. The best-fit spectral model consisted of an absorbed power-law combined with iron fluorescence emission line. The near neutral Fe K<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>α</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math> doublet was detected only during certain pulse phases. The Fe K<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>β</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math> emission line was detected in the phase-averaged spectrum only. We detected pronounced Compton shoulder of iron K<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>α</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math> emission line at <mml:math><mml:mo>~</mml:mo></mml:math>6.33keV. A weak extension further down to <mml:math><mml:mo>~</mml:mo></mml:math>6.24keV was detected during harder state. The photon index varied across the pulse cycle and closely followed the profile shape.

paper.title: A comparative study of occurrence rates and nature of Ultraluminous X-ray sources in spiral and elliptical galaxies
paper.abstract: Ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) are mostly extragalactic non-nuclear point sources having X-ray luminosity exceeding the Eddington luminosity of 10 <mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>M</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⊙</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math> black hole i.e., <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>L</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>X</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>>=</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:math> 10<SUP>39</SUP> erg s<SUP>-1</SUP>. They are observed in all types of galaxies; spirals, ellipticals and dwarf irregulars. But the rate of occurrence of ULXs per galaxy varies, some might host a single ULX, whereas some host a large number. In this work we attempt to identify possible differences in ULX properties between two extreme categories in spirals and ellipticals, i.e. ULXs occurring at a rate of one per galaxy (<mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>N</mml:mi><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:math>) and those occurring at larger rate. We adopt an effective scheme to generate flux limited, credible samples corresponding to the two groups in spirals and ellipticals. From this study, we infer the presence of a separate population of ULXs in the <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>N</mml:mi><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:math> spiral group which contains a reasonable fraction of both soft and hard sources, while the remaining categories contain mostly harder sources. We also find six ULXs in <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>N</mml:mi><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:math> ellipticals with globular cluster association. In addition, we identify few luminous candidates likely hosting massive accretors. This study provides crucial hints of a potential link between ULX types and their occurrence rates and host morphology, a finding that warrants validation via targeted observations and detailed spectral analysis of these sources.

paper.title: HD3191, the high-mass X-ray binary that wasn't there
paper.abstract: The rapidly rotating B1IV:nn star HD3191 lies within the error box of a flaring Fermi<mml:math><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi></mml:math>-ray source. Although the counterpart of the Fermi source is likely an active galaxy, HD3191 has nevertheless been suggested to be a high-mass X-ray binary, possibly hosting a black hole companion. The star displays roughly sinusoidal photometric variations with amplitudes of <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mo>~</mml:mo><mml:mn>12</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:math>mmag for two frequencies <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>ν</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mn>0</mml:mn><mml:mo>.</mml:mo><mml:mn>1235</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:math>d<SUP>-1</SUP> and <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>ν</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn><mml:mo>.</mml:mo><mml:mn>6038</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:math>d<SUP>-1</SUP>. Half of the former frequency (<mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>ν</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>/</mml:mo><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:math>) had previously been interpreted as the orbital frequency of a high-mass X-ray binary in which the B1IV:nn primary undergoes ellipsoidal variations. We show that this scenario fails to account for the lack of significant radial velocity variations and for the overall properties of the star. Our spectroscopic observations instead unveil line profile variations, suggesting that the photometric and line profile variations arise from multi-mode pulsations rather than from orbital effects. Whilst we cannot rule out the possibility that HD3191 could be a nascent binary, consisting of a B1IV:nn with a low-mass pre-main sequence companion, the most likely scenario is a single star displaying non-radial pulsations. The fast stellar rotation would thus be intrinsic to the B1IV:nn star rather than being the result of a spin-up during a past mass-transfer episode.

paper.title: An ALMA view of the jet-arc CO clouds toward the TeV γ-ray source HESS J1023-575 and Westerlund 2: Evidence for the footprints of microquasar jets, the very powerful cosmic ray accelerator in the Galactic disk
paper.abstract: The TeV <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0002" notation="LaTeX">$\gamma$</tex-math></inline-formula>-ray source HESS J1023-575 (HESS J1023 hereafter) is one of the brightest High Energy Stereoscopic System (H.E.S.S.) sources near the young massive cluster Westerlund 2. HESS J1023 shows a remarkable positional alignment with the jet and arc CO clouds on its eastern and western sides over a length of 170 pc. We have carried out sub-parsec scale observations of the CO clouds with ALMA and have discovered that the clouds consist of numerous thin filamentary features of <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0003" notation="LaTeX">${\sim}0.5$</tex-math></inline-formula> pc width and 10-20 pc length at distance of 7.5 kpc, which are well aligned with the jet-arc axis. Based on the magnetohydrodynamical model of microquasar jets launched from the center of the <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0004" notation="LaTeX">$\gamma$</tex-math></inline-formula>-ray source HESS J1023-575, we present an interpretation that the thin filamentary clouds are the footprints of the microquasar jets on the H I gas. The model also explains the dissimilar jet vs. arc clouds in terms of H I density difference on each side. By using the density of the CO and H I gas and the <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0005" notation="LaTeX">$\gamma$</tex-math></inline-formula>-ray luminosity, we have calculated the cosmic ray proton energy <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0006" notation="LaTeX">$W_{\rm p}$</tex-math></inline-formula> to be <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0007" notation="LaTeX">$7\times 10^{48}$</tex-math></inline-formula> erg under the hadronic scheme, which is 10 times larger than those derived in the TeV <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0008" notation="LaTeX">$\gamma$</tex-math></inline-formula>-ray supernova remnants (SNRs) RX J1713.7-3946 and RX J0852.0-4622. It is likely that HESS J1023 has been active over 1-10 Myr, which is significantly longer than the duration of cosmic ray acceleration of the SNRs. HESS J1023 is therefore an outstanding source of cosmic rays equivalent to at least 1000 SNRs, and is possibly the most powerful CR accelerator in the Galactic disk. A high energy compact source in HESS J1023, which is likely a Myr-old black hole or neutron star, remains veiled due to heavy extinction.

paper.title: Polarized emission, neutrino deposition and geodesic-induced quadrupole waveforms in exact Horndeski and disformal black-hole exteriors
paper.abstract: We study which observables retain information about the radial structure of exact black-hole exteriors when circular-orbit or shadow diagnostics are degenerate. We compare the static non-stealth seed of quartic square-root Horndeski theory and a separate constant-kinetic disformal exterior. The first metric is used in its original seed frame, not as a new disformally generated solution. The specified nonzero-hair square-root realization has a horizon-divergent scalar invariant and an exterior scalar ghost with a negative radial characteristic speed squared. For the inverse-square lapse <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>N</mml:mi><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mn>2</mml:mn><mml:mi>M</mml:mi><mml:mo>/</mml:mo><mml:mi>r</mml:mi><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mi>χ</mml:mi><mml:msup><mml:mi>M</mml:mi><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:msup><mml:mo>/</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mi>r</mml:mi><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:msup></mml:mrow></mml:math>, we derive an exact eccentric separatrix and regular anomaly equations. At fixed turning points (8M, 24M), changing χ from zero to one lowers the radial frequency by 5.18% and raises the azimuthal frequency by 6.53%, although a different Schwarzschild orbit can match both frequencies. Fully differentiated eccentric mass quadrupoles yield distinct numerical-kludge burst profiles and, for suitable periodicity classes, a recurrence shorter than orbital closure. These are geodesic-induced quadrupole waveforms. Polarization is a source-dependent geometric response, and moving the prescribed neutrinosphere can reverse the fixed-radius deposition trend. The constant-disformal comparison preserves the critical shadow radius and azimuthal frequency while changing radial and transport observables. Published EHT and stellar-precession summaries are translated only into approximate, assumption-dependent consistency estimates. In particular, a Gaussian summary likelihood with a uniform nonnegative-χ prior gives approximate 95% upper endpoints 0.967 and 1.142 for the two Sgr A* mass--distance priors. Fixed-theory mass comparisons retain the coupling length.

paper.title: Periodic timelike motion and gravitational wave signatures around a magnetically charged black hole surrounded by quintessence
paper.abstract: We study bound timelike geodesics and gravitational-wave signatures of periodic motion around a static magnetically charged black hole surrounded by quintessence. Accounting for the nonasymptotically flat geometry, we determine the horizons and the inner and outer stability boundaries. Over the parameter range considered, increasing the quintessence strength narrows the angular-momentum interval supporting stable circular orbits and shifts it toward smaller values. Periodic trajectories are classified by the zoom-whirl taxonomy, (z, w, v) and their waveforms are calculated using the quadrupole-order numerical kludge approximation. Highly eccentric trajectories produce strong periastron modulation, whereas smaller radial excursions yield more continuous signals with narrower Fourier spectra. For <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>M</mml:mi><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mn>10</mml:mn><mml:mn>7</mml:mn></mml:msup><mml:msub><mml:mi>M</mml:mi><mml:mo>⊙</mml:mo></mml:msub></mml:mrow></mml:math>, <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>m</mml:mi><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mn>10</mml:mn><mml:msub><mml:mi>M</mml:mi><mml:mo>⊙</mml:mo></mml:msub></mml:mrow></mml:math>, and <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:msub><mml:mi>D</mml:mi><mml:mi>L</mml:mi></mml:msub><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mn>2</mml:mn><mml:mspace></mml:mspace><mml:mtext>Gpc</mml:mtext></mml:mrow></mml:math> yield approximate sky-averaged LISA signal-to-noise ratios of <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mn>0.009</mml:mn><mml:mspace></mml:mspace><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mspace></mml:mspace><mml:mn>0.032</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:math> under the adopted noise model. These fixed-geodesic signals exclude radiation reaction and do not establish inspiral detectability. Their differences reflect both the background geometry and the selected orbital propertie.

paper.title: Three-form dark energy: Constraints and multi-probe comparison with ΛCDM
paper.abstract: Three-form fields provide a theoretically well-motivated framework for dark energy, arising in higher-dimensional theories and exhibiting a rich cosmological phenomenology. We investigate a minimally coupled three-form dark energy model with a Gaussian potential and constrain it using current cosmological observations, including CMB shift parameters, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation measurements, Pantheon+ supernovae with and without SH0ES calibration, cosmic chronometers, and gamma-ray bursts. Parameter estimation is performed within a Bayesian Markov-chain Monte Carlo framework, while model comparison relies on several information criteria and the Bayesian evidence, as well as tension statistics. We find that the three-form model provides a viable and competitive description of the expansion history. It is mildly preferred over ΛCDM for the combination of early and late-time datasets that are heavily tensioned (CMB+BAO and Pantheon+SH0ES). This preference decreases to neutrality for the other, less tensioned combination of early-time and late-time data, while for individual early-time or late-time datasets analysed separately, the information criteria are neutral or favour ΛCDM. This suggests that the additional degrees of freedom associated with the three-form field may help accommodate cosmological observations of different origins within a common framework. The reconstructed dark energy dynamics exhibit a phantom phase at intermediate redshifts while approaching a cosmological-constant-like behaviour at early and late times, providing a distinctive observational signature. Although the model does not significantly alleviate the Hubble tension despite allowing higher values of H<SUB>0</SUB>, it remains consistent with current observations and offers a well-motivated alternative to ΛCDM whose predictions can be tested by future cosmological surveys.

paper.title: Diagnosing dark energy in the post-DESI era: From effective dynamics to multi-probe consistency tests
paper.abstract: The recent baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements from the dark energy spectroscopic instrument (DESI) have sharpened one of the central questions in modern cosmology: whether cosmic acceleration is driven by a true cosmological constant or by new physics in the dark sector, gravity, or the early Universe. Although DESI BAO data alone remain broadly consistent with flat Λ cold dark matter model, their combination with cosmic microwave background and supernova observations shows a moderate preference for an evolving dark-energy equation of state, often associated with effective phantom-crossing behavior. This preference should not be interpreted as a definitive detection of a time-varying dark-energy fluid. Rather, it exposes a broader degeneracy among late-time dynamical dark energy, dark-sector interactions, modified gravity, early-Universe sound-horizon calibration, neutrino-mass inference and residual systematics. In this review, we summarize the post-DESI status of dark-energy research, emphasizing both the significance and the limitations of the present evidence. We discuss dynamical dark energy as an effective description of the expansion history, compare it with interacting dark-energy and modified-gravity interpretations, and examine how the Hubble tension, the S<SUB>8</SUB> tension and cosmological neutrino-mass constraints act as joint consistency tests of the underlying framework. We further highlight the role of future geometry, growth, absolute-distance and baryon-distribution probes, together with reproducible multi-probe likelihoods, in distinguishing physical mechanisms from statistical fluctuations and residual systematics. We argue that the post-DESI era is shifting dark-energy research from parameter fitting toward multi-sector physical diagnosis.

paper.title: Simulating an imaging atmospheric radio telescope to observe cosmic gamma rays and cosmic neutrinos
paper.abstract: Observations of cosmic gamma rays with energies above the 10<SUP>12</SUP> electronvolts (TeV) regime are often a direct probe of events where our theoretical predictions are challenged by extreme conditions. Because high energetic cosmic gamma rays are rare, one needs collection areas with the size of roughly a dozen football fields (10<SUP>5</SUP>m<SUP>2</SUP>) or more to gather significant counting statistics in a short time. The imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope detects cosmic gamma rays in such large areas and currently offers the best reconstruction power for the cosmic particle's type, energy, and direction in particular. However, with only about 1,000hours of dark and clear nights every year, the imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope only has a duty cycle of about 12%. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel imaging atmospheric radio telescope. paper.title: Finite distance corrections to vacuum birefringence in strong gravitational and electromagnetic fields
paper.abstract: We develop a finite-distance framework for vacuum birefringence in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes threaded by strong magnetic fields. In the geometric optics limit of nonlinear electrodynamics, the two photon polarizations propagate along null geodesics of distinct effective (optical) metrics. Using a controlled weak-coupling expansion, we isolate the polarization dependent correction to the standard gravitational deflection and obtain a general expression for the differential bending angle ∆α ≡ α+ − α− with the source and observer at arbitrary radii. The derivation is based on a finite-distance Gauss-Bonnet construction on the polarization dependent optical manifolds, thereby extending the usual scattering at infinity treatment. As an examples, we apply the formalism to Euler-Heisenberg QED and to Born-Infeld electrodynamics, the latter providing a non-birefringent consistency check with ∆αBI = 0. We show that finite-distance truncation of the curvature flux generically suppresses the observable birefringence and provide explicit series corrections suitable for data analysis. For magnetar motivated field falloff and near surface emission, the suppression can reach the level of tens of percent and may approach ̃ 1/2 for near-limb, outward only trajectories. These results supply an essential finite-distance calibration for interpreting X-ray polarimetry measurements and for placing unbiased constraints on strong-field QED and broader NLED parameters.

paper.title: On the assessment of the disk truncation and detection of type-II-like bursts from the accreting millisecond X-ray pulsar IGR J17062-6143
paper.abstract: We present a spectral analysis of the NuSTAR and NICER observations of the accreting millisecond X-ray pulsar IGR J17062-6143, performed in 2022. The source remained in the hard spectral state during these observations, with a luminosity of about ~ 0.13-0.14 percent of the Eddington luminosity. The continuum emission of the NuSTAR spectrum is entirely dominated by a power-law component or by Comptonized emission of disc photons by a plasma with a high electron temperature ( ≳ 100 keV). The NuSTAR spectrum also reveals clear evidence of disc reflection, a broad Fe K line around 6--8 keV, and a Compton hump peaking at 20 keV, irrespective of the choice of the continuum models. Our spectral studies suggest a disk extending close to the neutron star surface ( ~ 6-20 R<SUB>g</SUB>) at low inclination angle ( ~ 41 degrees), as revealed by the self-consistent relativistic reflection model, relxill. In addition, we detected type-II-like bursts for the first time in the NICER observation of this source. Light curve profiles of type-II-like bursts exhibit different patterns, mostly associated with the so-called mode-0 and transition from mode-0 to mode-1 type-II bursts. The energy spectra of the persistent (pre-burst) and burst emission are well described by an absorbed Comptonization component, scattering disk- and blackbody-distributed photons, respectively, by a corona with a temperature of 1--3 keV. Although the origin of the type-II-like burst is not very clear, it has been possibly linked to disk-magnetosphere interaction of the accretion flow.

paper.title: Curvature-radiation geometries across the second CHIME/FRB fast radio burst population
paper.abstract: We present a population-level spectral analysis of fast radio bursts from the second CHIME/FRB catalog using three curvature-radiation--motivated templates: point-source, one-dimensional bunch, and paired-bunch cavity, together with two non-curvature oscillatory baselines. Fits are evaluated with reduced chi-squared <mml:math><mml:msubsup><mml:mi>χ</mml:mi><mml:mi>r</mml:mi><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:msubsup></mml:math>, the Akaike information criterion (AIC), the Bayesian information criterion (BIC), and the Ljung--Box residual autocorrelation test. All three templates yield median <mml:math><mml:msubsup><mml:mi>χ</mml:mi><mml:mi>r</mml:mi><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:msubsup></mml:math> values close to unity for both repeating and non-repeating bursts. Repeaters show narrower <mml:math><mml:msubsup><mml:mi>χ</mml:mi><mml:mi>r</mml:mi><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:msubsup></mml:math> distributions than non-repeaters, with statistically significant but modest population-level differences. AIC favours the one-dimensional bunch model for the largest fraction of sources within the curvature-radiation family; BIC also favours the 1d model in both FRB classes, though with a markedly increased relative share for the simpler point-source model. However, residual autocorrelation remains widespread across all models: only 12%--22% of sources simultaneously satisfy goodness-of-fit and residual-independence criteria, indicating persistent structured residuals beyond the tested templates. These results suggest that while curvature-radiation-motivated geometries capture the dominant spectral envelope of many FRBs, additional physical ingredients or spectral components are required to describe the fine-scale spectral structure of the data. Comparison with non-curvature baselines shows that oscillatory modulation is the dominant spectral signature within the CHIME band, with the curvature-radiation envelope not independently constrainable at these frequencies. The inferred effective spatial scales are ~ 16--18 cm for the one-dimensional model and ~ 25--28 cm for the cavity model. Their interpretation as bunch lengths or cavity separations is conditional on the assumed emission model.

The resulting Newman-Kerr-like metric depends on four intrinsic parameters: the electric charge <mml:math><mml:mi>Q</mml:mi></mml:math>, the ModMax nonlinearity <mml:math><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi></mml:math>, the Lorentz-violation amplitude <mml:math><mml:mi>ℓ</mml:mi></mml:math> and the spin <mml:math><mml:mi>a</mml:mi></mml:math>. We analyse horizon structure and separatrices in parameter space, derive the null geodesic equations and obtain the photon capture boundary that defines the BH shadow. Using ray-tracing, we compute shadow silhouettes and a suite of shadow observables (areal radius, characteristic radius <mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>R</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>s</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>, distortion <mml:math><mml:mi>δ</mml:mi></mml:math>, oblateness <mml:math><mml:mi>D</mml:mi></mml:math>) and show how <mml:math><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi></mml:math> and <mml:math><mml:mi>ℓ</mml:mi></mml:math> produce qualitatively distinct effects: <mml:math><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi></mml:math> acts as a screening factor for the electromagnetic imprint, while <mml:math><mml:mi>ℓ</mml:mi></mml:math> introduces angular-dependent metric rescalings that deform shadow shape beyond simple size rescaling. We confront model predictions with EHT angular-radius measurements for M87<mml:math><mml:msup><mml:mrow></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>∗</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msup></mml:math> and Sgr A<mml:math><mml:msup><mml:mrow></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>∗</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msup></mml:math> and derive conservative bounds on the combinations of <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mo>(</mml:mo><mml:mi>Q</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mi>ℓ</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mi>a</mml:mi><mml:mo>)</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:math>. paper.title: The X-ray Variability of the Ultraluminous X-ray Sources in the NGC 4631 Galaxy
paper.abstract: We perform a systematic study on the long-term X-ray variability for the five ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) in the NGC 4631 galaxy (X1--X5), using Chandra, XMM-Newton, and Swift observations covering a 24 yr span. Light curves for the five ULXs are presented, while X-ray spectra were modeled for observations with sufficient counts. The normalized excess variance and structure function are utilized to study the X-ray variability behavior of the ULXs. The normalized excess variance is anti-correlated with average X-ray luminosity for three ULXs, indicating that objects with higher average luminosity tend to exhibit relatively lower amplitude of variability. The structure function values increase with time interval in two sources, showing that flux variations become more significant for longer timescales. These trends are also found in the X-ray variability of active galactic nuclei (AGNs). The similarity between ULXs and AGNs, if confirmed for a larger sample of sources, possibly indicates similar underlying physical mechanisms for their X-ray variability.

summary.tldr: 利用 Chandra、XMM-Newton 与 Swift 在 24 年跨度上的存档观测，系统研究了 NGC 4631 中五个极亮 X 射线源（X1–X5）的长期 X 射线光变，发现归一化超方差与平均光度反相关、结构函数随时间间隔增大，行为与活动星系核相似。
summary.highlight: 首次对 NGC 4631 的全部五个 ULX 做统一的长基线（24 年、多台望远镜）变率分析，并用归一化超方差与结构函数两种统计量交叉验证；结果显示 ULX 的变率标度关系与 AGN 高度相似，为二者共享同一吸积物理机制提供了新的观测线索。
summary.authors_en: Jiashun Chen, Jianfeng Wu, Zikun Lin
summary.context_outlook: ULX 的 X 射线光变此前多为单源、短基线的零散观测，样本小且观测策略不统一，很难判断其变率是否存在可推广的规律，也难与 AGN 长期积累的变率–光度标度关系直接比较。本文将 Chandra、XMM-Newton 与 Swift 的存档数据统一处理，对同一天体中五个 ULX 做长基线变率测量，把归一化超方差和结构函数同 AGN 中已知的变率行为对照：三个源的变率幅度随平均光度升高而下降，两个源的结构函数随时间间隔增大而上升，这些正是 AGN 光变的典型特征。若这一相似性在更大样本中得到确认，ULX 与 AGN 可能由同一类吸积过程（如吸积率起伏或盘内不稳定性）驱动，变率因而可以作为区分不同物理状态、乃至探测 ULX 中黑洞质量的独立探针。展望未来，随着 XMM-Newton、Chandra 以及 Athena 等新一代 X 射线设施持续积累更长、更密且更均匀采样的光变曲线，ULX 变率研究有望像 AGN 领域那样从个案描述走向统计化的统一图景。

paper.title: R-mode Evolution and Gravitational Wave Radiation of Accreting Neutron Stars: The Effect of an Evolving Accretion Rate and the Accumulation of the Accreted Matter
paper.abstract: Neutron stars (NSs) in low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs) are considered as potential sources of gravitational waves (GWs) due to unstable r-modes. Contrary to the constant Eddington accretion rate <inline-formula> <mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mover><mml:mrow><mml:mi>M</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>̇</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:mover></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>Edd</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math> </inline-formula> generally used in previous studies, the accretion rate <inline-formula> <mml:math><mml:mover><mml:mrow><mml:mi>M</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>̇</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:mover></mml:math> </inline-formula> should actually vary with time as the binary system evolves. We thus investigate the r-modes, spin, and thermal evolutions of NSs in LMXBs using a realistic time-evolving <inline-formula> <mml:math><mml:mover><mml:mrow><mml:mi>M</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>̇</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:mover></mml:math> </inline-formula> obtained with the Modules for Experiments in Stellar Astrophysics (MESA) code. Our results show that using the time-evolving <inline-formula> <mml:math><mml:mover><mml:mrow><mml:mi>M</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>̇</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:mover></mml:math> </inline-formula>, the GW spectrum emitted by r-modes slightly differs from that derived with the constant rate <inline-formula> <mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mover><mml:mrow><mml:mi>M</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>̇</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:mover></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>Edd</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math> </inline-formula> in the frequency band 200 < f < 400 Hz and at f ≃ 70 Hz. However, in the former case, the duration of r-modes is significantly reduced to ≲4 × 10<SUP>6</SUP> yr, much shorter than the lifetime of the binary system. We further investigate the effect of accumulation geometry of accreted matter on the evolution of NSs and the GW radiation from r-modes. We find that in the presence of accretion mountains, both the evolution trajectory of the accreting NS in the internal temperature-angular velocity plane and the GW spectrum obviously differ from those obtained by assuming a uniform distribution. Taking the Cosmic Explorer as an illustration, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the GWs is 24.08 when accretion mountains are present, while 22.13 in the case of the uniform distribution. Although the SNRs are above the detection threshold for a single-detector search, the short duration of r-modes would probably make the detection much more difficult.

paper.title: Design and Implementation of a Dual-mode Digital Backend for the GZNU Small-aperture Antenna Array
paper.abstract: Small-aperture radio antenna arrays provide flexible platforms for high-time-resolution searches of bright radio transients, such as pulsar giant pulses and fast radio bursts (FRBs), as well as for long-duration monitoring and technical validation of array observing modes. To support the Guizhou Normal University (GZNU) small-aperture antenna array under construction, we developed a dual-mode digital backend based on the Xilinx RFSoC 47DR. The backend is designed to serve two complementary observing requirements. In Baseband Mode, the backend digitizes analog signals at a sampling rate of 1024 MHz and streams the raw voltage data with VDIF header to a server via a 100 Gbps interface for further processing. In PSRFITS Mode, dual-polarization signals from a single antenna are channelized using a polyphase filter bank (PFB) and Fourier transform, integrated, gain-adjusted, quantized, and converted into AABBCRCI polarization products before being encapsulated into PSRFITS files. System characterization show that the relative timing offsets among four ADC channels are on the order of 10<SUP>-2</SUP>-10<SUP>-1</SUP> ns for a reference signal at various frequencies. Packet-transmission tests show no packet loss during a four-hour PSRFITS-mode run, while a short-duration Baseband-mode test gives a packet loss rate of approximately 0.04%, limited mainly by the current storage system. Validation was completed via observations of the pulsar B0329+54 in PSRFITS Mode, resulting in well-defined waterfall plots and integrated profiles. These results demonstrate the initial end-to-end functionality of the RFSoC-based backend and provide a basis for future long-duration baseband recording, multi-antenna interferometric verification, and fast-transient searches.

paper.title: Holographically motivated Hubble-running dark energy: Phantom-divide crossing in VCDM and observational constraints
paper.abstract: Motivated by power-law dependences on the expansion scale in holographic dark-energy constructions, we study the Hubble-running equation of state $w_{\rm DE}=w_0(H/H_0)^q$ (HoloEoS), where $H$ is the Hubble expansion rate, $H_0$ and $w_0$ are the present values of $H$ and $w_{\rm DE}$, and $q$ is a constant dimensionless exponent controlling the running. We embed this history in VCDM, a type-II minimally modified gravity theory that propagates only the two tensor modes of general relativity. For regular expanding histories with standard matter, we reconstruct the potential $V(φ)$ of its nondynamical auxiliary scalar field, providing a Lagrangian description of both the homogeneous background and cosmological perturbations. This framework allows HoloEoS to realize a smooth late-time crossing of the phantom divide $w_{\rm DE}=-1$. We confront this VCDM realization with SPT, Planck, and ACT CMB data, updated DESI DR2 distances, and optionally DESY5 supernovae with Dovekie recalibration, comparing it with $Λ$CDM and the Chevallier--Polarski--Linder parameterization embedded in the same gravitational framework (CPL-VCDM). For the full data combination, the posterior medians and central $68\%$ credible intervals are $w_0=-0.881^{+0.040}_{-0.038}$ and $q=0.453^{+0.143}_{-0.133}$, with a crossing redshift $z_\times=0.476^{+0.106}_{-0.081}$ conditional on $0<z_\times<6$. For this data combination, physical-likelihood optimization by Metropolis--Hastings (MH) simulated annealing gives Akaike information criterion differences of $Δ\mathrm{AIC}\simeq-3.40$ for HoloEoS and $-4.10$ for CPL-VCDM relative to $Λ$CDM. Thus, a Hubble-scale-motivated dark-energy history realized within a specified gravitational theory achieves fitting performance comparable to CPL-VCDM while naturally allowing phantom-divide crossing.

paper.title: Simple multi-interacting fluids in SymBoltz
paper.abstract: We implement a simple and general way of specifying arbitrary interactions between baryons, dark matter and dark energy in the Einstein--Boltzmann code SymBoltz. Due to the symbolic-numeric interface and approximation-free structure of SymBoltz, the model definition is remarkably compact and convenient to modify by specifying only the covariant coupling. The full equations are stiff, but stable and fast to integrate with an efficient implicit solver, particularly with the sparse and analytical ODE Jacobian generated from the symbolic equations. We first validate it using single-interaction models, comparing their background evolution and matter and CMB power spectra with those from modified versions of CLASS, finding $0.1\%$--$1\%$ agreement at most scales. Finally, we show how our framework makes it trivial to implement models with any interactions of any complexity among all three species simultaneously, which requires a more involved implementation in other Einstein--Boltzmann codes like CLASS or CAMB. Our full model is specified in only around 300 lines of code and is easy to modify for any other interaction by just specifying it in three lines.

paper.title: Mapping the Evolving Cosmic Web on the Lightcone with WebON: HOLI Mock Strategy
paper.abstract: Wide-area spectroscopic surveys such as DESI require large ensembles of mock catalogues that follow gravitational evolution and tracer populations across the observer's past lightcone. We present WebON (Web ON the lightcone), a fast method for mapping the evolving dark-matter cosmic web onto the lightcone without periodic-box replication or the stitching of separately evolved snapshot shells. Displacements computed at a limited set of redshifts are combined with a particle-wise Zel'dovich estimate of the emission redshift and a continuous-redshift correction, allowing lightcone positions to be generated in a single forward pass. The method supports regularised ALPT and eALPT gravity solvers, with an optional short-range ridging correction. We illustrate full-sky matter and cosmic-web evolution and find percent-level agreement between lightcone and fixed-redshift angular power spectra over the tested redshift and multipole ranges, providing an internal consistency check of the lightcone construction. Optional modules address approximate relativistic position corrections and local primordial non-Gaussianity. Finally, we show how the spectral cosmic-web hierarchy connects WebON to the HOLI (Higher Order LIghtcone) mock strategy, in which post-processing ridging and calibrated HICOBIAN bias and subgrid prescriptions can recover tracer clustering beyond the nominal resolution of the ALPT matter field. Independent comparisons of ridged LPT matter fields with Abacus N -body simulations and published percent-level tests of the hierarchical tracer-bias model complement the lightcone consistency measurements presented here.

paper.title: Microscopic Realizability of Non-unique Bubble Hydrodynamics
paper.abstract: First-order phase transitions drive fluid motion that induces energy transport and gravitational-wave production. The flows are usually classified in terms of the wall velocity and the transition strength. We show that this description fails when the two phases have unequal sound speeds $c_\pm$. New mixed-hybrid profiles may appear, and for a strong hierarchy, $c_+\gg c_-$, where the phase behind the wall is much softer, heating or cooling ahead of the wall allow for the coexistence of distinct stationary flows at the same wall velocity and transition strength. This ambiguity is removed once thermodynamic normalization and entropy production are specified. We identify microscopic settings that realize these sound-speed hierarchies. In thermal plasmas it requires exponentially large mass-to-temperature ratios, whereas at finite density a conserved charge removes this obstruction, making dense matter its natural arena.

paper.title: Full-shape analysis of the Lyman-alpha forest power spectrum and bispectrum: validation on simulations
paper.abstract: The Lyman-$α$ (LyA) forest of neutral hydrogen provides a large-volume, high-resolution map of cosmological fluctuations from optical spectra at high redshift. To extract more information from the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), we derive an effective field theory (EFT) model for joint full-shape analyses of the LyA forest data. It combines the one-loop power spectrum of the LyA forest (FF), and of its cross-correlation with dark-matter halos, used as proxies for high-redshift quasars (FQ), with the tree-level bispectrum of the LyA forest (FFF). Importantly, the bispectrum breaks the LyA-specific degeneracy between the mean flux and the amplitude of the power spectrum. We validate our theory framework on idealized large-volume LyA forest mocks painted onto the AbacusSummit N-body simulation suite at redshift z=2.5. Fitting scales up to $k_\mathrm{max}^{FF\,(FQ)}=0.6\,(0.3)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the power spectrum and $k_\mathrm{max}^{FFF}=0.1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the bispectrum, our full-shape analysis yields unbiased constraints on the cosmological parameters in simulations. For a fully sampled flux field in a simulated volume of $V=8\,h^{-3}\,{\rm Gpc}^3$, we measure the Hubble constant, $H_0$, to $0.6\%$, the matter density, $Ω_{\rm m}$, to $1.6\%$ and the amplitude of matter clustering, $σ_8$, to $3.5\%$. Adding the bispectrum improves the constraints on $σ_8$ by $28\%$. We also demonstrate that the inclusion of the quasar one-loop power spectrum (QQ) and tree-level bispectrum (QQQ) further improves cosmological constraints by $\approx 35\%$ using $k_\mathrm{max}^{QQ,\,(QQQ)}=0.2,\,(0.08)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. Our theory framework enables full-shape analyses of high-redshift data from DESI and its successor DESI-II, enhancing knowledge of the growth of structure of the Universe during matter-domination.

paper.title: Astrometric microlensing by isolated black holes in the Roman Galactic Bulge Time Domain Survey
paper.abstract: Most of the hundred million stellar-mass black holes (BHs) expected in the Milky Way are predicted to be isolated. Characterizing this BH population will provide insights into stellar evolution and supernova explosion physics. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Galactic Bulge Time Domain Survey (GBTDS) will enable the detection of isolated BHs through astrometric microlensing, apparent stellar position shifts caused by deflection of distant starlight. We combine a Galactic model, stellar population synthesis model, BH initial--final mass relation, and kick velocity distribution to simulate events caused by isolated BH lenses. We assess the expected yield, sensitivity, characterization potential, and signal characteristics of these events to inform GBTDS search strategies. We predict $487 \pm 37$ isolated-BH microlensing events with detectable astrometric signals, 82% of which have impact parameters beyond 2 Einstein radii and consequently have small or undetectable photometric signals. Standard astrometric fits yield unit weight errors > 1.2 for 18% and > 2 for 2% of these events. Sensitivity peaks for 5-6$M_\odot$ BHs and is limited by the five-year GBTDS baseline. Weak microlensing parallax constraints limit BH mass precision, but events with Einstein timescales > 100 days and angular Einstein radii > 1.2 mas have high BH lens probabilities within our Galactic model. Wide-separation astrometric microlensing offers an independent discovery channel for isolated BHs beyond photometrically selected events. Realizing this opportunity requires dedicated multi-season GBTDS searches, joint astrometric and photometric modeling, and accounting for other astrometric variability. Although precise individual masses are challenging for these events, probabilistic lens classification could lead to Galactic abundance constraints on the population of isolated BHs.

paper.title: HydróDex: gotta match 'em all!
paper.abstract: We present a comprehensive hydrodynamic classification of stationary fluid profiles in first-order phase transitions within the constant-sound-speed model, a physically motivated extension of the standard bag model that allows the sound speeds in front of and behind the wall, $c_+$ and $c_-$, to differ. Solving the matching conditions at the bubble wall and evolving the profile in the surrounding plasma, we systematically identify and classify all the possible stationary solutions. The classification recovers all previously known direct and inverse detonation, deflagration, and hybrid solutions, while revealing a new class of stationary configurations, termed mixed hybrids, featuring rarefaction waves on both sides of the wall and oppositely directed fluid flows. For a sufficiently pronounced hierarchy $c_+ > c_-$, the classification in terms of the wall velocity $ξ_w$ and the asymptotic strength parameter $α_N$ further exhibits degenerate regions in parameter space, where multiple distinct stationary profiles correspond to the same physical inputs $(ξ_w,α_N)$. This non-uniqueness arises as the parametrization discards thermodynamic information and is resolved once the underlying microphysics is specified. We also compute the kinetic-energy budget and the associated acoustic gravitational-wave spectra within the sound-shell model, finding that mixed-hybrid solutions, despite their oppositely directed flows, introduce no additional spectral feature, and their spectra can be closely mimicked by ordinary direct or inverse hybrids with very different fluid profiles. Finally, we release HydróDex, a public code that implements the complete hydrodynamic classification, fluid-profile construction, kinetic-energy budget, and gravitational-wave calculation.

paper.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Enhancing deep-learning models: the impact of image processing and training data selection for strong-lens detection
paper.abstract: Euclid is expected to discover ~$10^5$ galaxy-galaxy strong gravitational lenses across ~14,000deg$^2$, requiring automated searches with high completeness and low false-positive rates. Despite advances in deep learning, the effects of training-set composition, image representation, and preprocessing on survey-scale detection remain poorly understood. We present an ablation study of the convolutional neural network used in the ECLIPSE strong-lens detection pipeline, evaluating different training configurations on a fixed test set. Using simulated and real Euclid data, we compare VIS-only and pseudo-RGB representations, FITS and JPEG formats, training-set composition, hard-negative selection, and multi-stage training. We also assess ensembling on ~67 million DR1 cutouts. Training-set composition and strategy strongly affect high-Recall performance. Omitting simulation based pre-training reduces high-Recall weighted average Precision by 83.7% for VIS-only and 74.5% for pseudo-RGB models. Negative-sample selection also substantially affects performance, while FITS yields modest gains over JPEG at high Recall (~2-5%). On DR1, the logit-mean ensemble improves average Precision by 28.0% and 39.9% over the individual VIS-only and pseudo-RGB models. Among ~70,000 candidates selected for visual inspection, it recovers 11,256 unique grade A (secure) and B (probable) lenses, compared with 9650 and 10,395 for the individual models. The branches show complementary ranking preferences, particularly for lenses benefiting from near-infrared information. Careful training-set design, realistic negatives, and multi-band ensembling improve survey-scale searches. Our final ensemble achieves ~80% Recall at the operational selection threshold, outperforming ablation models with higher global classification metrics and highlighting the need to optimise performance for realistic survey conditions.[Abridged]

paper.title: The Gravitational Wave Foreground from Galactic Cataclysmic Variables in LISA
paper.abstract: Electromagnetic observations have been the primary medium for studying cataclysmic variable (CV) systems, capitalizing on the invaluable opportunity they present to study binary stellar evolution and accretion. The launch of the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) mission, however, will enable a multi-messenger perspective of the population. We extend previous work to explore the gravitational wave (GW) spectra sourced by a local and Galactic population of CVs. Using the Bayesian LISA Inference Package (BLIP), we simulate LISA data containing these CV populations to understand their impact and our ability to jointly model CV and double white dwarf (DWD) GW spectra. While we find that a local CV population has negligible effect on the LISA datastream, a Galactic CV population will have a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 76, depending on the characteristics of the DWD population present, and will bias existing DWD spectral models if ignored. Current approaches struggle to accurately recover both populations' respective spectra, calling for the creation of multi-component spectral models that include GW contributions from both CVs and DWDs. These results point toward a promising future for the study of CVs with LISA.

paper.title: The Full-Shape Analysis of the Fading Dark Sector Model
paper.abstract: We analyze the Fading Dark Sector (FDS) model, which is motivated by string theory and in which the fading of the dark sector is driven by a scalar field. The model is specified by two $O(1)$ numbers $(c,c')$ that parametrize the logarithmic derivatives of the dark energy and dark matter densities with respect to the field in Planck units. In previous work, we showed that this model provides a good fit to the DESI BAO, CMB, and SN datasets. Here, we extend that analysis to include the DESI DR1 full-shape galaxy power spectrum, which adds information about the time evolution of cosmic structure and provides an independent consistency check of the FDS model. We find that, when the DESI DR1 full-shape data are combined with CMB+DESI DR2 BAO+DES-Dovekie, the FDS model outperforms the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) $w_0$-$w_a$ parameterization by $Δχ^2_{\rm MAP}=-4$ at equal parameter count and is preferred over $Λ$CDM at $4.1σ$. The inferred values of $(c,c')$ with the full-shape data are unchanged from our previous analysis, so this improvement indicates that FDS makes a prediction for the growth of structure that captures the observed growth history better than the $w_0$-$w_a$ parameterization.

paper.title: Exoplanets are predominately aligned with exo-Kuiper Belts
paper.abstract: The architectures of planetary systems encode their formation and dynamical histories. In the Solar System, the near alignment of planetary orbits, the Kuiper Belt, and the Sun's equator supports planet formation in a rotating disk of gas and dust. However, some exoplanet systems show planets on orbits misaligned with their host stars or other planets, raising the question of whether misalignments are primordial or produced by post-formation dynamics. We present the first population-level constraints on the mutual inclinations of 32 planets in 16 systems relative to debris disks. We find that planets across orbital distances from 0.1 to 100 AU are predominantly aligned with the debris disks within 10 deg (30/32 planets). The alignment holds across systems spanning tens of million years to a few gigayears in age. These results indicate that the aligned architecture of the Solar System is representative of the birth conditions of exoplanet systems.

paper.title: Augmenting Galaxy Catalogues using Machine Learning in the FLAMINGO Simulations
paper.abstract: Hydrodynamic simulations are instrumental in the analysis of observations such as galaxy clustering used for the estimation of cosmological parameters. However, for these purposes, the simulations need both a large box size and high resolution, which is computationally prohibitive. In this work we use the connection between galaxies and their host dark matter halos to populate dark-matter-only simulations, using data from the FLAMINGO simulations suite. We employ the Extremely Randomized Trees algorithm to model the connection between the mass profile, history and environment of dark matter halos and the probability distribution of the stellar mass of the galaxy contained in the halo. We use halos matched between a dark-matter-only simulation and the corresponding hydrodynamical simulation to train a model for centrals. For satellites, we employ a Gaussian Processes emulator that simultaneously optimises the hyperparameters of a model and selects for the dark matter features that are predictive of the stellar mass while being insensitive to the differences between the hydrodynamic and dark-matter-only simulations, then train a model on only these features. We then apply these models to produce a new galaxy catalogue for the 2.8 Gpc FLAMINGO-10k dark-matter-only simulation as a product of this work. We demonstrate that this catalogue reproduces the statistics of the galaxy-halo connection predicted by the smaller volume hydrodynamical simulation on which the model was trained, including the stellar mass function, stellar mass-dark matter mass relation, 2-point correlation functions and correlations between stellar mass and dark matter concentration, half mass radius and dark matter mass within 3 Mpc.

paper.title: Gravitational-wave hierarchical inference from population samples
paper.abstract: Standard approaches to gravitational-wave population inference require evaluating the probability density of the population model. While appropriate for models composed of exact functional forms, this approach is not compatible with state-of-the-art astrophysical predictions from population-synthesis codes, which simulate samples from astrophysical models whose densities are unknown. We present an approach that solely requires samples and never density evaluations of the targeted population model. Key technical ingredients include efficient surrogates for the single-event likelihoods and detection probability, together with an efficient sampling strategy. Using detections up to GWTC-5.0, we validate the method against standard inference with a parametric model, showcase its flexibility on a simulated population including hierarchical mergers, and present a realistic application to a grid of astrophysical population-synthesis simulations with five formation channels. This work paves the way toward a direct comparison of astrophysical models and gravitational-wave data.

summary.context_outlook: 层级贝叶斯族群推断长期依赖可解析求值的族群密度，参数化与非参数化模型皆然，其与天体物理的联系多靠事后把峰、断点等特征与形成通道预言作定性对比 [[Abbott+ 2023]]。为直接接入族群合成模拟，前人先在模拟网格上构造中间密度插值——核密度估计、高斯过程回归、神经网络、归一化流等 [[Taylor+ 2018]]，[[Colloms+ 2025]]，或改用免密度的模拟推断 [[Leyde+ 2024]]，但这些方案会引入难以量化的系统误差，且每套新模拟都需重建或重训 [[Cheng+ 2023]]。本文转而「以抽样代替求值」：只需从族群模型取样，把求值负担转移到单事件似然与探测概率的代理上，并用限制在事件后验支撑内的抽样压低蒙特卡洛方差——后者已被证明会偏置族群推断 [[Essick+ 2022]]，[[Mancarella+ 2025]]。作者在 GWTC-5.0 上依次验证了参数化模型、含层级合并的模型 [[Gerosa+ 2021]] 与五通道族群合成网格三类应用。该框架的关键组件只依赖引力波数据与探测网络，可与具体天体物理模型解耦、一次构建反复使用，因而朝「模拟预言与引力波数据直接比较」的长期目标迈出一步；未来随模拟速度与样本量提升，有望扩展到端到端推断，并系统研究网格分辨率与统计精度之间的权衡。

paper.title: Searching for magnetic field changes in the central compact object 1E 1207.4-5209 in two decades of X-ray spectra
paper.abstract: The central compact object (CCO) 1E 1207.4-5209 is remarkable in that its X-ray spectrum shows clear absorption features at ~0.7 and 1.4 keV. Attributing these features to electron cyclotron resonance, the implied surface magnetic field is B~(7-8)x10^10 G, which agrees approximately with the field inferred from the spin properties of the pulsar. Here we examine all XMM-Newton EPIC pn spectra from more than 30 observations of 1E 1207.4-5209 from 2001-2020. We model the rotation phase-averaged and phase-resolved spectra with a two blackbody and multiple absorption line model, focusing on potential changes in the absorption lines which would correspond to changes in the magnetic field that could be related to the pulsar's possible spin glitch in 2015 and recent detection in radio. We find the phase-averaged spectral parameters, and by implication the magnetic field, are constant across nearly 20 years of data, while some parameters characterizing the phase-resolved spectra vary with rotation phase. The spectral line energies and widths (e.g., E_1~0.66 keV and full width of 0.34 keV) imply the magnetic field distribution across the X-ray emitting regions spans the range B~(6-11)x10^10 G, with the highest fields being visible during the declining phase of the pulsations of 1E 1207.4-5209.

paper.title: Many-body Response to Spin-Independent and Spin-Dependent Dark Matter Scattering in a Superfluid Helium-3 Target
paper.abstract: The QUEST-DMC experiment employs an ultra-low-temperature superfluid $^3$He target in an effort to detect sub-GeV dark matter (DM). The low-momentum scattering of such light DM is sensitive to the many-body structure of superfluid $^3$He, making it necessary to account for the collective behaviour of the medium. We present a first-principles calculation of the DM scattering rate in this inherently quantum many-body medium for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions. The leading consequence of this many-body behaviour is a kinematic enhancement of the scattering rate arising from the Fermi-Dirac statistics of the ultra-low-temperature target. Accounting for this extends the projected reach to lower DM masses for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions under the benchmark detector assumptions considered here. The resulting sensitivity improvement becomes increasingly pronounced as the detector threshold drops into the sub-eV regime. It is negligible at the conventional readout threshold of approximately $31$ eV, but becomes significant at the $0.51$ eV benchmark threshold for SQUID-based readout. Specifically, at this threshold, incorporating the many-body response extends the higher-energy recoil tail and improves the projected low-mass reach by approximately $2.5\%$ relative to the single-atom approximation. This improvement becomes more pronounced at lower thresholds. Reaching a threshold of $5$ meV could further extend the sensitivity of QUEST-DMC into the realm of sub-MeV DM.

paper.title: Soft Excess Variability and a Test of X-ray Reprocessing in AGN Mrk 359 and NGC 4051 using NICER and TESS
paper.abstract: Continuum reverberation mapping of AGN accretion disks assumes that X-ray reprocessing drives the UV/optical variations on short timescales. This reprocessing should also produce an X-ray reflection spectrum, which could be the soft excess observed in many Type 1 AGN. Consequently, if the soft excess traces the reflected emission, the soft excess and optical light curves should be correlated because their variability is driven by the same illuminating X-ray continuum. We present results from a cross-correlation study using simultaneous NICER and TESS observations of $\sim$$30\mathrm{~days}$ for two AGN: Mrk 359 and NGC 4051. We performed time-resolved spectroscopic fits to the X-ray data using a model with power-law and soft-excess components. We find no strong correlation between the optical and soft excess light curves, with correlation coefficients $R(τ)$ $\sim$0.5 for both sources. The total X-ray light curve also shows a similarly poor correlation with the optical variations. However, we find a stronger correlation between the primary X-ray flux and the soft excess flux for both sources. The lack of correlation between the primary X-rays and soft-excess with the optical variations implies that simple linear X-ray reprocessing is not the dominant process driving the optical variability. Either an intervening reprocessor between the inner X-ray region and outer disc is present that dilutes the X-ray-optical correlation, or the optical variability is driven by other mechanisms such as extreme-UV reprocessing or intrinsic disk variability.

paper.title: Euclid DR1 Legacy Science on Ultracool Dwarfs: New URLD candidates in Euclid and SPHEREx
paper.abstract: Unusually red L dwarfs (URLDs) probe extreme atmospheric conditions in the substellar regime, where enhanced dust opacity, cloud structure, and surface gravity effects challenge standard brown dwarf models. As free-floating analogues of young giant exoplanets, they provide key benchmarks for interpreting low-resolution infrared spectra from current and future wide-field space missions.   The goal is to identify new red L dwarf candidates both photometrically and spectroscopically in the first data release (DR1) of the Euclid space mission. The area covered is about 1,900 and 50 square degrees in the wide and deep survey, respectively.   We used colour cuts in multiple colour-colour diagrams combined with point-source and quality criteria to identify candidate red L dwarfs in both the Euclid wide and deep survey fields. We cross-matched photometric candidates with the SPHEREx mission and Euclid red grism spectra to confirm spectroscopic properties and evaluate bolometric magnitudes and colours.   We identified 1202 and 38 red L dwarf candidates in the Euclid wide and deep surveys, respectively. Spectroscopic follow-up and archival cross-matching confirm a substantial new population of red L dwarfs. Distance-independent diagnostics show that these objects occupy distinct loci characterised by enhanced condensate opacity and significant redness.   Euclid vastly expands the census of unusually red L dwarfs. While preliminary spectral classifications suggest many of these new candidates are intermediate-age (Pleiades-like) objects, a subset exhibits extremely red signatures indicative of very young, low-gravity (<=10 Myr) atmospheres, providing vital benchmarks for young exoplanet research.

paper.title: Multipoles in the IllustrisTNG simulation galaxies and implications for Strong Gravitational Lens modelling in Time-delay Cosmography
paper.abstract: Time-delay cosmography is a powerful independent probe of the Hubble constant ($H_0$), yet reaching the sub-2$\%$ precision required to resolve the Hubble tension demands a rigorous treatment of mass model systematics. We use realistic massive elliptical galaxies from the IllustrisTNG hydrodynamic simulation suite to characterise higher-order angular mass complexity in the form of multipoles ($m=1,3,4$) and quantify their impact on $H_0$ inference. We find that these multipole perturbations are common and emergent features of galaxy assembly; in 51$\%$ of our total samples ($54\%$ TNG100-1 galaxies and $85\%$ for TNG50-1 galaxies), the addition of multipole terms to a standard elliptical power-law model is preferred by the Bayesian Information Criterion. Ignoring these structures in lens modelling introduces systematic biases in $H_0$: for perturbations of $\sim2\%$, the biases are of the order of 1--2$\%$ for $m=1$, 4--5$\%$ for $m=3$, and 3--6$\%$ for $m=4$ multipole. While the $m=4$ (boxy/discyness) mode induces a predictable directional bias, odd-order modes ($m=1,3$) introduce significant stochastic scatter. We demonstrate a degeneracy where unmodelled internal multipoles can be effectively absorbed by the external shear component. This combined with low signal-to-noise observations can create ``hidden biases'' where formally perfect fits to imaging data ($χ_ν^2 \approx 1$) could harbour significant cosmological errors. Our results provide an astrophysical basis for multipole priors and highlight the necessity of moving beyond rigid parametric models to achieve high-accuracy cosmography in the era of \textit{Euclid} and LSST.

paper.title: Note on quantum optimal measurements of CMB spectral distortions
paper.abstract: As quantum sensing techniques continue to push the frontier of detection of ultra-weak signals, one may wonder if a sophisticated quantum strategy could be used to enable measurement of spectral distortions in the cosmic microwave background. Using quantum Fisher information techniques, we prove that the optimal strategy is simple frequency-binned intensity measurement. This proof strategy also enables us to provide numerical estimates for the information-theoretic minimum observation time required to observe the $μ$- and $y$-distortions expected from $Λ$CDM cosmology. As case studies, we compare these results to the PIXIE and SPECTER mission concepts, and show that they are within a few orders of magnitude of this fundamental limit.

paper.title: Receiving Exoplanet Messages with Gravitational-wave Carriers: The Gravitational-wave Radial Velocity Method
paper.abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) radial velocity (RV) may offer a new method for detecting exoplanets, one that would primarily target planets orbiting GW-emitting, ultracompact, post-main-sequence stellar objects such as white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes. In this work we show that while similar to electromagnetic-based RV, this GW-based method depends on the ''phase modulation index'' (PMI), a parameter that is more sensitive to high-mass, long-period exoplanets. We investigate the potential of GW RV for GW sources in both the mid-frequency spectrum (where the upcoming LISA mission will operate) and the high-frequency spectrum (where the current LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) observatories operate). Remarkably, we find that the PMI increases by a factor of $\sim \mathrm{O}\left(10^4 - 10^6\right)$ going from the mid-frequency to the high-frequency GW spectrum, which results in a greater redistribution of observed power due to the exoplanet's presence. By analyzing the power content of the observed GW signal, we derive analytic expressions to predict the GW carrier frequency power loss due to the exoplanet and the signal-to-noise ratio of the GW source and the exoplanet. We also explore the effects of the additional Doppler effect caused by the motion of the GW observatory and the potential for GW source parameter bias introduced by the presence of an undetected exoplanet. All of this helps us better understand where the GW RV method may work best in the exoplanet mass-period discovery space.
