paper.title: Multimessenger Exoplanets: Combining Infrared Excess and Astrometry with Gravitational-wave Detections of Double White Dwarf Exoplanets
paper.abstract: Multimessenger astrophysics provides a powerful framework for characterizing astrophysical systems through multiple, independent signals rather than relying solely on electromagnetic (EM) observations. While most prior multimessenger studies have focused on the properties of ultracompact objects, recent work has shown that gravitational waves (GWs) detectable with the upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) observatory can also be used to detect exoplanets orbiting stellar remnants. In particular, this includes circumbinary planets around tight double white dwarf (DWD) systems. This population is unique: no such planets are currently known around DWDs, and only a handful of circumbinary planets around main-sequence stars and planets orbiting white dwarfs (WDs) have been identified. Independent EM confirmation will be essential, especially for the first GW-detected exoplanets, to validate this method. While EM techniques are unlikely to efficiently survey large populations of DWDs, GW detection followed by targeted EM confirmation provides one pathway for identifying and characterizing these systems. Using a representative case, the known DWD ZTF J2243+5242 scaled to a fiducial distance of 150 pc, we compute the detectability of circumbinary exoplanets via LISA GW observations. We then demonstrate two complementary EM techniques--JWST infrared (IR) excess and Gaia or Habitable Worlds Observatory astrometry--that could independently confirm a GW-detected planet in this fiducial system. We present the first exploration of IR excess around DWDs as a viable exoplanet detection method, extending its established use for solitary WDs. Both EM techniques overlap with regions of parameter space where LISA is sensitive to DWD exoplanets, enabling robust confirmation and characterization.

paper.title: The Eclipsing $δ$ Scuti Binary HIP 7666: Absolute Dimensions and Pulsation Properties
paper.abstract: We present a comprehensive analysis of the pulsating eclipsing binary HIP 7666 (TIC 308953703), containing a $δ$ Sct-type component, based on 120-s TESS photometry and 63 newly acquired high-resolution echelle spectra. While previous orbital solutions were limited by sparse spectroscopic sampling, our extensive radial velocity (RV) measurements enable a robust determination of the system's physical parameters. The primary has an effective temperature of $T_{\rm eff,A}$ = 7376$\pm$72 K and a projected rotational velocity of $v_{\rm A}\sin i$ = 56.6$\pm$5.3 km s$^{-1}$. Joint modeling of the light and RV curves shows that HIP 7666 is a detached system in a circular orbit, with Roche-lobe filling factors of $f_{\rm A}$ = 57 \% and $f_{\rm B}$ = 44 \%. The masses and radii are determined to better than 2 \% precision: $M_{\rm A}$ = 1.822$\pm$0.029 $M_\odot$, $R_{\rm A}$ = 2.154$\pm$0.017 $R_\odot$ for the primary, and $M_{\rm B}$ = 1.246$\pm$0.020 $M_\odot$, $R_{\rm B}$ = 1.170$\pm$0.015 $R_\odot$ for the secondary. The binary-based distance (316$\pm$8 pc) agrees well with the Gaia DR3 parallax-based distance (313$\pm$1 pc), validating the derived system parameters. Frequency analysis of the light-curve residuals reveals 15 significant signals, predominantly in the $δ$ Sct pulsation frequency range. PARSEC evolutionary tracks indicate an age of $\sim$0.9 Gyr and a supersolar metallicity ($Z=0.03$), with the primary on the main sequence and the secondary located close to the zero-age main sequence. Galactic kinematics place HIP 7666 in the thin disk.

paper.title: Resonant Trapping of Neutrinophilic Dark Matter in Supernovae
paper.abstract: Supernova cooling provides some of the strongest constraints on light particles beyond the Standard Model, including sub-GeV dark matter (DM). While sufficiently large couplings to the Standard Model sector can trap these particles inside the supernova or cause them to decay before escaping, there typically exists an intermediate range of couplings in which their efficient production and subsequent escape lead to excessive energy loss, resulting in stringent constraints on new light particles. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time that, for certain types of DM-neutrino interactions, resonantly enhanced $s$-channel scattering with neutrinos can efficiently trap DM inside the supernova and can fundamentally alter the conventional supernova cooling constraints. In particular, we show that for mediator masses comparable to the supernova core temperature, this resonant scattering can prevent a substantial fraction of the produced DM from freely escaping, thereby significantly weakening, or even evading, the usual supernova cooling constraints on such models.

paper.title: Calibrated Period-Luminosity Relations for Mira variables in the Large Magellanic Cloud in the Vera C. Rubin Observatory $zy$-band Photometric Systems
paper.abstract: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space Time (LSST) is expected to discover numerous Mira variables in nearby galaxies, enabling their application for the cosmic distance scale. Miras are excellent distance indicators at infrared wavelengths, and therefore their period-luminosity (PL) relations in reddest $zy$ photometric systems will be crucial in the LSST era. We present first empirical $zy$-band PL relation for 85 oxygen-rich (O-rich) Miras located in the Large Magellanic Cloud based on time-series observations collected using the Dark Energy Camera (DECam) at the Víctor M. Blanco 4-m Telescope. The DECam photometry was directly calibrated using the Rubin Observatory Data Preview 2 (DP2) data. The observed PL relations were found to exhibit a break around a period of $\sim 300$ days, and therefore we only derived and calibrated the PL relations for Miras with a period shorter than $300$ days. We also explored the Rubin LSST DP2 data for known Mira variables in three Local Group dwarf galaxies. The $zy$-band light curves of Miras in IC 1613 are too sparsely sampled, whereas the DP2 observations of NGC 6822 and the Sagittarius Dwarf Irregular Galaxy cover only a short temporal baseline. For an O-rich Mira in NGC 6822, we obtain a distance modulus $μ= 23.32\pm0.24$~mag in good agreement with the literature. Significantly improved temporal coverage is expected in the first official Rubin LSST data release that will enable a robust validation of the PL relation in these nearby systems.

paper.title: Polarization of strongly lensed gravitational waves as a probe of the lens-induced orientations of electromagnetic counterparts
paper.abstract: Strong gravitational lensing is a well-established phenomenon in electromagnetic (EM) observations, where the lensed images and arcs are resolved on the two-dimensional sky and constrain the mass distribution of the lens. Strongly lensed gravitational waves (GWs) are also expected to be detected routinely by next-generation detectors, but their multiple images are recorded only as one-dimensional time series without positions. Among them, lensed binary neutron star mergers can be accompanied by EM counterparts with resolvable structures, such as relativistic jets. In EM lensing, the lens-induced change in the apparent orientation of such a structure can be measured only relative to other images or statistically, because its intrinsic orientation is not directly observable. In this work, we show that the GW polarization, which the lens leaves unchanged, provides this missing reference, i.e., a compass, so that the orientation offset of each image can be measured in absolute terms. We place this orientation layer on the EM image plane together with image positions from the lensed host arcs and Fermat-potential heights from GW time delays and magnifications. Using a mock population of such mergers observable by the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer, we find that the predicted image positions and arrival times are calibrated once the detection selection is included. The lens-induced orientation offsets reach tens of degrees and are detectable in up to a third of the events, at viewing angles above about $40^\circ$ for quadrupole-dominated signals.

paper.title: Linear monitoring-feedback Model for Linearized gravity
paper.abstract: Whether gravity has quantum degrees of freedom is a question of fundamental importance. We formulate a linear monitoring-feedback framework for gravitational interactions that includes local classical-record models of semiclassical gravity and, when quantum resources are supplied in correlated ancilla inputs, can reproduce linearized quantum-gravity dynamics. Auxiliary systems monitor the positions of massive bodies, and their records are fed back through a chosen gravitational response kernel. At the level of linear input-output theory, this construction makes the deterministic response explicit while exposing the force noise and correlations associated with the auxiliary sector. We organize the allowed ancilla correlations into three regimes. In Regime-I, independent ancillas have unsqueezed, uncorrelated sensing and back-action quadratures. A single object then has a minimum classical-gravity noise (CGN), S_F^min = 2 hbar M Omega_SN^2, where Omega_SN is the Schrodinger-Newton frequency set by the microscopic mass distribution. In Regime-II, arbitrary local sensing--back-action correlations are allowed, but the ancillas associated with different objects remain independent. The single-object CGN is then unrestricted, while the joint force-noise matrix obeys a determinant bound that is equivalent to the local classical-channel/no-entanglement bound. In Regime-III, cross-object correlations and a common nonlocal mediator are allowed. The commuting force noises can then be jointly squeezed, entanglement between the masses can occur, and--with a suitable retarded response and input state--the monitoring-feedback system can reproduce the noise and commutators of linearized quantum gravity, including non-Markovian quantum fluctuations.

paper.title: $^8$B Solar Neutrino Measurements of Solar Core Size and Temperature from 5805 Days of Super-Kamiokande
paper.abstract: The detection of solar neutrino provides direct evidence for on-going fusion in the core of the Sun and serve as a probe for that solar core. Production rate of $^8$B is sensitive to the solar core temperature. Adiabatic flavor conversion of $^8$B solar neutrinos depends on the local solar electron density. Combined with the roughly exponential decrease in solar electron density with increasing distance from the center of the solar sphere, the solar core size, density, and temperature are inferred. This article presents an outer bound on solar core size and measurements of the density and temperature in the solar core based on Super-Kamiokande phase I-IV solar neutrino data. An outer bound is set for the solar core at $90\%$ confidence level as $0.499R_\odot$ for the high metallicity B16+GS98 Standard Solar Model and $0.381R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12 which includes protosolar accretion. A combined fit with the SNO polynomial coefficients improves the limit to $0.268R_\odot$ for B16+GS98 and $0.215R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12. Results for other metallicity cases are also reported. In the high metallicity scenario assuming nominal solar core density and solar core size, temperature at the solar center is reported at $T_\text{C}=(15.599\pm0.0016)\times10^6$ K and $T_{\text{npz}}=(15.492\pm0.0017)\times10^6$ K at the peak radius of the $^8$B production profile.

paper.title: SN Progenitors of SNRs in OB Associations in the LMC. I. Assessment of Methodology Using N63A
paper.abstract: Color--magnitude diagrams (CMDs) can constrain the progenitor masses of supernova remnants (SNRs), but mass estimates for massive stars are affected by limited temperature sensitivity, extinction, crowding, and nebular contamination. We use the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) SNR N63A and its OB association LH83 as a benchmark to evaluate CMD-based mass estimates. Among the tested diagnostics, the extinction-corrected MCPS $B$ vs. $U-B$ CMD provides the most useful constraint on the massive-star population. The $V$ vs. $B-V$ CMD is less reliable, while the reddening-free $W$-$Q$ diagram does not improve individual mass estimates because of its larger photometric uncertainties. Gaia EDR3 recovers bright stars missing or saturated in MCPS but provides weaker separation among the hottest stars. For seven spectroscopically classified stars, the $B$ vs. $U-B$ CMD-based masses are lower than the HR-diagram masses inferred using the same MIST tracks by $8.0~M_\odot$ on average, with a scatter of $7.0~M_\odot$. Isochrone comparisons suggest that most of the massive stars in LH83 formed about 7-15 Myr ago, complicating progenitor mass estimates based on the present-day mass function. Nevertheless, the masses of D243-1a and D243-2, stellar lifetimes predicted by the MIST models, and the empirical bubble-size-progenitor-mass relation suggest a progenitor mass of order 25-30 $M_\odot$. Our results highlight the potential and limitations of this approach for studying other LMC SNRs in OB associations.

paper.title: Predicting Individual Dark Matter Halo Concentrations from Their Assembly Histories
paper.abstract: We present an empirical model for predicting concentration parameters of individual dark matter halos in cold and warm dark matter (WDM) cosmologies over z=0-5. Constructed using a large suite of cosmological N-body simulations, our model separately incorporates cosmic expansion (linear growth factor), mass scale (linear density fluctuations), halo mass assembly histories via the Extended Press-Schechter (EPS) scaled formation variable, plus a WDM damping term tied to the half-mode mass. It works for both virial and 200 $ρ_{crit}$ halo definitions. Across all tested cosmologies and redshifts, our global logarithmic fit gives concentration scatter ~0.09 dex for relaxed halos and ~0.09 to 0.10 dex for all halos. While relaxed halos maintain nearly constant scatter near 0.09 dex, the scatter of all halos at z>3 increases from 0.10 to 0.18 dex, revealing substantial violent-relaxation impacts on high-redshift halo structure. At fixed mass, concentration scatter is dominated by assembly history. We extract the scaled formation variable's probability distribution function (PDF) from merger trees and find departures from standard EPS theory. This PDF is narrower in WDM than LCDM due to suppressed small-scale perturbations and rapid, delayed monolithic collapse near the WDM truncation scale. Monte Carlo realizations with our formulae reproduce concentration distributions and match our prior peak-concentration model, whereas standard EPS underestimates concentrations from delayed-formation bias. Our framework offers a transparent, computationally lightweight tool to predict individual halo concentrations across diverse cosmological models.

paper.title: Axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant: Bayesian constraints from current cosmological data
paper.abstract: We constrain canonical axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant using DES Year 5 supernovae, DESI DR2 BAO, compressed CMB information, and geometry-corrected Gold-2017 growth data. We solve the background and linear-growth equations and sample with PolyChord. Our joint prior is logarithmic in the decay constant over $0.005\leq f/M_{\rm Pl}\leq10$ and uniform in the initial angle $θ_i=φ_i/f\in[0,π]$, conditioned on $π-θ_i\geq H_{\rm inf}/(2πf)$ with $H_{\rm inf}=10^{13}$ GeV and reduced Planck mass $M_{\rm Pl}$. The broad-prior model favors recent thawing, with median $w_{{\rm DE},0}=-0.865^{+0.068}_{-0.053}$, $m_φ\in[0.91,4.39]\times10^{-33}$ eV, and $f/M_{\rm Pl}\in[0.589,4.899]$ (central 68\% credible intervals). Bayes factors relative to flat $Λ$CDM are 0.70 and 30.1 for the normalized fluctuation-conditioned prior (Convention I) and its further conditioning on numerical acceptance (Convention II). Restricting $f\leq M_{\rm Pl}$ gives $f/M_{\rm Pl}\in[0.262,0.822]$ at 68\% credibility and Bayes factors 0.233 and 32.4. Relative to the zero-vacuum axion model, the broad-prior Bayes factors are 0.620 and 1.65, providing no compelling evidence for a negative cosmological constant. Local likelihood optimization gives an Akaike information criterion difference $Δ{\rm AIC}\simeq-10.87$ for the zero-vacuum model relative to flat $Λ$CDM. For this model, assuming that the instanton generating $m_φ^2f^2=Λ_{\rm UV}^4e^{-S_{\rm inst}}$ satisfies the axionic Weak Gravity Conjecture, the one-sided 95\% posterior lower limit on the minimum compatible coefficient $c_{\min}$ rises from 37 to 55 as the ultraviolet scale $Λ_{\rm UV}$ increases from $10^{-10}M_{\rm Pl}$ to $M_{\rm Pl}$, in tension with an order-one coefficient under these assumptions.

paper.title: Periodic Modulation of Linear Polarization Fraction in Repeating FRB 20240114A
paper.abstract: Long-term polarization changes in repeating fast radio bursts (FRBs) can probe their emission geometry and propagation environment. We searched for periodic variation in the degree of linear polarization (DOL) of FRB~20240114A using the polarization catalog from the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope. The sample contains 6,099 bursts detected on 95 observing days over $\sim 488$ days. The daily mean DOL series was analyzed using phase distance correlation and Lomb--Scargle periodograms over trial periods of 10--240 days. The strongest peaks occur at $119.91^{+2.67}_{-2.04}$ and $122.31^{+2.63}_{-2.82}$ days, respectively. The quoted ranges correspond to the period intervals above the global $3σ$ thresholds. Global false-alarm probabilities were estimated from \(10^7\) random permutations of the daily values among the fixed observing dates, with the full period search repeated for each permutation. The resulting probabilities are \(9.98\times10^{-4}\) and \(8.95\times10^{-4}\), corresponding to equivalent Gaussian significances of \(3.09σ\) and \(3.12σ\), respectively. As a supplementary check, the same analysis using daily median DOL yielded similar peaks near 120 days. A descriptive sinusoidal fit to all 95 daily mean DOL measurements at a fixed period of 119.91 days has a semi-amplitude of 3.23\%. Possible explanations include precession-driven changes in viewing geometry and variations in propagation conditions within a binary system.

paper.title: Squeezing Drives Southward Magnetic Field Enhancement During 10 May 2024 CME-CME Interaction
paper.abstract: The southward magnetic field carried by coronal mass ejections (CMEs) is a key driver of space weather events, yet how interacting CMEs amplify this field remains debated. The 10 May 2024 event, which produced the strongest geomagnetic storm since 2003, offers an ideal testbed for this question. Combining multi-spacecraft observations with high-resolution controlled numerical experiments, we track the CMEs continuously from their origin near the solar surface to beyond Earth, and find that inherent squeezing during CME-CME interactions generates the sustained enhancement of the southward field, exceeding 60 nT in magnitude near Earth. First driven by the dynamic pressure of the trailing CME and later maintained by magnetic and thermal pressures at the CME-CME interface, squeezing transforms the preceding CME from a bulky cloud into a flattened "pancake" structure, prevents expansion-induced field decay, and maintains an amplified southward field over long distances. The strength of this enhancement scales with the intensity of the squeezing. Our findings establish a direct link between CME-CME interaction and strong southward fields, laying a physics-based foundation for understanding and forecasting the geoeffectiveness of interacting CMEs.

paper.title: Probing the Activity History of Repeating Fast Radio Bursts with Cluster Lensing
paper.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond duration coherent radio transients, some of whose sources repeat, but the nature and active lifetimes of their engines remain uncertain. Strong lensing by galaxy clusters provides a physical lever on this lifetime problem: a short campaign can sample emission epochs of a repeating FRB separated by years, and distinct bursts in different lensed images, given a known relative lens delay, set a lower bound on its active lifetime, whereas delayed copies of a single burst only encode the lens delay. Based on the cluster-lens model of MACS J0717.5+3745, we quantify the accessible range of emission epochs for finite activity episodes, observing windows, and discovery selection. For a source-frame episode of duration \(100~{\rm yr}\) at \(z_s=2\) and a source-frame rate of \(0.1\,{\rm h}_{\rm src}^{-1}\), a five year campaign conditional on discovery yields a \(95\%\) gain threshold of \(m_{95}\simeq25.6\), corresponding to a source-frame span of \(L_{95}\simeq42.6~{\rm yr}\). At the population level, combining distinct burst associations with same burst echoes provides a way to test specified activity durations with a finite lens catalogue, e.g., activity durations differing by an order of magnitude can be distinguished with expected Bayes factor above $20$. More broadly, these lensed source frame epochs enable applications beyond activity-duration tests, e.g., linking burst activity to the evolution of the engine and its environment. Galaxy-cluster lensing therefore provides a promising future probe for accessing otherwise unobserved source history and for distinguishing between different activity duration models.

paper.title: High-resolution Observations of Physical Properties of Dynamic Fibrils Around a Sunspot
paper.abstract: Understanding the formation and evolution of dynamic fibrils (DFs) in active regions is essential for uncovering the physical processes operating in the highly structured and magnetized solar atmosphere. High-resolution chromospheric observations from the New Vacuum Solar Telescope (NVST) show DFs with periodic up-and-down motions. We carry out a statistical analysis of 176 DFs around a sunspot. The mean values of deceleration, maximum velocity, maximum length, and duration of the DFs are $120 \boldsymbol{\pm 43}~\mathrm{m~s^{-2}}$, $15.9 \boldsymbol{\pm 4.5}~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$, $1.13 \boldsymbol{\pm 0.48}~\mathrm{Mm}$, and $270 \boldsymbol{\pm 63}~\mathrm{s}$, respectively. Several pairs of parameters exhibit correlations, most notably a clear positive correlation between deceleration and maximum velocity. The consistency between the periodicities of DFs and running penumbral waves is first identified. We further find that DFs in regions with more vertical magnetic fields exhibit larger decelerations and shorter periods, whereas those in regions with more horizontal magnetic fields exhibit the opposite behavior. These results, together with the presence of running penumbral waves, support the interpretation that DFs are driven by slow magnetoacoustic waves. Furthermore, the multiwavelength signatures of DFs from the chromosphere to the corona imply a potential contribution to energy transport and heating in the solar atmosphere.

paper.title: Axial gravitational-wave propagation and mass--gravity identifiability in conformal scalar--tensor lensing
paper.abstract: We investigate tensor-wave propagation in a specified massless, unscreened conformal scalar--tensor theory using a static Einstein--scalar exterior matched to a weakly self-gravitating matter lens. The odd-parity gravitational master potential has a scalar-charge correction at radial order $R^{-4}$ for fixed Einstein-frame mass. Its next $R^{-5}$ coefficient depends on $\ell(\ell+1)-9$, reversing sign between the quadrupole and higher multipoles; we test the expansion against the exact exterior potential. We connect this result to the locally normalized post-Newtonian light-deflection parameter and distinguish the Schwarzschild baseline at fixed Einstein-frame mass from that at fixed measured matter mass. A finite-radius WKB expansion reveals cancellation of the leading frequency-dependent potential moment for the quadrupole at fixed multipole, whereas a separate fixed-impact-parameter limit recovers an achromatic geometrical-optics action and a subleading axial contribution. Independent null-geodesic bending and numerical quadrature check these limits. For a point lens, achromatic observables constrain an effective mass rather than the lens mass and scalar coupling separately. An illustrative two-image Fisher calculation quantifies differential-phase identifiability after arrival-time and constant-phase nuisance parameters are released. The phenomenological phase experiment is separated from action-derived propagation quantities; model-specific dispersive observations require a complete matched image transfer function.

paper.title: What constrains the neutron-star crust? Present data, future measurements, and EOS doppelgängers
paper.abstract: The neutron-star crust plays a central role in pulsar glitches, thermal evolution, and stellar oscillations, yet its properties remain difficult to constrain. We use Bayesian inference with a unified crust-core equation of state to assess what present nuclear and astrophysical data tell us about the crust and what future stellar measurements can add. Within this model, present crust constraints are dominated by chiral effective field theory, with laboratory data providing additional information and current stellar observations having a smaller effect. The adopted theoretical bands determine how tightly the crust properties are constrained, while the treatment of neutron-rich surface energy affects their inferred values. Forecasts centred on a single reference equation of state show that more precise measurements of radius, tidal deformability, and total moment of inertia mainly constrain crust thickness. They provide little additional information about the crust-core transition, crust mass, or crustal moment of inertia and do not recover the precision lost when the chiral effective field theory constraint is removed. Two models with nearly identical global stellar observables can have crust masses and crustal moments of inertia differing by about a factor of two, yet remain indistinguishable at the assumed precision. Precise global measurements therefore need not uniquely determine the crust. Observations that directly probe the crust are needed to distinguish these models.

paper.title: Complexity and symmetry: The asymmetry factor approach
paper.abstract: We study the influence of the instantaneous appearance of a time-like Killing vector (TKV) in self-gravitating fluid spheres during their evolution. For doing so we resort to the concept of asymmetry factor which allows the existence of any specific type of symmetry (e.g. a TKV), exclusively, for a given value of the time-like coordinate. We consider adiabatic and dissipative fluids. The analysis of different relevant physical variables in this process shows the imprints of the emergence of TKV at some point of the evolution. Particular attention is paid to the relationship appearing between the TKV, and the complexity factor describing the degree of complexity of the fluid, bringing out for the first time a link between complexity and symmetry.

paper.title: Numerical experiments on sunspot penumbral flows
paper.abstract: We present 3D radiative magnetohydrodynamic simulations of sunspots with a self-consistently generated penumbra. We analyze the impact of resolution, surrounding opposite-polarity fields and subsurface large-scale flows on the structure and stability of the simulated penumbra. Extended penumbral filaments are obtained for a subset of the simulations. These were run at 25 km (15 km) horizontal (vertical) resolution and with initial conditions favoring fields with strong horizontal components in the penumbral region. The surface velocities in these simulations are consistent with observations of Evershed flow. The main driving mechanism remains the same as illustrated previously in Rempel (2012). The most successful simulations produce extended penumbrae using a potential magnetic field top boundary, in contrast to previous simulations of extended penumbra with an artificial enhancement of horizontal magnetic field at the top boundary.

paper.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1) : Performance of the redshift measurement and spectroscopic analysis
paper.abstract: The European Space Agency's Euclid mission has issued its first major data release(Data Release 1, DR1), providing a transformative view of the extragalactic sky through deep photometry and near-infrared slitless spectroscopy. This paper presents the Euclid DR1 spectroscopic data set and details the evolution of the spectroscopic processing function (SPE PF) pipeline, which is responsible for the automated analysis of 1-dimensional spectra acquired by the Near-Infrared Spectro-Photometer (NISP). The SPE PF pipeline workflow comprises spectroscopic classification, redshift determination, and the systematic measurement of spectral features. Emission line fluxes are derived using two independent methodologies: direct integration (DI) and Gaussian fitting (GF). For sources exhibiting broad H$α$ profiles (velocity dispersion larger than $1500$ km s$^{-1}$), a dedicated `QSO mode' is implemented to robustly deconvolve nuclear and host galaxy components. The data set was validated by cross-matching Euclid results with external spectroscopic catalogues, specifically Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR1, and through an extensive visual inspection campaign of approximately 4000 sources within the Euclid Deep Field North (EDF-N). For high-quality samples selected in the EDF-N, we find a 98.5\% agreement between Euclid and DESI spectroscopic redshifts. This success rate increases to 98.9\% when incorporating pipeline probability and reliability estimators. (abridged)

paper.title: Evidence for a Fast, Long-Period, Hot Population of Accreting Neutron Stars
paper.abstract: Context. Accreting neutron stars in low-mass X-ray binaries allow us to probe the accretion histories that produce recycled millisecond pulsars. Aims. We expand the analysis of the spin distribution with an enlarged sample of 39 accreting neutron stars and investigate whether the high-frequency objects preferentially occur in binaries with longer orbital periods and have higher quiescent surface temperatures. Methods. We compare several empirical models for the spin distribution. We use stochastic drift-diffusion estimates and simple braking models to determine whether short-timescale torque fluctuations or secular spin-down can account for the observed population widths. Results. The best statistical description of the spin distribution consists of a broad low-frequency component and a narrow high-frequency concentration centred at ~566 Hz with a width of ~32 Hz. Fast rotators preferentially occupy longer orbital-period binaries, with possibly higher neutron star temperatures. Short-timescale stochastic accretion torque fluctuations cannot produce the observed spin-frequency dispersion in either the fast or the slow component, even under generous assumptions. We show that a non-linear deterministic braking mechanism can instead shift and compress a spin distribution, but the spin data alone do not identify the braking mechanism. Conclusions. The population widths appear to reflect differences in long-term torque conditions and/or evolutionary histories rather than short-timescale torque noise. If the fast systems are close to spin equilibrium, their narrow distribution requires the combination of physical parameters setting the equilibrium frequency to vary relatively little from source to source.Any model that explains the spin distribution should therefore also explain why the fast systems tend to have longer orbital periods and, possibly, higher temperatures.

paper.title: General $δN$ formalism in Single Field Inflation and Graph Theory
paper.abstract: We study higher order correlation functions in single field inflation using the $δN$ formalism and methods from graph theory. By representing connected tree level contributions as graphs, we systematically classify their independent topologies, momentum shapes and amplitudes. We show that the amplitudes of arbitrary trees factorize into products of primary amplitudes, providing a general framework for relations among higher order correlators, including the Suyama-Yamaguchi equality. As the number of external legs increases, the number of distinct tree topologies grows exponentially, whereas the number of algebraically distinct amplitude products grows considerably more slowly. As an application, we consider ultra-slow-roll inflation followed by a transition to a slow-roll attractor. For transitions without a potential step, we derive an explicit all-order expression for the vertex amplitudes and establish their positivity and dependence on the sharpness of the transition. When a potential step is included, we prove that all nonlinear vertex amplitudes remain positive for upward steps, whereas downward steps allow cancellations at specific parameter values. These cancellations can eliminate entire families of tree contributions, including configurations in which the leading local bispectrum and trispectrum vanish simultaneously while higher order correlations remain nonzero.

paper.title: Asteroseismology of blue straggler stars in $ω$ Centauri. Stellar collisions as a possible formation scenario
paper.abstract: Context. Blue stragglers are intriguing stars that appear more massive and younger than expected from single-star evolution, yet their evolutionary histories remain elusive because of the multiple possible formation channels. A promising and poorly explored avenue for addressing this problem is asteroseismology, which provides the most stringent constraints on internal structure and evolution.   Aims. We investigate five SX Phoenicis stars from the core of the globular cluster ωCentauri that pulsate in two radial modes and occupy the blue-straggler region of the colour-magnitude diagram. Seismic models are constructed assuming a collisional origin and compared with our previous seismic studies based on single-star evolution. For comparison, we also explore a binary-evolution scenario involving mass transfer for one of the stars.   Methods. The evolution of the parent stars is computed with MESA. The collision is then modelled with the MMAMS code, which reconstructs the merger remnant using an entropic variable. The subsequent evolution is followed with MESA up to the current age of the cluster. Finally, we construct seismic models reproducing the observed frequencies of the two radial modes.   Results. We present the first seismic modelling of SX Phe stars (blue stragglers) based on the collision-formation scenario. Convective-core overshooting is essential for rejuvenation and for obtaining seismic models in the main-sequence phase of evolution, but it is not always sufficient. Whether a merger remnant undergoes rejuvenation depends in a complex way on the masses of the parent stars, metallicity, and collision time. We identify three evolutionary behaviours: no, delayed, and immediate rejuvenation. The collisional seismic models imply younger ages and higher masses than the seismic models based on single-star evolution.

paper.title: WISE-VAULT: Decade-long Mid-Infrared Variability of WISE AGN
paper.abstract: Mid-infrared (MIR) variability provides a powerful probe of accretion processes and dust reprocessing in active galactic nuclei (AGNs), as it is less affected by extinction than optical flux. Using multi-epoch photometry from \textit{WISE} and NEOWISE spanning over a decade, we investigate the MIR variability of $\sim$4.5 million color-selected AGNs. Variability is quantified using maximum--minimum amplitudes ($ΔW1$), excess variance, reduced $χ^2$, and structure function (SF) analysis over timescales of 0.5--10 years. We identify 632,939 variable AGNs, including 54,897 sources that exhibit large-amplitude variability ($ΔW1 > 0.5$ mag) and 624 with extreme intrinsic variability ($A_{\rm var} > 0.5$ mag). A subset of these sources shows flare-like behavior, identifying them as candidate changing-look AGNs or tidal disruption events that warrant further spectroscopic and multi-wavelength follow-up. The SF analysis shows radio-detected AGNs exhibit the highest variability amplitudes, followed by X-ray detected and the overall AGN sample. The variability amplitude is strongly anti-correlated with the Eddington ratio, indicating enhanced variability in lower accretion rate systems. A weak positive dependence on radio-loudness further suggests a contribution from non-thermal emission in radio sources. These results demonstrate that MIR variability provides a robust diagnostic of accretion physics and an efficient means of identifying extreme and rapidly evolving AGN phenomena. The full catalog of variable AGNs is made publicly available.

paper.title: Symbolic Regression Fitting for Roche Lobe Radius
paper.abstract: We present a compact approximation to the dimensionless, volume-equivalent Roche lobe radius $R_{\rm L}/a$, obtained by applying symbolic regression to radii calculated from the full Roche potential. Over $10^{-5}\leq q\leq10^5$, the expression reduces the root mean square error from $1.97\times10^{-3}$ for Eggleton's formula to $5.95\times10^{-4}$, while its maximum relative error is $1.39\%$, compared with Eggleton's $0.83\%$. Calculations at additional mass ratios give a mean relative error of $0.331\%$. The formula is monotonic, recovers the $q^{\frac{1}{3}}$ scaling at small mass ratio, and approaches a large-mass-ratio limit within $0.036\%$ of the limiting Roche model. In a NumPy float64 benchmark of $10^7$ direct formula evaluations, the SR expression takes $0.217$~s compared with $0.450$~s for Eggleton, a speed-up of $2.08$. These results quantify the accuracy and evaluation cost of a compact algebraic alternative for binary-system calculations.

paper.title: Unsupervised Machine Learning Classification of FRB 20121102A across Distinct Active Episodes: Implications for FRB Emission Physics and Source Environments
paper.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients of extragalactic origin. Identifying distinct burst populations and investigating their variations across active episodes provide important insights into the physical origins of repeating FRBs. In this paper, we apply an unsupervised machine learning approach to bursts from three active episodes of FRB 20121102A observed by the Five-hundred-metre Aperture Spherical Telescope (FAST). Our analysis reveals four distinct clusters primarily distinguished by their spectral properties. Notably, Cluster 1 exhibits bimodal-like distributions in central frequency and bandwidth and contains nearly all high-energy bursts, with a mean energy about an order of magnitude higher than those of the other clusters. It also occupies a distinct region in the width--fluence parameter space. These results suggest that this cluster may represent a distinct burst population potentially associated with different emission physics. Furthermore, the fractions of different burst clusters vary across active episodes. Cluster 1 accounts for about 27\% of the bursts in 2019, compared with about 8\% in 2022 and 2023. Cluster 2, with higher central frequencies and narrower bandwidths, has the largest fraction in 2019 and 2022, whereas Cluster 3, with broader bandwidths and intermediate central frequencies, has the largest fraction in 2023. These variations may indicate changes in the physical conditions of the emission regions or the local propagation environment across active episodes.

paper.title: Quasinormal modes of dyonic axion black holes with nonlinear electrodynamics
paper.abstract: We study quasinormal modes (QNMs) of static charged black holes with a massless axion and nonlinear electrodynamics (NED). Without NED corrections, we compute the complex QNM frequencies of five oscillatory mode families in the system of five dynamical degrees of freedom. These families are continued from the fundamental Reissner--Nordström (RN) modes. Axion coupling generically breaks gravitational and electromagnetic parity isospectrality. At representative nonzero couplings, all five frequencies are distinct even on purely electric RN backgrounds without axion hair. Adding magnetic charge sources axion hair, couples all five perturbations, and modifies their oscillation frequencies and damping rates. Additional purely imaginary growing modes occur in some strong-coupling benchmarks. The known electromagnetic--scalar spectral degeneracy at $Q/M=\sqrt{7}/4$ for $\ell=2$ in the decoupled RN limit explains the linear frequency splitting induced by a small axion coupling. We include two quartic NED interactions obtained by squaring the two standard electromagnetic invariants. With the axion decoupled and equal quartic coefficients, electromagnetic duality makes the first-order NED frequency shift of each individual gravitational or electromagnetic branch independent of electric--magnetic charge composition at fixed $Q/M$. For unequal coefficients, duality instead constrains the sum of the first-order NED frequency shifts within each isolated RN parity pair. Depending on the coefficients, NED increases or decreases the damping rates by about one percent in representative backgrounds, while the quartic terms remain small compared with the local Maxwell energy density throughout the exterior. The QNM frequencies and NED shifts obtained with the spectral method agree with independent integration-and-matching results at representative parameter values.

paper.title: Suprathermal bulk viscosity in binary neutron star mergers
paper.abstract: Numerical relativity simulations of binary neutron star mergers and core-collapse supernovae indicate that the neutron star matter can be driven far from equilibrium due to large amplitude density oscillations, with frequency in the kHz range. Urca processes in neutron star matter try to restore the system towards equilibrium providing strong bulk viscous damping of these density oscillations. Standard bulk viscosity calculations typically assume small amplitude density oscillations, such that the deviation from chemical equilibrium $μ_Δ$ is less than the temperature $T$. In this work we compute the complete amplitude dependent bulk viscosity, taking into account, for the first time, thermal blurring effects and collisional broadening of in-medium nucleons. Our results show that the non-linear effects in bulk viscosity start to become important when the oscillation amplitude is about $10$ percent of the background density. In this regime the bulk viscosity can increase by three to five orders of magnitude. These results have important consequences for simulations of binary neutron star mergers as well as their multi-messenger observations.

paper.title: Constraining Accretion Regimes of Little Red Dots from Their Variability
paper.abstract: The ``little red dots'' (LRDs) are photometrically and spectroscopically non-variable on rest-frame baselines of months, with a $5.9σ$ deficit relative to ordinary active galactic nuclei (AGNs). If we consider LRDs to be accreting black holes, this non-varying could be a clue about the nature of the accretion. Here, we present a general semi-analytic model of variability from super-Eddington (slim) accretion disks. We consider three mechanisms that play crucial roles in the observed variability, viz., advective attenuation, photospheric averaging, and photon diffusion filter. With this, above $\mdot \sim$ a few, the fractional rms collapses steeply with $\mdot$. Comparing with JWST monitoring constraints, we find that the non-detection of LRD variability requires $\mdot \gtrsim 30$ for $M_{\rm BH}\sim10^{7}\,M_\odot$ on a 0.5\,yr rest-frame baseline; a Monte Carlo forward model of the TWINKLE non-detections of 18 LRDs sharpens this to $\mdot\gtrsim60$ at 95\% confidence. On current baselines, these non-detections remain formally degenerate with a frozen sub-Eddington disk ($\mdot\lesssim0.1$). Longer monitoring will separate the two regimes as the frozen-disk variability grows with baseline, while the super-Eddington collapse does not. The same framework predicts strongly suppressed X-ray variability, testable with future X-ray observatories.

paper.title: 2D and 3D unified RHD atmospheres and wind models of early B-supergiants including approximate NLTE effects
paper.abstract: B supergiants are evolved massive stars with low surface gravities and lower effective temperatures, with substantial radiation-driven winds. Generally, they have been studied assuming 1D spherical symmetry. We present the first multi-D unified atmosphere and wind models for B supergiants, especially investigating the effects of approximate NLTE ionization and subsurface turbulence on the atmosphere and wind dynamics. We computed multi-D box-in-a-star RHD unified atmosphere and wind simulations of 2D/3D early B supergiant models using a hybrid opacity approach. We calculated line opacities from approximate NLTE populations, including line scattering. We calculated the flux-, energy-, and Planck-mean line opacities separately from our large line database using Sobolev escape probabilities, assuming two-level atoms. The models develop a highly turbulent atmosphere with time-averaged turbulent velocities of ~ 40 - 55 km/s at the photosphere in the 2D simulations, and ~ 25 km/s in 3D. In the cooler B1, B1.5 models, the wind acceleration is more gradual than in the hotter B0 model, leading to a significantly higher maximum wind speed in the B0 model. Further, the approximate NLTE formalism strongly alters the ionization stratification in the wind compared to LTE, modifying the line force. Mass-loss rates obtained in the models are of order 10^-6 - 3 x 10^-6 solar masses per year. Including turbulent pressure in hydrodynamically consistent NLTE CMF steady-state 1D simulations with comparable parameters can produce higher mass-loss rates and lower terminal wind velocities than in corresponding models without turbulent velocity, in overall qualitative agreement with our multi-D simulations. Our calculations suggest that in the lower surface-gravity B supergiants, in addition to modifying the photospheric density scale heights, turbulent pressure also influences global properties of the wind.

paper.title: Separability of coupled gravitational perturbations in Plebański--Demiański spacetimes
paper.abstract: Recently, a major breakthrough in the separability of gravitational perturbations of the Kerr--Newman rotating charged black hole was achieved by Hintz [arxiv:2609.33661], and extended to non-zero cosmological constant Kerr--Newman-(A)dS black holes by Yoshida [arxiv:2610.20500] and Zhao [arxiv:2610.22274]. This method removes the need for the freezing approximation, wherein coupling to the electromagnetic degrees of freedom are ignored, at the price of a coupled set of equations in the gravitational radiative degrees of freedom. The key insight is to transform the coupled system of equations into a chiral form which is amenable to a modified matrix $R$-separation of variables. In this work we extend the construction to the most general type D electro-vacuum solution to the Einstein-Maxwell equations, with aligned matter and cosmological constant. The construction makes use of the conformal properties of the equations and we find a symmetry operator underlying the decoupling of the chiral system.

paper.title: Discovery of a Short-Duration Fast X-ray Transient Associated with a Short Gamma-Ray Burst
paper.abstract: Extragalactic fast X-ray transients (EFXTs) are an emerging population of high-energy transients with diverse physical origins. Only a few observed EFXTs are associated with compact object mergers, and the known events generally display X-ray emission lasting much longer than their associated short gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). Here we report EP260411a, an $\sim8$-s EFXT discovered in archival Einstein Probe Wide-field X-ray Telescope (EP-WXT) observations through a time-targeted search for X-ray counterparts of short GRBs. This fast X-ray transient is temporally coincident with short GRB 260411A, with both the pulse width and peak time showing clear anticorrelations with the characteristic photon energy across the gamma-ray and soft X-ray bands. Joint EP-WXT and Fermi-GBM spectral fitting further shows that the broadband emission can be described by a cutoff power-law model with an additional low-energy spectral break, suggesting a common origin for the single-pulse X-ray and gamma-ray emission. The resulting properties place the event within the Type I GRB region in the $E_{\rm p,z}$-$E_{\rm iso}$ plane, supporting its classification as a compact object merger event. Unlike previously known merger-driven Type I EFXTs with long-lasting X-ray emission, EP260411a reveals that the Type I EFXT population can also extend to the short timescale of a few seconds. Its combination of short duration and hard spectrum occupies a sparsely explored region of the EFXT parameter space, providing a new observational link between short-duration EFXTs and compact object mergers.

paper.title: Cubic Galileon Gravity on Nonlinear Scales with \texttt{Hi-COLA} for LSST Year 1
authors: for the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration
paper.abstract: Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) is in a prime position to test Modified Gravity (MG) with Weak Lensing (WL) and Large Scale Structure (LSS). However, many nonlinear MG emulators in the literature enforce a $Λ$CDM background by design, missing where data suggest the most interesting deviations lie. We present an emulator for the 3D nonlinear matter power spectrum in Cubic Galileon gravity, a Horndeski theory with a single additional MG parameter, $f_φ$, that modifies the background, growth, and lensing. Trained on \texttt{Hi-COLA} simulations with Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), the emulator achieves $\lesssim 2\%$ accuracy for $k \leq 1.2\ h\,\text{Mpc}^{-1}$ at the fiducial cosmology relative to \texttt{Hi-COLA}, and $\lesssim 5\%$ relative to full N-body \texttt{EFT-RAMSES} simulations. Additionally, conservative scale cuts excluding angular bins affected by baryonic physics enable unbiased parameter estimation in LSST Year 1 weak lensing and galaxy clustering ($3\times2$pt) forecasts, even when validated against simulated data based on higher-resolution N-body simulations. This demonstrates that, within a simplified LSST Y1 setup and the adopted scale cuts, \texttt{Hi-COLA}-based emulation is sufficient to develop inference infrastructure with Stage IV precision for Horndeski gravity models previously unmodeled on nonlinear scales.

paper.title: A helium-rich mass-donor in a 3.5-hr low mass X-ray binary
paper.abstract: Binary systems in which a neutron star accretes material from a low-mass stellar companion arise from evolutionary processes that depend sensitively on the progenitor properties. It is usually assumed that the accreted material has approximately solar composition, unless the orbital period is $\lesssim80$ min, indicating an "ultracompact" system with a hydrogen deficient donor. However, few constraints on the donor composition are available. Here we apply a Bayesian model-comparison framework, BEANSP, to a sample of 21 thermonuclear bursts from the accretion-powered millisecond pulsar, IGR J17511-3057, to constrain the fuel composition as well as the system parameters. Our analysis strongly indicates an extremely hydrogen- and CNO-deficient fuel composition, with $X \approx 0.03$ and $Z_\rm{CNO}\approx 4 \times 10^{-4}$, unexpected for this system with its relatively long 3.5 hr orbital period. We explore the possible circumstances under which such an object can evolve, and discuss the implications for its history also in light of the three transient outbursts that have been observed to date. Such analyses are finding an unexpectedly wide range in donor compositions, that may help to explain the remarkable diversity in the burst properties of the known burst sources

paper.title: JWST/NIRISS-SOSS Spectroscopic Variability and Auroral Modelling of Warm Ultracool Dwarf LSR J1835+3259
paper.abstract: Auroral variability in ultracool dwarfs (UCDs) has been proposed as a key source of optical and infrared modulation, yet its physical origin remains poorly understood. We present JWST Near Infrared Imager and Slitless Spectrograph/Single Object Slitless Spectroscopy (NIRISS/SOSS) time-series spectroscopy of the M8.5 UCD LSR J1835+3259. These observations probe the object's wavelength-dependent rotational variability, providing insight into the atmospheric processes underlying its infrared behaviour. Additional GTC/MEGARA optical spectra reveal that its H$α$ emission has declined markedly since earlier epochs, suggesting a reduced activity state during the JWST observations. We detect no emission from H$_3^+$ or absorption by hydronium in the NIRISS spectra. We use principal component analysis to identify two distinct modes of spectral variability: one dominated by FeH modulation near 1 $μ$m and another contributing broadband variability across the H and K bands. We find that no model atmosphere grid provides a reasonable fit to the average NIRISS spectrum. However, a blended model comprising an M-dwarf photosphere and a cooler blackbody component provides an improved fit to the mean spectrum, the broadband spectral energy distribution and the NIRISS broadband variability. By adding perturbations to PICASO model grids, we demonstrate that a combination of atmospheric heating and non-equilibrium chemistry can successfully mimic a blend of unperturbed photosphere and a blackbody, and that the presence of these effects may explain the unusual spectrum and variability of LSR J1835+3259.

paper.title: Properties of near-surface turbulence in hot, massive stars: Statistical signatures from multi-dimensional models of O-type stars
paper.abstract: Variability of massive stars indicates the presence of complex, multi-D physics near the surface. Recent advancements in multi-D radiation-hydrodynamical modelling of massive star atmospheres show strong turbulence triggered by the iron opacity bump. We analyze statistical properties of sub-surface turbulence in multi-D simulations of O-star atmospheres. Particularly, we study potential dependencies of turbulent properties on global stellar parameters. Using 2D O-star models, we studied several statistical properties of the turbulence that develops in these models. We compute autocorrelation functions of density and velocity to study typical eddy length scales. Moreover, we compute kinetic energy power spectra to analyze the energy distribution and compare this to known results from established turbulence theories. We find anisotropy of the turbulent eddies in velocity space. Moreover, this anisotropy increases with classical Eddington factor. This anisotropy disappears in density space where all models show nearly isotropic structures and no dependence on stellar parameters. The kinetic energy power spectra exhibit an inertial range with a cascade exponent that has an average value of -2.57. This exponent does not show any clear dependence on stellar parameters. Importantly, this energy cascade is significantly steeper than those in known turbulence theories such as Kolmogorov turbulence with exponent -5/3 and Burgers turbulence with exponent -2. This additional steepening can potentially be attributed to radiative damping which increases with increasing wavenumber. Sub-surface turbulence in hot, massive stars is anisotropic and radially dominated in velocity space and its energy cascade is steeper than both Kolmogorov turbulence and Burgers turbulence. Although not rigorously proven here, we suggest that this steepening is due to the scale-dependent effect of radiative damping.

paper.title: Magnetic kink instability of jet-wind outflows. I. Static column configuration
paper.abstract: We describe the results of computer simulations investigating the stability of an axisymmetric static equilibrium combining a highly magnetised ($σ=10^3$) central column and a mildly ($σ=0.1$) to weakly ($σ=0.001$) magnetised outer shell with a helical and mostly force-free magnetic field of constant pitch. The measured linear growth rates of the instability are in agreement with the maximum growth rate for a uniform density column with a force-free magnetic field of constant pitch obtained by Appl et al. (2000), being only a little bit higher. At the non-linear phase, the interface separating the central column and the outer shell develops the characteristic corkscrew shape, with the space inside and between the coils of the corkscrew filled by the shell plasma. In high-resolution runs, a secondary instability is seen as well. It has the form of helical protuberances of low-$σ$ plasma intruding inside the corkscrew coils. These appear to be aligned with the local magnetic field lines. We tentatively identify the secondary instability as the magnetic Rayleigh-Taylor instability. Overall, the results indicate that the current-driven kink instability may provide the baryon-loading of AGN jets suggested by the observations.

paper.title: bihalofit-JAX: A Differentiable Code for the Nonlinear Matter Bispectrum and its Projected Statistics
paper.abstract: Theoretical predictions for the nonlinear matter bispectrum and related projected statistics have been historically very expensive to evaluate, leading many analyses to rely on emulators to speed up slow numerical codes. We show in this paper that this need not be the case: improved numerical techniques can be leveraged to directly evaluate predictions for the nonlinear matter bispectrum and projected statistics at speeds preferable for inference. We present bihalofit-JAX, an open-source, fully differentiable code for the nonlinear matter bispectrum based on the BiHalofit fitting formula, which includes numerous related projected statistics such as angular bispectra, skew spectra and aperture statistics. It computes $10000$ triangles of the matter bispectrum in $\sim1$--$2\ \rm{ms}$ per cosmology, one to three orders of magnitude faster than other implementations. It agrees numerically with the original BiHalofit code to better than $0.02\%$ on average over the cosmologies the formula was calibrated on, where the formula itself is accurate to $\sim20\%$ against simulations. It is also efficiently vectorised such that one can compute e.g. $500$ cosmologies in $\sim 2\ \rm{ms}$. This speed-up grows even more in the case of the third-order aperture statistics, which we compute in $\sim 6\ \rm{ms}$ for one cosmology, between $3\times10^3$ and $2.4\times10^4$ times faster than other publicly available codes. The pipeline is fully differentiable, and we demonstrate its performance in a simple inference problem, comparing the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS) to gradient-free inference with the affine-invariant ensemble sampler (emcee).

paper.title: Zeeman-Doppler imaging of V889 Her: Surface spots and magnetic field topology 2017 - 2023
paper.abstract: The surface magnetic field of the young solar analogue V889 Her is studied using Zeeman-Doppler imaging (ZDI). This well-studied star has previously been reported to have an exceptionally high differential rotation and show abrupt changes in the surface magnetic field and spot configuration. Our aim is to study the evolution of the magnetic field topology in V889 Her. This will contribute to understanding dynamo action in young solar-type stars. We also want to constrain the surface differential rotation curve of the target star.Methods. We employ the ZDI method on observations collected with the SOFIN spectropolarimeter mounted at the Nordic Optical Telescope. We test differential rotation parameters previously reported in studies of the star. We observe significant changes in the radial field near the rotational pole throughout the whole span of the observations. Specifically, the polarity of the radial field is reversed around 2021. The large-scale magnetic field also contains a persistent strong azimuthal component at high latitudes. We detect abrupt changes in the spot configuration in June 2018 on the time scale of a week. The observations favour a solar type differential rotation. The different rotation parameters influence the brightness map more than the magnetic field topology. We cannot link the observed changes in the magnetic field topology with the evolution of the long-term spot activity. The abrupt changes observed in 2018 confirm previous reports that the surface magnetic field and spot configuration may undergo rapid evolution on short time scales. This complicates the estimation of the surface differential rotation.

paper.title: A Multiscale Analysis of an Interplanetary Shock from IMAP, SOLAR-1, and the L1 Constellation to Earth
paper.abstract: Collisionless shocks are primary sites of particle acceleration throughout the Universe. Transient, mesoscale structures forming around these shocks influence their energy conversion efficiency, yet remain poorly observed at interplanetary (IP) shocks: spacecraft sample the shock transition briefly, and single-point measurements cannot disentangle temporal evolution from spatial structure. Here, we examine a fast, CME-driven IP shock of 2026 January 19, observed by IMAP, SOLAR-1, Wind, ACE, DSCOVR, and Aditya-L1 at L1 and by ARTEMIS and MMS near Earth, to determine its spatial and temporal structure. At MHD scales, a pre-existing solar wind flux tube is overtaken by the shock as it crosses the L1 fleet. This inflates the apparent magnetic compression ratio far beyond the ideal strong-shock limit of 4, showing that upstream and downstream intervals can sample different plasma and bias single-spacecraft estimates. At kinetic scales, IMAP and SOLAR-1, separated by only $\sim$7 $R_E$ ($\sim$340 ion inertial lengths), sample the same foreshock yet record localized structures that differ measurably; these are the first candidate signatures of large-scale foreshock transients at an IP shock. Further upstream, shocklets appear hundreds of $R_E$ ahead of the shock, consistent with steepening of ambient solar wind waves. Near Earth, the shock-to-flux-tube arrival lag increases to approximately six minutes, corresponding to a nominal sheath extension of $\sim$50 $R_E$, indicating sheath expansion over $\sim$200 $R_E$ of propagation. Together, these results show that the IP shock, its foreshock, and its sheath evolve across multiple scales from L1 to Earth, underscoring the need for multipoint measurements to resolve the underlying processes.

paper.title: Density fluctuations in pseudo-streamer and helmet streamer: Generation, propagation and comparison with Metis observations
paper.abstract: Recent white-light observations from the Metis coronagraph on board Solar Orbiter have shown the presence of propagating density fluctuations with a period of $\sim5$ minutes, particularly in the observationally bright regions of helmet streamers and pseudo-streamers. These density fluctuations have been shown to originate from magnetohydrodynamic wave modes -- slow and fast modes can directly compress the plasma, whereas Alfvén waves generate density fluctuations via a non-linear coupling with the slow and fast modes. In general, in low plasma $β$ regions, slow modes contribute more towards the generation of density fluctuations, whereas in high $β$ regions, there are significant contributions from both slow and fast waves. In this work, we investigate the propagation of (non-linear) Alfvén waves and the associated density fluctuations using a 2.5D axisymmetric global solar wind model that includes two distinct magnetic field topologies -- a helmet streamer and a pseudo-streamer. Key differences in these magnetic configurations give rise to differences in the wave behaviour due to, for example, the presence of a current sheet in the helmet streamer and an X-type null point in the pseudo-streamer, and the structure of the $β= 1$ layer in both magnetic field configurations. This leads to the possible creation of prominent interference patterns along the helmet streamer axis, which do not appear along the pseudo-streamer axis. Unlike in the streamer region, we also find that along the pseudo-streamer axis, the contribution to the density fluctuations is due to the fast waves only, despite being in a low $β$ plasma.

paper.title: Gravitational production of dark QED by the trace anomaly
paper.abstract: We revisit the production of fermionic dark matter $χ$ through the graviton portal, sourced by inflaton annihilation at the end of inflation. Because the production rate is helicity-suppressed, $\propto m_χ^2$, the dark fermion must be very heavy to account for the observed relic abundance, $m_χ\gtrsim 10^{10}$ GeV, with the exact bound set by the reheating temperature $T_{\rm RH}$. Here we examine how interactions within the dark sector could modify this result. As a toy model, we consider dark QED, in which $χ$ couples to a light dark photon. We first show that, as a consequence of classical conformal invariance, bremsstrahlung of a dark photon does not lift the helicity suppression for light fermions. We then show that the trace anomaly of dark QED, which affects the coupling of the graviton to dark photons, can produce light dark fermions via a Dalitz process. This allows to extend the fermionic dark mass range possibly down to $m_χ\sim 10^7$~GeV, depending on $T_{\rm RH}$ and the dark QED coupling. We also determine under which conditions the hidden sector reaches thermal equilibrium and derive a lower bound on the temperature ratio at reheating $(T'/T)_{\rm RH}$ as function of the dark QED coupling and the reheating temperature.

paper.title: Notes on the singularity theorems of general relativity
paper.abstract: The notes begin with an exploration of the local geometry of spacetime and proceed with an investigation of its global causal structure. The results obtained are used to present a proof of the Hawking cosmological and the Penrose black hole singularity theorems. The aim is to give a pedagogical, but still technical, proof of the statements. The notes include a large number of drawings to aid the understanding of the material and many examples to explain key concepts. Some of the mathematical tools utilised in the proof of the singularity theorems are also illustrated. These include an extensive description of the topological and analytic properties of curves and their spaces, of the Arzelá-Ascoli theorem and of the properties of semi-continuous functions. The Hopf-Rinow theorem, which describes the conditions for geodesic completeness in the context of Riemannian manifolds, is also partially demonstrated.

paper.title: Distinguishing cosmologies with topological analysis of 21-cm hydrogen 2D brightness fields at Cosmic Dawn
paper.abstract: The 21-cm hydrogen line brightness field is a potentially valuable source of information about astrophysical parameters during the cosmological Dark Ages and the Epoch of Reionization. However, it can also be a source of observational data for cosmologists seeking to constrain cosmological parameters. While much of the effort has been focused on constraining parameters using information across a broad frequency range, most often with the power spectrum of inhomogeneities, we investigate whether a single frequency channel, corresponding to a single redshift slice, can distinguish between cosmological models. We utilize topological data analysis to evaluate the possibility of such constraints. In particular, we use cubical complexes to perform persistent homology analysis of the 21-cm line brightness field. We generate 21-cm brightness fields of different cosmologies with the 21cmFAST package and then select snapshots at several redshifts corresponding to the Epoch of Reionization. Our goal is to find the redshift that is most suitable for highlighting the diversity between scenarios within a certain range of cosmological parameters. To compare persistent pictures built on simulations of the brightness field, we use Wasserstein distance, computed between any two persistent diagrams. We find that observations of the 21-cm field near $z=10$ have the potential to distinguish between cosmological models with different values of the normalized Hubble parameter $h_0$, the spectral index of scalar matter perturbations $n_s$, the matter density parameter $Ω_m$, and the matter fluctuation amplitude $σ_8$, even in the presence of instrumental thermal noise. We perform the PERMANOVA statistical test on the matrices of Wasserstein distances to confirm this hypothesis for all considered cosmological parameters.

paper.title: A New Galactic Close Binary Supersoft Source Candidate
paper.abstract: The identification of a new galactic Close Binary Supersoft Source (CBSS) candidate, whose main ID is ZTF J043609.49+364057.7, is presented on the basis of the analysis of its optical spectrum, light curve and Spectral Energy Distribution (SED). During a survey designed to find candidates to the aforementioned class independently of X-ray emissions, this object's optical spectrum was found to exhibit the typical emission features expected for a CBSS. The available photometric data show a quasi-sinusoidal modulation, with a period of 5.42 h, compatible with the orbital modulation of the system. Although there is no current identification of X-ray emission from this source, its SED displays a highly absorbed bright FUV component, given the estimated E(B - V) ~ 0.7 mag.

summary.context_outlook: 密近双星超软源（CBSS）是发光超软 X 射线源中由白矮星以约 10⁻⁷ M⊙/yr 吸积富氢物质、表面发生半稳定热核燃烧的一类，自 ROSAT 时代以 CAL 83、CAL 87 为原型被定义 [[Kahabka+ 1997]]、[[van den Heuvel+ 1992]]。银河系中确认为非新星 CBSS 的此前只有 QR And [[Beuermann+ 1995]]，WX Cen、V Sge、V617 Sgr、QU Car 等则被归为光谱相似的「V Sge 型星」 [[Steiner & Diaz 1998]]；由于银盘软 X 射线受星际吸收强烈压制，银河系样本远少于麦哲伦云与 M31 中的探测 [[Greiner+ 2000]]、[[Orio+ 2010]]。人口合成研究却预示银河系仍应存在相当数量、只是被 X 射线选择效应遗漏的系统 [[Rappaport+ 1994]]、[[Chen+ 2015]]、[[Galiullin & Gilfanov 2021]]。本文正沿此思路，改以光学光谱中的 He II/Hβ 比值与 O VI、N V 高电离发射线为判据，筛出 ZTF J043609.49+364057.7：其光谱与 QR And 高度相似，SED 呈现强吸收的明亮 FUV 成分 [[Mazzero+ 2026]]、[[Stecchini+ 2026]]，TESS 给出 5.42 小时轨道周期，而 ROSAT 档案无探测（该源此前还被 ZTF 周期变星目录误判为 W UMa 型接触双星 [[Chen+ 2020]]）。这提示银河系 CBSS 种群可能大部分在 X 射线波段不可见，未来需要 X 射线跟进观测与更大规模光学–红外光谱巡天的交叉筛选，才能厘清这类系统在单简并通道走向 Ia 型超新星中的真实比例。

paper.title: Precise Deep-Learning Reconstruction of Galaxy Cluster Mass Maps and Substructures from Optical Observations
paper.abstract: Accurately mapping the total mass distribution within galaxy clusters, including dark matter, is fundamental to understanding structure formation and constraining cosmological parameters. Conventional mass-mapping techniques rely predominantly on gravitational lensing and often produce smooth mass distributions based on analytical profiles, potentially missing important internal substructures. We introduce a complementary, simulation-based inference approach to reconstruct detailed galaxy cluster mass maps and resolve their internal substructures directly from optical imaging. We trained deep learning models on realistic hydrodynamical simulations of galaxy clusters to infer their mass distributions from optical observations. We subsequently applied this framework to observations of real galaxy clusters obtained with the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) as part of the Cluster Lensing And Supernova survey with Hubble (CLASH) programme. The reconstructed mass maps successfully reproduce the overall shapes and radial mass profiles of the CLASH clusters, showing strong agreement with independent gravitational lensing measurements. Furthermore, the subhalo mass functions derived from the reconstructed maps exhibit power-law behaviour broadly consistent with predictions from numerical simulations. Our results demonstrate that combining optical imaging with deep learning provides a scalable and physically meaningful approach to mapping galaxy cluster mass distributions. This framework opens a new avenue for exploiting upcoming wide-field imaging surveys to systematically investigate dark matter substructures across large cluster samples, complementing traditional gravitational lensing techniques. Moreover, the model is inherently flexible and can incorporate multi-wavelength observations, including X-ray and Sunyaev--Zel'dovich data, to further improve total mass predictions.

paper.title: Probing baryonic feedback using fast radio bursts and galaxy surveys
paper.abstract: The dispersion measure (DM) of fast radio bursts (FRB) provides a noisy measure of the free-electron column density to the burst. With next-generation FRB surveys the number of bursts will drastically increase and measurements of the baryon distribution will be possible on the Mpc scales most relevant to Stage IV weak lensing surveys. Comparing the DM auto-spectrum, DM-shear cross-spectrum and the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect, we argue that the cross-correlation of FRB catalogs with galaxy surveys offers many advantages. Hybrid Effective Field Theory (HEFT), often used in large-scale structure cosmology, is capable of modeling the clustering of electrons jointly with galaxies and matter to small scales. Using HEFT with the Padé model of baryonic feedback, we forecast that next-generation FRB surveys (combined with galaxy samples) will be able to constrain feedback at a level informative for Stage IV weak lensing surveys. In particular we should not be limited by modeling the manner in which galaxies trace the matter field. Rather constraints of the higher-order electron biases and the electron-galaxy cross-stochasticity provide the dominant limitation, and are an obvious target for improvement in order to reach percent-level constraints. The same measurements also provide a valuable means of constraining feedback in hydrodynamic simulations of galaxy formation in a way that is not tied to the modeling of particular galaxy samples.

paper.title: Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space
paper.abstract: Recent observational investigation of cosmological Parity Violation (PV) through the galaxy Four-point Correlation Function (4PCF) has motivated a careful theoretical examination of potential systematic contributions. In this work, we demonstrate that parity-odd contributions to the isotropic 4PCF estimator induced by Redshift Space Distortion (RSD), up to the leading order $\mathcal{H}/k$ of general relativistic corrections, vanish upon averaging over all the Line-of-Sight (LOS). We analyse the perturbative relativistic galaxy number density, combining the biased tracer expansion and the dark matter gravitational dynamics within the framework of Standard Eulerian Perturbation Theory (EPT) to third order in the density perturbation. Building on prior studies of the parity-odd mode of the trispectrum (the Fourier-space counterpart of the 4PCF), we extend existing results in three directions: incorporating the wide-angle effect by adopting a local LOS definition for each galaxy in the 4PCF, accounting for tidal bias in the galaxy population, and generalising the assessment to an arbitrary cosmological background. Expanding the 4PCF in spherical harmonics, we show that angular momentum selection rules, encoded in the Wigner 3-j symbols, enforce that only parity-even contributions survive the integration over all LOS orientations, both in the plane-parallel approximation and in the full wide-angle case. This result is crucial for large-scale statistical analyses using isotropic estimators. It supports interpreting possible PV detections as a signal not due to a systematic RSD artefact. We conclude with a discussion of the caveats of our results and identify potential sources of PV.

paper.title: Does Dark Energy Evolve $\textit{and}$ Cluster?
paper.abstract: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in dynamical dark energy, and naturally raise the question of whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics. We address this question through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark-energy contribution to the expansion and the gravitational responses governing clustering and lensing, complemented by a combined covariance-mode analysis, without imposing model-specific relations between the sectors. Combining CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, and Pantheon+ supernova observations, and subsequently adding large scale structure observations including DES Year 3 $6\times2$pt data and other surveys, we recover a broad maximum in the effective dark-energy density near $z\simeq0.6$--$0.7$. The gravitational responses exhibit suggestive low-redshift enhancements over their GR values, approximately coincident with the background feature. Adding large scale structure information preserves the background feature but favours a mildly reduced lensing response. The combined covariance-mode analysis identifies the combinations of background and gravitational responses most tightly constrained by current observations and quantifies their departures from $Λ$CDM. The leading modes are decisively background dominated, while the gravitational sector remains less precisely constrained. Thus, present data cannot yet determine whether the suggestive low-redshift features in the two sectors share a common physical origin, a question that ongoing Stage-IV surveys will be able to address

paper.title: Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data
paper.abstract: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in non-standard late-time evolution. We investigate whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark energy density, $Ω_{\rm X}(a)$, and the gravitational response functions $μ(a)$ and $Σ(a)$. Combining CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+, and large scale structure observations, including DES Year 3 $6\times2$pt data, we perform reconstructions with and without a theory motivated correlation prior derived from stable Horndeski models. We find a persistent maximum in $Ω_{\rm X}$ at $z\simeq0.5$--$0.7$, corresponding to a crossing of the effective phantom divide. This feature is already present in the CMB+BAO combination and remains robust when modifications to clustering and lensing are allowed. The reconstructed gravitational response exhibits suggestive enhancements in $μ$ and $Σ$ over approximately the same redshift range, although these departures are less significant. Including LSS information instead favours a reduced lensing response, $Σ<1$, while leaving the background feature largely unchanged. An interpretation within Generalized Brans-Dicke theories illustrates how modifications to the effective gravitational coupling and a scalar-mediated fifth force may contribute to these trends. Our results indicate that current departures from $Λ$CDM are most significant in the expansion history, while leaving open the possibility of correlated modifications to gravitational dynamics that future Stage IV surveys can test.
